artigo.texto: A LG anunciou um novo Chiller Centrífugo Refrigerado a Ar (ACC) desenvolvido para atender à demanda de resfriamento de data centers voltados à inteligência artificial. O equipamento combina tecnologias proprietárias da empresa para aumentar a eficiência energética e manter a operação do sistema de refrigeração em ambientes que exigem disponibilidade contínua. O novo chiller possui capacidade de 480 a 600 toneladas de refrigeração (RT) por unidade e pode ser configurado de acordo com as necessidades de diferentes data centers de IA (AIDCs). Entre os principais recursos estão um compressor centrífugo com mancal magnético livre de óleo, tecnologia de free-cooling por refrigerante, sistema de alimentação ininterrupta (UPS) e recuperação da capacidade total de resfriamento em até três minutos após o restabelecimento da energia. Compressor com mancal magnético elimina o uso de óleo O compressor centrífugo utiliza um sistema de mancal magnético para suspender o eixo rotativo sem contato físico. Com isso, o projeto dispensa óleo lubrificante e reduz perdas associadas ao atrito mecânico. A tecnologia faz parte do conjunto de soluções proprietárias Core Tech da LG, que também inclui componentes como motores, inversores e outros elementos utilizados nos sistemas de refrigeração. A empresa afirma que desenvolve e fabrica internamente esses componentes antes de integrá-los aos sistemas completos. Segundo a LG, essa estratégia também busca melhorar a disponibilidade de peças e reduzir o tempo necessário para manutenção. Free-cooling por refrigerante reduz consumo de energia Outro recurso utilizado pelo novo chiller é o free-cooling por refrigerante. A tecnologia utiliza o ar externo quando as condições climáticas permitem reduzir a carga sobre o compressor. A solução se diferencia de sistemas convencionais de free-cooling hidrônico porque o refrigerante circula diretamente, sem a utilização de um trocador de calor intermediário. O sistema também não exige glicol, segundo a LG. Com base em uma simulação interna da empresa, o free-cooling por refrigerante apresentou consumo anual aproximadamente 30% menor do que uma solução de free-cooling hidrônico. A comparação foi feita pela LG considerando uma unidade de 1.750 kW operando com 100% da capacidade de resfriamento nas condições climáticas da região metropolitana de Seul. Nesse cenário, a empresa calculou consumo de 1.479.655 kWh para o free-cooling hidrônico e 1.044.824 kWh para o sistema por refrigerante. A LG ressalta que o consumo real pode variar de acordo com as condições de instalação e operação. O chiller também utiliza a tecnologia SCF (fluxo contracorrente em série), desenvolvida pela empresa para distribuir a carga de resfriamento entre os compressores. Sistema pode recuperar capacidade em até três minutos A continuidade do resfriamento é outro ponto destacado pela LG. O chiller possui sensores integrados ao sistema de mancal magnético para monitorar a posição do eixo rotativo e permitir um controle mais preciso. Recursos de machine learning também são utilizados para adaptar o funcionamento do equipamento aos padrões de operação e auxiliar na redução de instabilidades. Em caso de interrupção de energia, um UPS integrado fornece energia de emergência. A solução permite que o eixo do compressor seja parado de maneira controlada, reduzindo o risco de danos ao mancal. Depois que a energia é restabelecida, o sistema conta com uma função de recuperação rápida que pode retornar à capacidade total de resfriamento em até três minutos. O resultado, entretanto, pode variar conforme as condições de teste. LG oferece software para gerenciamento do resfriamento O novo chiller também pode ser integrado ao Data Center Cooling Management (DCCM), plataforma da LG voltada ao monitoramento e controle de infraestruturas de resfriamento. O sistema pode trabalhar com diferentes equipamentos, incluindo Coolant Distribution Units (CDUs), Computer Room Air Handlers (CRAHs) e chillers centrífugos refrigerados a ar. Entre os recursos estão detecção antecipada de anomalias, diagnósticos baseados em sensores virtuais e manutenção preditiva. A plataforma também permite otimização em tempo real de acordo com as cargas de trabalho de TI. A proposta é centralizar informações dos equipamentos de refrigeração para auxiliar no gerenciamento de instalações mais complexas. Solução modular busca facilitar expansão de data centers Além do novo chiller, a LG apresentará uma solução modular de resfriamento hidrônico durante a Data Centre World Asia 2026, que acontece entre 29 e 30 de setembro no Marina Bay Sands, em Singapura. A solução reúne componentes como bombas de água gelada e um tanque-pulmão para armazenamento térmico de energia (TES) em um módulo padronizado. A empresa afirma que a pré-fabricação e a montagem em fábrica podem simplificar a instalação no local. O projeto modular também permite ampliar a infraestrutura conforme o data center aumenta sua capacidade. A abordagem é particularmente voltada para instalações de inteligência artificial, que podem exigir expansão da capacidade computacional e, consequentemente, da infraestrutura necessária para remover o calor gerado pelos equipamentos. Chillers da LG possuem certificações internacionais Segundo a empresa, os chillers e as instalações de teste da LG seguem padrões do Air-Conditioning, Heating, and Refrigeration Institute (AHRI). Os chillers refrigerados a ar da companhia também receberam o AHRI Performance Award por nove anos consecutivos. A linha atende ainda a requisitos relacionados a diferentes mercados, incluindo normas da ASME para vasos de pressão, certificação ETL para segurança elétrica na América do Norte e requisitos CE de segurança, saúde e meio ambiente na Europa. Com o novo chiller centrífugo refrigerado a ar, a LG amplia seu portfólio de soluções destinadas à infraestrutura térmica de data centers de IA, combinando sistemas de refrigeração, gerenciamento e arquitetura modular para instalações que precisa

artigo.texto: Data centers may be the sleeper issue of the midterm elections. Fox News reported that Senate candidates are confronting growing voter anger over the electricity costs, water consumption, and sprawling developments associated with artificial intelligence. One recent Gallup survey found that 70 percent of Americans oppose the construction of new AI data centers in their own communities. Politicians are paying attention. Some are calling for moratoriums. Others are targeting tax incentives or demanding that projects generate their own power. The political temptation is obvious: When voters are worried about higher utility bills and rapid changes in their communities, blaming large technology companies is easier than explaining a complicated energy and infrastructure problem. ANXIETY GROWS OVER EMERGING ELECTION ISSUE, BUT GOP SAYS WASHINGTON ISN'T THE ANSWER The concerns are real. They should not be dismissed by industry, and they cannot be ignored by elected officials. No family should be forced to subsidize the grid upgrades required by one of the world’s wealthiest companies. Communities deserve honest answers about water use, noise, land, electricity demand, tax incentives, and who will pay for new infrastructure. But, legitimate concerns are quickly hardening into something far more dangerous: a political campaign against the physical infrastructure of American artificial intelligence. If that happens, we will repeat one of the most damaging patterns in modern American history. For decades, the United States surrendered factories, critical supply chains, mineral production, and industrial capacity to foreign competitors. Communities lost jobs, our national security became dependent on adversaries, and Washington eventually spent billions trying to rebuild industries that should never have left. THE AI REVOLUTION COULD BECOME A NATIONAL SECURITY DISASTER IF WE AREN'T CAREFUL We cannot make the same mistake with AI. Artificial intelligence does not exist somewhere in the cloud. It requires chips, servers, power plants, transmission lines, cooling systems, construction workers, electricians, pipefitters, engineers, and data centers. These facilities are not incidental to the AI economy. They are the factories of the next industrial age. AMERICA RUNS ON DATA. IF WE DON’T BUILD THE INFRASTRUCTURE, CHINA WILL China understands this. Beijing is not debating whether it should possess the energy and computing infrastructure necessary to dominate artificial intelligence. It is building. The International Energy Agency projects that data-center electricity consumption will increase substantially in both China and the United States through 2030. If America decides that data centers are too politically difficult to construct, the demand for AI will not disappear. The investment, jobs, technical expertise, and strategic advantage will simply move elsewhere. That would be a profound failure of American competitiveness. It would also create a serious political problem for Democrats. Data-center construction has become an important source of work for the building trades. The Associated Press recently reported that data centers account for at least 40 percent of the work hours performed by members of the Columbus-Central Ohio Building and Construction Trades Council and at least 50 percent for the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers Local 26 in the Washington metropolitan area. WELDER TURNED LAWMAKER SEES A ‘NUCLEAR BOMB FOR WORK’ — AND A CHANCE TO HELP BLUE COLLAR AMERICANS Those are not theoretical jobs promised years from now. They are jobs for electricians, laborers, operating engineers, pipefitters, and other skilled workers today. Democrats cannot claim to represent organized labor while allowing progressive activists to shut down the projects employing union members. Republicans should resist a similar temptation. Conservatives have spent years arguing for reshoring, energy dominance, permitting reform, American manufacturing, and competition with China. Those commitments mean very little if they disappear when building the next American industry becomes locally controversial. The answer is not to wave every project through without conditions. It is to build responsibly and communicate honestly. Data-center developers should be expected to explain what they are building, how much electricity and water it will require, how they will protect residential ratepayers, and what the surrounding community will receive in return. Utilities and regulators should ensure that large customers pay the costs created by their demand. Projects should pursue closed-loop cooling, on-site generation, long-term power agreements, and other options that reduce pressure on local systems. TO BEAT CHINA IN AI, AMERICA MUST WORK WITH COMMUNITIES — NOT AROUND THEM Most importantly, America needs more energy. Data centers are exposing a problem that existed before the AI boom. Electricity demand from data centers has tripled over the past decade and could double or triple again by 2028. Electricity demand is rising after years of stagnant generation, premature plant retirements, congested transmission systems, and permitting processes that make major infrastructure nearly impossible to build on time. Stopping data centers will not modernize the grid. Building more reliable generation, accelerating transmission, preserving existing nuclear capacity, expanding natural gas infrastructure, and deploying advanced nuclear power will. Industry also needs to recognize that silence is no longer a strategy. As Sen. Jon Husted told Fox News, data-center companies have not done a good enough job explaining why they should be allowed to develop in communities. He is right. Americans hear about enormous power consumption, water use, and tax incentives. They need to hear, in plain language, what data centers make possible, which jobs they create, how they support national security, and why domestic computing capacity matters i

artigo.texto: Data centers are powering your chat ramblings — and the growth in the American construction industry. AI buildouts are set to become the largest capital expenditure project in US history, per a Brookings Institution analysis, outpacing spending on highways and railroads as a share of GDP. That massive spending and construction boom needs workers to — literally — prop it up. And blue-collar employment for data centers is booming, with the number of nonresidential specialty trade contractors — workers like electricians in non-residential buildings, which includes data centers— growing by 86,000 in the past year. "I think it's fair to say that a very large portion of construction labor demand right now is being driven by increasing data center construction activity," said Zach Fritz, an economist at Associated Builders and Contractors. The American Institute of Architects found, based on multiple forecasts of nonresidential construction, that data center construction spending is set to climb more than other kinds and account for about 8% of nonresidential building spending by 2027. But the sustainability of that jobs boom could be precarious. Construction spending on the whole has fallen 3.8% year-over-year as of July, according to the Census Bureau, and KPMG finds that data centers are a "structural growth driver" for spending. Year-over-year spending on data centers has grown by just over 57%, a sharp contrast to both residential and non-residential private spending growth since early 2025. For now, the data center boom is good news for construction workers and larger industry spending. Guy Berger, a senior fellow at the research organization Burning Glass Institute, said one concern is if the data center boom cycle ends up being shorter than anticipated: "And all of a sudden, we trained a lot of electricians, people like that, to do stuff that is no longer needed," Berger said. Data center workers are in demand Job postings on Indeed for data center-related roles have skyrocketed, up almost 130% from about two years ago, while overall postings are down compared with the same period. About half of the data-center demand this year came from the IT infrastructure, operations, and support occupational group and the installation and maintenance occupational group. A job-posting analysis from Lightcast, a job market intelligence company, showed a rise in demand for some data-center-related jobs. Based on growth in average monthly job postings from January to August 2022 and the same period this year, postings for electrical engineers within the utilities sector have increased 34%, and 22% for project management specialists. Within commercial and institutional building construction, there's been a rise in demand for construction managers, project management specialists, cost estimators, and civil engineers. And so, in the short term, the data center boom will likely remain a workhouse for the construction industry. What's more unclear is the longer-term prognosis, especially since AI infrastructure is still reliant on a slice of hardcore spenders to keep it afloat. "The next few years, it's stable. It's going to keep growing. We're going to keep building data centers," Fritz said. But rising community opposition could eventually limit the rate of growth, he said, or technological advancements might require smaller footprints. "There's all kinds of things that could happen here," he said. "They're not going to happen anytime soon." It's unclear how permanent data center jobs will ultimately be, especially after data center construction, but listings on Indeed at least suggest firms are advertising them as long-term. Aubrey Woessner, an economist at Indeed Hiring Lab, said only about two in every 1,000 data center postings are temporary. "'Permanent' is a label the employer chooses, and there's reason to think it may overstate how durable these roles really are: Local incentive agreements often require a project to create a set number of permanent positions, which gives employers a reason to post that way regardless of how long a given build-out job actually lasts," Woessner said. Are you in a data center-related job? Reach out to these reporters to share at mhoff@businessinsider.com and jkaplan@businessinsider.com.

artigo.texto: ROME, Sept 29 (Reuters) - Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and her Czech counterpart Andrej Babiš will agree joint proposals to curb energy costs and overhaul the European Union's carbon market, officials from Rome said ahead of their meeting on Tuesday. The two leaders aim to present the reform package at the October 15-16 EU summit, the Italian officials said. Meloni and Babiš are focusing on easing European Union rules that could trigger energy supply disruptions while also reforming the EU Emissions Trading System (ETS), a regulation forcing power plants and industries to buy CO2 permits when they pollute. As part of the package, Rome and Prague are calling on the EU to temporarily suspend a regulation on methane which, according to the officials, could make it more difficult to rely on alternative gas suppliers from January, potentially increasing energy costs and threatening security of supply. The two governments also want the EU to postpone ETS2 regulation, currently scheduled to come into force in 2028, arguing it could further increase energy costs in some sectors including road transport and housing. (Reporting by Giuseppe Fonte; Editing by Alvise Armellini and Kirsten Donovan)

Gotion High-tech (SZSE: 002074) and Volkswagen Group plan to jointly invest about €3.22 billion ($3.67 billion) in battery and materials production projects in Europe and North Africa, deepening supply chain cooperation to serve Volkswagen's European market. The companies plan to establish 3 joint ventures through their subsidiaries in Spain, Slovakia and Morocco, Gotion said in a stock exchange filing on Monday. Gotion plans to invest about €1.6 billion in total, while Volkswagen's PowerCo plans to contribute about €1.62 billion, with funding to be provided in stages. The largest project, in Valencia, Spain, calls for an investment of about €2.26 billion to build annual lithium-ion battery production capacity of 29.1 GWh. Gotion plans to acquire a 49% stake in the existing PowerCo Spain through a capital increase. PowerCo will retain control with a 51% stake after the transaction. The project in Šurany, Slovakia, involves a planned investment of about €480 million for annual lithium-ion battery production capacity of 8.4 GWh. Gotion will hold 51% and PowerCo 49%. Cells produced by the 2 European projects will prioritize Volkswagen's demand in Europe. Specific purchase volumes and supply assurance arrangements remain subject to subsequent definitive agreements. The companies also plan to invest about €480 million in Kenitra, Morocco, to build a lithium iron phosphate cathode materials project with annual capacity of 100,000 metric tons, prioritizing supplies to the 2 battery joint ventures. Gotion will also control the Moroccan joint venture with a 51% stake, while PowerCo will hold the remaining 49%. The construction scope specified in the filing for all 3 projects excludes land and factory buildings. Each project is expected to take no more than 5 years to build, subject to actual construction progress. The cooperation will further strengthen the companies' equity and business ties. Volkswagen (China) Investment Co held a 24.28% stake in Gotion as of September 20, making it the battery maker's largest shareholder. Gotion said it will participate in the development of Volkswagen's key European cell production base, while PowerCo will take stakes in Gotion's battery and materials projects in Europe and Africa to jointly build a localized battery supply network for Europe. Gotion's board approved the proposal on September 28, but the companies have yet to sign the investment agreement. The transaction still requires shareholder approval and government clearances in China and overseas. The projects will increase capital expenditure in the near term, Gotion said, adding that financing, approvals and market changes could affect construction progress and expected returns. The investment plan comes as Gotion gains share in the global battery market. Its global EV battery installations totaled 34.0 GWh in the first 7 months of 2026, up 44.2% from a year earlier, according to South Korean market research firm SNE Research. Gotion High-tech ranked fifth globally during the period, with its market share rising to 4.7% from 3.9% a year earlier. ($1 = €0.8783)

artigo.texto: Conhecida por ser a fábrica de bilionários, a empresa WEG anunciou que vai investir US$ 165 milhões, aproximadamente R$ 840 milhões, para expandir sua capacidade de produção de geradores na América do Norte. O projeto será realizado em duas fases e tem como objetivo atender à crescente demanda por soluções de geração de energia para aplicações críticas nos EUA, especialmente impulsionada pela expansão dos data centers. A iniciativa representa mais um passo na estratégia de crescimento dos negócios incorporados à companhia por meio da aquisição da Marathon. A WEG, que tem sede e nasceu em Jaraguá do Sul, no Norte de SC, tem operações em diversas partes do mundo e vai continuar expandindo. A primeira fase do projeto anunciado para a América do Norte contempla investimentos de 24 milhões de dólares para aquisição e adequação de um prédio industrial localizado ao lado do atual Parque Industrial de Quma I, em Atotonilco de Tula, no México. A unidade será destinada à montagem de geradores e contribuirá para a expansão da capacidade produtiva da companhia, com início das operações previsto para o segundo trimestre de 2027. Na segunda fase, em local ainda a ser definido na América do Norte, a WEG investirá 141 milhões dólares na construção de duas novas instalações industriais. O projeto prevê a implantação de uma estrutura produtiva verticalizada que abrangerá processos estratégicos como fabricação de lâminas, bobinas de baixa e média tensão, eixos e carcaças, aumentando a eficiência operacional e a competitividade da operação. Ao fim da segunda fase, prevista para ser concluída em 2030, a companhia terá capacidade global de fabricar cerca de 50 geradores por dia em suas fábricas no México, EUA, Brasil e China, frente a atual capacidade de 10 geradores por dia. “Este investimento representa mais um passo importante na consolidação da nossa estratégia para o negócio de geradores na América do Norte. Além de ampliar nossa capacidade de produção, o projeto fortalece a integração das operações incorporadas com a Marathon e nos prepara para acompanhar a evolução de mercados que demandam infraestrutura crítica cada vez mais robusta, como o de data centers”, afirma João Paulo Gualberto da Silva, vice‑presidente da Unidade de Energia da WEG.

artigo.texto: O candidato ao Governo do Rio Grande do Norte Robério Paulino (PSOL) afirmou que apoiará Cadu de Lula (PT) caso o petista dispute o segundo turno contra Allyson Bezerra (União). A declaração foi feita durante sabatina promovida pelo Grupo Dial Natal, a seis dias do primeiro turno, marcado para 4 de outubro. Questionado se Cadu seria seu candidato numa segunda etapa do pleito, Robério respondeu: “Sem dúvida. Se o Cadu for para o segundo turno, o Psol vai apoiar o Cadu contra o Allyson, indiscutivelmente“. O apoio veio acompanhado de ressalvas. Robério descreveu Cadu como “um homem da área fiscal” e “uma pessoa de esquerda há pouco tempo“. “Respeito muito o Cadu, mas a visão dele é uma visão muito gerencialista“, afirmou, acrescentando que o petista tem “menos visão social” do que a dele. Data centers Na mesma sabatina, o candidato do PSOL disse não se opor à instalação de data centers no estado, desde que gerem empregos. “Eu, a priori, não estou contra“, afirmou. Robério, porém, apontou o impacto ambiental desses empreendimentos, em especial o alto consumo de água, e defendeu que cada projeto seja avaliado considerando os efeitos ambientais e o número de empregos gerados. “Não vejo que essa é a grande saída para o Estado“, disse sem detalhar qual seria a alternativa. A posição contrasta com a de Cadu, que em sabatina na mesma série, citou a resolução do Conselho Estadual de Meio Ambiente (Conema) que abriu caminho para data centers no RN. O petista apresentou os empreendimentos como parte de sua estratégia para agregar valor à energia renovável produzida no estado.

artigo.texto: BYD says its new solid-state EV battery tech is nearly ready for the open road The Chinese company is one of several car makers expected to adopt solid-state batteries in the next few years. Switching from lithium-ion to solid-state batteries promises to extend the range and charging speeds of electric vehicles, and Chinese car maker BYD believes it's in a "leading position" to commercialize the technology. BYD's Executive Vice President Stella Li shared the claim in a recent interview with Carwow's Spanish outlet, alongside the news that BYD would release its first car with a solid-state battery in 2027. "Talking about solid-state batteries, BYD is in the leading position," Li said. "We're in the leading position for commercialization and technology. So to prove that, next year, we have one model that will be the first one with that technology." Li's comments further confirm plans shared by Sun Huajun, the Chief Technology Officer of BYD's battery subsidiary FinDreams, at a battery conference in February 2025. At the time, Sun said BYD would offer its first demonstration and installation of solid-state batteries in 2027 before the technology enters mass production around 2030, CarNewsChina reports. While that means people will be able to buy cars with the company's sulfide solid-state batteries, that doesn't mean its traditional lithium batteries will be phased out, BYD Chief Scientist Lian Yubo shared at the same conference. "Solid-state batteries will be mainly used in high-end models, empowering each other with lithium iron phosphate batteries, and used in vehicles of different levels," Lian said. In comparison to lithium-ion batteries, which move ions between positive and negative terminals through a liquid solution of dissolved lithium salts, solid-state batteries replace the liquid with solid electrolytes made from oxides, polymers or sulfides (the kind BYD is developing). Solid electrolytes give solid-state batteries higher energy density, which opens up the possibility of smaller, lighter batteries and a longer range on a single charge. Solid-state batteries are also theoretically safer because they're far less prone to catching fire and they're able to operate at extreme temperatures, an issue current lithium-ion batteries struggle with. The problem with using the battery technology as it exists now is cost, which is why BYD suggests you'll see its solid-state batteries on more expensive models first, like possibly a future version of its Denza Z. The company is one of several car makers planning to ship a vehicle with solid-state batteries in the next few years. For example, Toyota committed to offering cars with solid-state batteries by 2027 or 2028; Mercedes-Benz began testing a solid-state EQS model and shared that it would ship the technology before the end of the decade; and Stellantis began road testing a solid-state Dodge Charger in 2026. Earlier this year, Honda struck up a new partnership with QuantumScape to develop solid-state batteries it hopes will help it reach carbon neutrality by 2050. The potential for solid-state battery technology is exciting, but most car makers are only in the first leg of the race.

artigo.texto: Weg investirá R$ 840 milhões para ampliar capacidade de produção na América do Norte com avanço de data centers Multinacional brasileira informou em comunicado que investimento será feito primeiro no México; duas novas unidades serão construídas na região Atualizado A multinacional brasileira Weg, fabricante de motores elétricos e equipamentos eletroeletrônicos, anunciou nesta segunda-feira um plano de investimento de US$ 165 milhões, aproximadamente R$ 840 milhões, para expandir sua produção de geradores na América do Norte. A Weg conta com três unidades industriais nos Estados Unidos focadas em equipamentos elétricos, tintas ou suporte produtivo. No México, a empresa tem quatro unidades industriais, com destaque para a operação em Atotonilco de Tula (Parque Quma) e a unidade em Monterrey, voltada para motores, geradores e pesquisa e desenvolvimento. O investimento tem como objetivo atender o aumento da demanda por soluções de geração de energia impulsionada pela expansão dos data centers. A iniciativa representa mais um passo na estratégia de crescimento dos negócios incorporados à companhia por meio da aquisição da Marathon. Em 2023, a Weg adquiriu os negócios de motores elétricos industriais e geradores da americana Regal Rexnord Corporation, incluindo a tradicional marca Marathon. O valor do negócio, à época, foi de cerca de US$ 400 milhões. O novo investimento na região será realizado em duas fases. A primeira contempla US$ 24 milhões para aquisição e adequação de um prédio industrial localizado ao lado do atual Parque Industrial de Quma I. A unidade será destinada à montagem de geradores e tem início das operações previsto para o segundo trimestre de 2027. Na segunda fase, em local ainda a ser definido na América do Norte, a WEG investirá US$ 141 milhões na construção de duas novas instalações industriais. O projeto prevê a implantação de uma estrutura produtiva verticalizada que abrangerá processos estratégicos como fabricação de lâminas, bobinas de baixa e média tensão, eixos e carcaças, aumentando a eficiência operacional e a competitividade da operação. De dez para cinquenta Ao fim da segunda fase, prevista para ser concluída em 2030, a companhia terá capacidade global de fabricar cerca de cinquenta geradores por dia em suas fábricas no México, EUA, Brasil e China, frente a atual capacidade de dez geradores por dia. "Este investimento representa mais um passo importante na consolidação da nossa estratégia para o negócio de geradores na América do Norte. Além de ampliar nossa capacidade de produção, o projeto fortalece a integração das operações incorporadas com a Marathon e nos prepara para acompanhar a evolução de mercados que demandam infraestrutura crítica cada vez mais robusta, como o de data centers", afirmou em nota João Paulo Gualberto da Silva, vice‑presidente da unidade de Energia da WEG. A WEG estima que as atuais tarifas dos Estados Unidos devem pressionar sua margem consolidada caso permaneçam em vigor, mas avalia que sua presença global e a diversificação da produção podem ajudar a reduzir os impactos das medidas comerciais, segundo a agência Bloomberg. Atualmente, 21% da produção no Brasil é destinada aos Estados Unidos, percentual inferior ao registrado em 2024, quando cerca de um terço da produção brasileira era exportada ao mercado americano. O México passou a ser o principal centro de produção da companhia para atender os EUA, com 41% da produção das operações mexicanas destinada ao país.

artigo.texto: Formas de reduzir as emissões e avançar rumo a um mercado de carbono em Phu Tho. TPO - À medida que as exigências de carbono se tornam cada vez mais interligadas com a produção, as cadeias de suprimentos e as exportações, a província de Phu Tho está intensificando os esforços para orientar as empresas no inventário de gases de efeito estufa, no desenvolvimento de planos de redução de emissões e na preparação para o mercado de carbono. Um repórter do jornal Tien Phong entrevistou o Sr. Nguyen Van Linh, chefe do Subdepartamento de Meio Ambiente e Mudanças Climáticas do Departamento Provincial de Agricultura e Meio Ambiente de Phu Tho, sobre este assunto. PV: Senhor, qual é o estado atual dos inventários de gases de efeito estufa em instalações e empresas na província de Phu Tho ? Senhor Nguyen Van Linh: De acordo com a Decisão nº 42/2026/QD-TTg, de 10 de agosto de 2026, a província de Phu Tho possui 177 estabelecimentos na lista que devem realizar o inventário de gases de efeito estufa, incluindo 82 estabelecimentos no setor de Indústria e Comércio, 93 estabelecimentos no setor de construção, 1 estabelecimento de transporte e 1 estabelecimento ambiental. De acordo com os resultados da avaliação de 2025, 84 instalações concluíram o inventário, representando 75,68% das instalações sujeitas à pesquisa; destas, 34 instalações concluíram o inventário e possuíam planos de redução de emissões, atingindo 30,63%. Esta é uma área relativamente nova para muitas empresas, portanto, aumentar a frequência de testes de emissões e desenvolver planos de redução de emissões são tarefas que precisam ser mais incentivadas no próximo período. PV: Com base na experiência de implementação, quais são os maiores desafios que as empresas enfrentam atualmente? Sr. Nguyen Van Linh: Uma dificuldade comum é que muitas empresas não compreendem totalmente suas responsabilidades ou os métodos para inventariar gases de efeito estufa. Coletar dados operacionais, identificar fontes de emissão e preparar relatórios exige conhecimento especializado, e nem todas as empresas têm o pessoal necessário para atender a esses requisitos. Você também pode gostar Portanto, para o relatório de inventário de gases de efeito estufa em nível de instalação de 2024, muitas empresas precisam contratar consultorias especializadas para realizar o processo com base nos dados fornecidos por elas mesmas. Essa é também uma das questões sobre as quais o órgão regulador precisa continuar orientando as empresas para garantir que o processo seja implementado de forma correta e eficiente. PV: De que forma a província de Phu Tho está apoiando as empresas no processo de inventário e redução de emissões? Sr. Nguyen Van Linh: No período anterior, o Comitê Popular Provincial e o Departamento de Agricultura e Meio Ambiente emitiram diversos documentos orientadores e incentivaram as empresas a implementar regulamentações sobre inventário, redução da emissão de gases de efeito estufa e adaptação às mudanças climáticas. A província também publicou o Plano nº 866/KH-UBND, datado de 28 de fevereiro de 2025, sobre a implementação de medidas para reduzir as emissões de gases de efeito estufa, juntamente com muitos planos relacionados à redução de emissões na produção agrícola, à separação de resíduos na fonte e à adaptação às mudanças climáticas. O Departamento também coordena e envia funcionários e empresas para participar de cursos de capacitação sobre inventário de gases de efeito estufa, avaliação de danos climáticos, economia circular, compras públicas sustentáveis e produção e consumo sustentáveis. Quando as empresas precisam mudar de tecnologia, usar energia de forma eficiente ou adotar a produção sustentável, o Departamento as orienta nos procedimentos de acordo com as normas e as apoia na conexão com fontes de financiamento preferenciais do Fundo Provincial de Proteção Ambiental, caso tenham necessidade e atendam aos critérios de elegibilidade. PV: Que preparativos as empresas precisam fazer tendo em vista os requisitos de redução de emissões e a formação de um mercado de carbono, senhor? Você também pode gostar Sr. Nguyen Van Linh: As empresas precisam ser proativas desde o início, principalmente compreendendo as regulamentações, coletando dados completos e realizando inventários de gases de efeito estufa. A partir daí, elas podem identificar as principais fontes de emissão e desenvolver planos adequados de redução de emissões. Além disso, as empresas precisam se concentrar na conservação de energia, na inovação tecnológica, no uso eficiente de matérias-primas e na transição gradual para a produção sustentável. Este será um processo de longo prazo, que não só atenderá aos requisitos de gestão ambiental, mas também ajudará as empresas a se adaptarem às demandas de carbono cada vez mais rigorosas na cadeia de suprimentos e nos mercados de exportação. Do ponto de vista administrativo, a província continuará a divulgar e orientar as regulamentações sobre créditos de carbono e o mercado de carbono, além de orientar as empresas na execução dos procedimentos relacionados. Atualmente, o setor de mudanças climáticas conta com 7 procedimentos administrativos sob a autoridade do Presidente do Comitê Popular Provincial.

artigo.texto: da Agência iNFRA Entidades do setor de gás natural e geração termelétrica defendem a inclusão do gás natural entre as fontes de energia elegíveis ao Redata (Regime Especial de Tributação para Serviços de Data Centers) e manifestam preocupação com a possibilidade de a regulamentação do programa excluir a fonte. A Abraget (Associação Brasileira de Geradoras Termelétricas) e a Abegás (Associação Brasileira das Empresas Distribuidoras de Gás Canalizado) argumentam que o gás pode complementar as fontes renováveis e contribuir para o fornecimento contínuo de energia aos empreendimentos. A Abraget afirma que a eventual exclusão do gás natural pode aumentar os custos do sistema elétrico e estima um impacto de aproximadamente R$ 7 bilhões na conta de luz dos consumidores. Segundo a entidade, além da necessidade de recorrer ao gás e a outras fontes nos períodos de menor geração renovável, a expansão de fontes intermitentes não garantiria, sozinha, o fornecimento firme exigido pelos data centers. “Quem pagará a conta será o consumidor brasileiro”, afirma a associação. A entidade também argumenta que a concentração da geração renovável no Nordeste pode exigir investimentos adicionais em transmissão para atender data centers instalados no Sul e no Sudeste, com possibilidade de repasse dos custos aos consumidores. Para a Abraget, o gás natural oferece geração firme e pode contribuir para a segurança e a viabilidade desses projetos. A Abegás também defende a presença do gás no Redata e sustenta que a fonte deve ser utilizada de forma complementar às renováveis. A associação afirma que a geração a gás pode permitir a implantação descentralizada dos data centers e reduzir a necessidade de novos investimentos em linhas de transmissão. “Defender a neutralidade tecnológica é permitir que esses projetos avancem sem sobrecarregar o sistema de transmissão nem encarecer a conta de energia para os demais consumidores”, afirmou o diretor-executivo da Abegás, Marcelo Mendonça. As duas entidades alertam ainda para o risco de insegurança jurídica caso a regulamentação, na avaliação delas, ultrapasse os limites definidos pelo Congresso Nacional. A Abraget afirma que isso pode provocar questionamentos legislativos e afetar investimentos. A Abegás acrescenta que medidas que excedam o escopo da lei aprovada podem levar à apresentação de PDLs (Projetos de Decreto Legislativo), o que, segundo a associação, poderia dificultar a implementação do regime.

artigo.texto: After completing its first 100 back-to-back charge-discharge cycles without faults or degradation, Qnetic has moved its 200-kilowatt-hour Pulsar energy storage prototype into low-speed testing. It's another sign the company believes flywheel storage can become a practical alternative to lithium-ion batteries. If the system keeps performing as expected, it could help address one of the biggest challenges tied to renewable energy: storing electricity cheaply, efficiently, and for long periods. Here's what to know According to Interesting Engineering, engineers are using this phase to verify how Pulsar's control and safety systems perform before spinning the machine at higher rotational speeds. Before reaching this stage, the prototype completed mechanical assembly in June and underwent structural and component tests meant to reduce technical risk ahead of full-speed operation. Instead of storing energy through chemical reactions, Qnetic's system holds it as motion. Solar or wind facilities generate electricity to accelerate a heavy rotor inside a frictionless vacuum chamber, and when demand increases, the system can convert that rotational energy back into power for the grid. Renewable generation is not constant. Solar panels stop producing at night, and wind output can rise or fall throughout the day, so storage helps make clean electricity available when people need it. Qnetic's motor surpassed 11,000 revolutions per minute and delivered 130 kilowatts of output at 97.3% efficiency, helping validate the system's power-conversion architecture. More background Interest in flywheel storage comes in part from the drawbacks of lithium-ion batteries. Although lithium-ion systems are widely used and can hold large amounts of energy, they are often expensive and tend to degrade as charge cycles accumulate. Because a flywheel stores energy mechanically rather than chemically, its core storage component does not undergo the same kind of wear as battery cells, which could allow it to operate for longer. For utilities and grid operators adding more renewable energy, that could be significant. A storage system that is both durable and efficient could support greater use of wind and solar while helping maintain grid stability without raising costs. What's being done? Rather than pushing Pulsar straight to full operating conditions, Qnetic is validating the system in stages. Michael Pratt, CEO of Qnetic, said the company is increasing operating demands step by step so engineers can confirm the data and solve problems before advancing further. Results from Pulsar testing are also being shared with the Electric Power Research Institute as part of the Readiness Informed by Shared Knowhow, Evaluation, and Data, or deRISKED, program. That kind of outside review could help utilities and customers assess the technology using measured performance rather than hype. If Qnetic's approach continues to hold up through higher-speed testing, it could strengthen the case for flywheels as a serious contender in grid storage. That would not replace lithium-ion batteries overnight, but it could give energy providers another option for storing renewable electricity in a way that is scalable and potentially more durable. "Our approach is to increase operating conditions methodically, validating the data at each stage and resolving issues before moving on," Pratt said in a press release. "That process fundamentally de-risks a system of this scale before full-speed testing and eventual customer deployment." Where can I learn more? Energy-storage technologies are advancing alongside flywheel systems like Pulsar. • Material scientists have unveiled a record-breaking storage device that could reshape clean energy systems. • Envision Energy said its grid battery system can deliver around 96% efficiency. • In Croatia, an automaker introduced an advanced battery system. • NASA engineers built a solid-state sulfur-selenium battery to push energy storage limits. • NASA has also created a battery that could power electric planes. artigo.texto: Vena Energy Wins 46.8 MW Battery Storage Contract in Japan Vena Energy's NRE Nakagawa 2 project in Nagano Prefecture has been selected in Japan's FY2025 auction for long-term decarbonised power sources. Vena Energy, the renewable energy arm of Vena Group and a provider of green energy solutions across the Asia-Pacific region, announced the selection of its NRE Nakagawa 2 Battery Storage project in Japan's FY2025 Long-Term Decarbonised Power Source Auction (LTDA), conducted by the Organisation for Cross-regional Coordination of Transmission Operators (OCCTO). The project, currently under development in Japan, was awarded a capacity of 46,828 kW, according to the company. This type of battery storage deployment reflects a broader trend of similar infrastructure being rolled out, such as the 210 MWh battery storage system installed in Nickelsdorf, Austria. An auction mechanism to support carbon neutrality Introduced in fiscal year 2023, the LTDA scheme is designed to support Japan's ambition to achieve carbon neutrality by 2050. The programme encourages investment in decarbonised power generation by providing long-term revenue certainty, thereby helping developers recover their development and capital costs, according to OCCTO. The NRE Nakagawa 2 project adds to the battery storage portfolio that Vena Energy is developing in Japan. It follows the Hikone Battery Storage project, which began commercial operations last year, according to the company. This new asset confirms Vena Energy's strategy in energy storage within the Japanese market. Company Vena Group: company profile A grid-connected site near Matsumoto The grid-connected battery storage system is located near Matsumoto City, in Nagano Prefecture. Raul Rienda, Head of Japan at Vena Energy, said that deploying battery storage systems is necessary to address the intermittency of renewable energy and enable more efficient use of electricity. According to Mr. Rienda, the project's selection in the FY2025 auction should help strengthen the reliability and resilience of Japan's power system. The company said it will continue to engage with local communities throughout the project's development, with careful attention paid to the surrounding environment. - Gas45.5 % - Coal15.4 % - Nuclear15.2 % - Solar10.9 % - Wind7.3 % - Hydro4.2 % - Bioenergy0.9 % - Other fossil0.5 % - Other renewables0.3 %

artigo.texto: Germany could need 10 GW to 14 GW of bankable BESS tolling capacity by the mid-2030s, according to a PwC and FfE whitepaper As of May 2026, independent developers accounted for 69% of the country’s installed BESS capacity, increasing the importance of debt financing and predictable revenues Authors recommend that higher fixed tolling payments, a greater share of capacity under contract and longer agreement terms can improve the cash flow certainty Germany could require 10 GW to 14 GW of battery energy storage system (BESS) tolling capacity by the mid-2030s to support the financing of its growing storage pipeline, according to a joint white paper by PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC) and the Research Centre for Energy Economics (FfE). The whitepaper titled Challenges in Financing and De-Risking BESS Projects, highlights the growing importance of tolling agreements as battery storage developers increasingly depend on debt financing. Germany’s large-scale BESS capacity is expected to expand significantly. The country’s current grid development plan assumes installed capacity will reach 40 GW by 2037, while FfE expects expansion to up to 28 GW by the mid-2030s. The report also anticipates a shift in storage duration: while installations in the coming years are likely to have durations of around two hours, new projects from the 2030s onwards are expected to increasingly feature around four hours of storage, reflecting changing flexibility requirements. Much of this expansion is driven by independent project developers, according to the whitepaper. Referring to Germany’s Market Data Register, the analysts believe only 31% of the installed capacity of the existing BESS portfolio in Germany was covered by energy supply companies till May 2026, while 69% was realized by independent project developers. The latter rely on debt financing having limited financing capacities of their own, which the report says is difficult to secure based solely on merchant revenues. Tolling models can help address this financing gap by providing more predictable income, recommend the authors. “Tolling makes volatile storage revenues more predictable, thus creating an essential prerequisite for bankable financing of BESS projects,” reads the whitepaper. A recent example of the model’s use in the Asia-Pacific region is Amazon’s tolling agreement with Anza Power for the 50 MW/200 MWh Bairnsdale battery in Australia. The agreement gives Amazon access to the battery’s storage capacity and flexibility without requiring it to own the asset (see Amazon Signs First Battery Storage Tolling Deal In Asia Pacific). However, the availability of bankable tollers is a key challenge, as they need to offer operational expertise, sufficient risk capital and creditworthiness, points out the whitepaper. Additionally, flexible connection agreements, changes to network charges and co-location with renewable energy projects could affect battery operations and revenues. Germany’s proposed AgNes reform of electricity network charges may also have significant implication for project revenues in the future. The reform will require BESS projects commissioned after August 4, 2029 with no qualifying FID, to contribute to network costs (see Germany's AgNes Draft Draws Industry Concerns On Storage FID Timeline). Such factors and uncertainties could lead tollers to demand higher risk premiums, offer lower payments or impose shorter and more restrictive contract terms. The authors of the whitepaper explain how tolling terms can affect the debt available to a BESS project. For instance, a higher fixed tolling payment or a larger share of battery capacity covered by the agreement can increase the cash flow available for loan repayments. A longer contract can also give lenders greater certainty over revenues. The report emphasizes that the tolling agreement, financing terms, manufacturer warranties and technical design must therefore be structured together. Florian Mayr, Partner, Strategy & Germany, PwC said, “The BESS market not only needs more projects and more capital. It also needs a scalable market for bankable tolling capacity and structures that allow risk to be sensibly distributed between asset owners, tollers and capital providers.” The authors therefore highlight the need for project-specific financing and tolling arrangements that account for grid connection conditions, technical design and the project’s marketing strategy. The white paper also identifies potential demand for tolling beyond standalone storage developers. This includes unsubsidized wind and solar plants, large electricity consumers such as data centers and electrolyzers, and certain must-run power plants as market participants that could use tolling structures to manage exposure to volatile electricity prices. The complete white paper in German is available for free download on FfE’s website.

artigo.texto: Pro-data center party interrupted by protesters in D.C. A pro-data center party took place in Washington D.C. on Saturday night, as opposition to data center construction has intensified across the country. An invitation to the event on Partiful said: "In light of the bipartisan psychosis over AI data centers, it's about time that the people who haven't lost their minds get together and celebrate the glory of American compute." Videos posted on social media showed the party in full swing, complete with a DJ booth and dance floor. One X user wrote that the event had "a generative AI photo booth, AI themed cocktails." At one point, protesters appeared to crash the party. One female protester took to the stage and shouted to the crowd "thank you for using all the water" and "you're killing the world," as party-goers chanted "USA!" The protester was eventually seen being removed from the stage. As data center construction accelerates, the debate over how and where the facilities should be built is expected to remain a growing political and environmental issue. After the disruption, Adam Thierer from the R Street Institute took to the stage to say: "You know who doesn't believe in freedom, is the freaks who were just up here charging the stage," the Washington Sun reported. As demand for AI computing has boomed, data centers have become a growing source of tension over their enormous demands for power, water and land. Newsweek contacted Jonas Du and Young Voices via email on Monday, outside of regular working hours. The Party "Data After Dark: A Pro-Data Center Party" was held at the self-described "Bitcoin bar," PubKey in D.C. More than a thousand people had signed up to attend through the Partiful invitation, though it is not clear how many ultimately attended. Young Voices, Pirate Wires and The Compute Optimist were listed on a flyer as the organizations behind the party. The event was sponsored by several think tanks, technology advocacy groups and organizations promoting the expansion of computing infrastructure. The event featured themed cocktails with names inspired by the data center industry, one of the organizers wrote on X. These included the Loudoun County Iced Tea, a reference to the Virginia county at the heart of the region's "Data Center Alley," as well as the SMRtini and the Closed-loop Spritz. Who Were the Event Organizers? The event was organized by Ed Tarnowski, a technology policy fellow at the free-market R Street Institute who has launched the Substack publication The Compute Optimist; Jonas Du, a writer at technology and politics publication Pirate Wires; and Casey Given, the CEO of Young Voices, a nonprofit that trains and promotes young pro-liberty commentators. Tarnowski and Du appeared in a video filmed at the event, in which a reporter asked attendees why they loved data centers. "This is our industrial revolution," Tarnowski said. "AI is poised to deliver benefits that we couldn't imagine," he said, adding that technological progress was reliant on American "dominance of data centers." He also touted the "national security benefits" of data centers, particularly their importance to the U.S. in maintaining a technological edge over China. Du also appeared in the video, and said: "The only way we can get young people and everyday Americans feeling more optimistic about the economy and the future of the country and the American dream is by growing our economy and increasing our innovation rate. And data centers power AI, which is the number one thing driving that right now." "We should use common sense as to where we built them and how we build them, but no question we need to build more," he added. Along with the protesters who expressed their displeasure in person, the event also sparked backlash on social media. While one X user went so far as to say they wished the party would be set on fire with attendees inside, others expressed more temperate criticisms that hosting a glitzy D.C. cocktail party in support of data centers would not help ordinary Americans get on board. Data Center Debate Heats Up The U.S. is in the midst of a boom of data centers, which are large facilities that house the computer servers and other equipment needed to store and process vast amounts of digital information. There are at least 4,000 operational facilities nationwide and some 3,000 more planned or under construction. But the expansion has faced growing opposition over the facilities' demands for resources and their proximity to residential areas. A Gallup poll found that around 70 percent of Americans are opposed to data centers being built in their area. The issue has increasingly become a political flashpoint, as opposition to data centers has spread across party lines, even as the Trump administration promotes their expansion as essential to the U.S. race for AI dominance. artigo.texto: FMC pede registro do herbicida rimisoxafen no Brasil Ingrediente ativo atua nos Grupos 12 e 32 e mira plantas daninhas resistentes em soja e milho O Brasil reúne 20 projetos de carbono agrícola e manejo do solo desenvolvidos com a metodologia VM0042, da Verra. O volume representa cerca de 8% dos 264 projetos desse tipo registrados na base global da certificadora. O pipeline nacional supera 10 milhões de créditos de carbono potenciais por ano. O levantamento consta em relatório da RaboResearch. A escala da agropecuária brasileira amplia o potencial desse mercado. Segundo os dados apresentados pela RaboResearch, com base na Embrapa, o país possui 177 milhões de hectares de pastagens. Desse total, cerca de 28 milhões de hectares, ou 15%, apresentam algum nível de degradação. Essas áreas poderiam passar por processos de recuperação com práticas regenerativas. A proposta associa a melhoria do manejo ao aumento dos estoques de carbono no solo. Entre as práticas citadas aparecem plantio direto, culturas de cobertura, rotação de culturas, integração lavoura-pecuária, manejo regenerativo das pastagens, menor revolvimento do solo e otimização do uso de insumos. O processo também pode gerar efeitos agronômicos. O relatório cita aumento da matéria orgânica, maior retenção de água, redução da erosão, melhoria da fertilidade, ganhos de produtividade e maior resiliência diante de secas e eventos climáticos extremos. A adoção, porém, exige investimento inicial, mudanças operacionais e período de adaptação. Os créditos de carbono podem funcionar como uma fonte adicional de remuneração nesse processo. O produtor adota práticas capazes de elevar os estoques de carbono. O projeto mede e monitora os resultados. Uma entidade independente realiza a validação e a verificação. Após essa etapa, o padrão de certificação pode emitir os créditos. A metodologia VM0042, denominada Improved Agricultural Land Management, concentra boa parte dos projetos analisados. A base pública da Verra reunia 264 projetos de carbono agrícola e manejo do solo na data considerada pelo estudo. A Ásia concentrava 119 projetos. A Europa somava 45. A América Latina tinha 40 e a África, 26. O Brasil respondia por 20 iniciativas, metade do total latino-americano. A maior parte dos projetos brasileiros ainda percorre fases anteriores à emissão. O relatório identificou sete projetos em pipeline aprovado, quatro em pipeline solicitado, um em pipeline solicitado já em validação, três em validação, dois em processo de registro e verificação, dois aguardando registro e apenas um projeto registrado com créditos emitidos. O quadro indica um mercado ainda em consolidação. A entrada de uma propriedade em um projeto agrupado de carbono no solo começa pela análise de elegibilidade. O processo considera histórico de uso da terra, práticas de manejo, localização, disponibilidade de dados e potencial de remoção de carbono. Depois da adesão, o projeto realiza um diagnóstico da propriedade. Essa avaliação estabelece a linha de base. A referência reúne as condições produtivas e os estoques de carbono existentes antes da implantação das novas práticas. O projeto define então o plano de manejo. Durante o período de creditação, o produtor precisa manter as práticas acordadas e fornecer dados operacionais. Também precisa permitir auditorias e participar do monitoramento. Esse acompanhamento pode envolver registros de manejo, imagens de satélite, análises de solo, visitas de campo e modelos científicos. O desenvolvedor consolida os dados. Entidades independentes fazem a validação e a verificação. Após a confirmação das remoções, o padrão aplicável emite os créditos. A comercialização gera receita. O produtor recebe uma parcela conforme as condições previstas em contrato. A RaboResearch ressalta o horizonte longo desses projetos. A implantação das práticas, o monitoramento, a verificação e a emissão dos créditos ocorrem ao longo dos anos. O retorno financeiro não ocorre de forma imediata. Entre as iniciativas citadas aparece o ReTerra, parceria entre Rabobank Brasil, Ruuts by Ovis 21 e Anthesis Group. O projeto pretende ampliar a integração lavoura-pecuária e o pastejo regenerativo adaptativo. A meta envolve pelo menos 350 mil hectares nos próximos cinco anos. O relatório também apresenta o Programa de Agricultura Regenerativa da América do Sul, conhecido como SARA. A iniciativa concluiu sua primeira emissão em fevereiro de 2026. Foram gerados 210 mil créditos sob a metodologia VM0042 para o período de monitoramento de 2019 a 2023. Mais de um quarto desse volume já havia sido comercializado na data do relatório. A receita alcançou cerca de 1,2 milhão de dólares. O valor implica preço médio próximo de 21,80 dólares por tonelada de dióxido de carbono equivalente. O programa atende mais de 130 fazendas em 150 mil hectares na Argentina, Chile e Paraguai. A meta prevê alcançar 500 mil hectares e superar um milhão de toneladas de dióxido de carbono equivalente em remoções anuais a partir de 2028, condicionadas às verificações e à expansão do programa. Outra iniciativa reúne AMAGGI e NaturAll Carbon em Rondônia. A primeira etapa abrange cerca de 25 mil hectares na Fazenda Carolinas. O manejo previsto inclui plantio direto, rotação de culturas, culturas de cobertura e maior uso de insumos biológicos. O projeto prevê certificação pela metodologia VM0042. A quantificação do carbono aparece entre os principais desafios. Os projetos precisam demonstrar remoções mensuráveis e associadas às mudanças de manejo. Também precisam comprovar a manutenção dos ganhos ao longo do período definido. O relatório aponta necessidade de sistemas robustos de monitoramento, amostragem e verificação. Os resultados ainda podem sofrer influência da variabilidade climática, de eventos meteorológicos extremos, dos preços dos créditos e da demanda dos compradores. A regulamentação brasileira também integra esse cenário. A Lei número 15.042, de 2024, instituiu o Sistema Brasileiro de Comércio de Emissõ

artigo.texto: Residents feel 'let down' by council as battery storage site approved Residents say they have been "let down" by their local council after a massive battery energy storage site was approved on appeal by Welsh government planning inspectors. Developers Innova have won a case to build a 400MW facility on a site near the village of Rhostyllen, Wrexham, which it said could power 900,000 homes. Campaigners claim Wrexham council officers failed to represent them properly at the inspectorate hearing. But the authority said it had presented as robust a case as it could and would now have to pay legal costs. Battery energy storage sites (BESS) are seen as an important part of reducing use of carbon by storing energy from renewables and releasing it to the grid when needed. Campaigners are concerned about the development's effects on agricultural land, biodiversity, the area's character and fire safety. "We were told by Wrexham planning department that they would represent us vocally and with evidence," said Alan Jones, chairman of Esclusham Community Group which has campaigned against the development. "We feel they didn't represent us at all. "Because we weren't represented, we have no case to take this to appeal so we're really disappointed." Developers appealed to inspectors at Planning and Environment Decisions Wales after Wrexham council failed to consider the application in the required time. The council's own planning committee then decided the local authority should oppose the plans at a hearing in July. Mark Andrew, from the local community council, said it had "hoped the local planning department would put a good argument in place". "The inspector said that no evidence was given against the case for the battery farm," he said. "It's angered so many people." Wrexham council said a senior officer was at the hearing and the authority had "presented as robust a case as it could explaining the reasons for the planning committee's decision". "The disappointment of the local community about the outcome of the appeal is understandable," it said. The council said it was now awaiting an invoice from the developers for costs after the inspector "concluded the council had acted unreasonably". Innova said it was pleased its appeal had been allowed and would "provide further updates to the local community as the project progresses towards construction".

artigo.texto: The New Economics of Enterprise AI AI costs stop being about tokens once it hits production — the real question is whether you own or just rent the economics. September 28, 2026 Sponsored by HPE Imagine your company just discovered electricity. At first only a few machines run on it, and nobody worries about efficiency — consumption is low and the value is obvious. But once electricity becomes infrastructure, every process depends on it, and the question changes from "can we use it?" to "how efficiently are we using it?" Enterprise AI is going through the same shift. What began as isolated chatbot and copilot experiments is becoming a foundational layer of the business, with models, agents, and data increasingly interconnected in production workloads. The important question stops being what a token or GPU-hour costs. It becomes how efficiently the AI environment converts paid capacity into useful business outcomes. That's the metric worth tracking: effective cost per useful outcome — the total platform, model, operations, and capacity cost required to complete work the business can actually use, whether a resolved request or a completed workflow. Three ways to run AI Utilization is central to this economics. Directing more work to paid-for capacity lowers effective unit cost; idle GPUs, fragmented workloads, and oversized models all raise the cost of every useful result. Enterprises generally choose among three models: A bespoke stack — procuring infrastructure and controls in-house. Flexible, but it creates a continuing burden, since teams must revalidate the environment as models and policies change. On-demand consumption — hyperscalers reduce the assembly burden and suit low or uncertain demand, but charges rise with every prompt or agent action. An integrated private AI platform — owned or dedicated capacity paired with a validated stack. The advantage isn't free inference; it's control over efficiency levers like scheduling, model selection, GPU partitioning, and cache management. The right model depends on the workload. APIs can be rational for experimentation or variable demand. As workloads become sustained and business-critical, enterprises need to weigh not just what they consume, but how efficiently they operate the system. Ownership is an operating discipline Buying a Formula 1 race car and parking it in your garage means owning one of the most sophisticated vehicles ever built — but ownership alone doesn't make you competitive; you still need drivers, mechanics, and track time to justify it. AI infrastructure works the same way. One of the biggest misconceptions in enterprise AI is that owning infrastructure automatically improves economics. Owning GPUs creates the opportunity for better economics, but only if the organization has sufficient demand and operational discipline to keep resources productive. The infrastructure that returns the best ROI isn't a reference architecture or a bespoke build-out — it's a fully integrated, qualified stack that lets teams route tasks to the least costly model that meets quality requirements and reuse context through techniques such as KV-cache management, reducing wasted capacity while maintaining responsiveness. Without these practices, committed infrastructure can become stranded capital. With them, rising demand improves economics as fixed costs are amortized across more useful work — increasingly important in agentic systems, where economics are shaped less by any single prompt than by the efficiency of the complete environment. From deployment to value HPE Private Cloud AI is a production-ready foundation combining infrastructure, software, models, tools, governance, and services, reducing the integration burden of operating private AI at scale. Its architecture lets teams manage scheduling, model selection, GPU partitioning, and cache management as operational levers, aligning capacity and service levels with each workload's requirements. It also includes a 90-day engagement with forward-deployed engineers who help customer teams deploy initial use cases and establish repeatable operating practices. In independent testing commissioned by HPE, an integrated platform serving multiple workloads at high utilization delivered a lower effective cost per token than repeatedly renting equivalent capacity. Actual results will vary based on workload mix and utilization. Measure what matters Token consumption remains useful, but it isn't a complete measure of AI economics. A fuller enterprise view tracks cost per business-relevant outcome, accelerator utilization, and model choice relative to task complexity. Enterprises already operating private AI should ask how mature their utilization is, and how workload volume will change over the next 12 to 18 months. Those earlier in the journey should build these practices in from the first deployment, so strategy anticipates growth before demand becomes a bottleneck. For low-volume, unpredictable demand, an API or hyperscaler may remain sensible. But as AI becomes a continuous production capability, enterprises have a growing incentive to control utilization, amortize fixed costs, and manage the environment as a long-term operating asset. The strategic question isn't whether enterprises will pay for AI — it's whether they will understand, and ultimately own, the economics behind it. His passion is turning the art of the possible into operational reality. There are phased risks in 2027-2029, with surplus pilot lines and localized price wars on the equipment side; after 2030, if technology routes converge, leading capacity is released, and demand growth slows, industry-wide involution could occur, with intensity likely lower than in PV but with slower market exit. Given the lessons from PV, the solid-state battery industry is fully capable of avoiding involution. SMM has recently reviewed the future of solid-state batteries and compiled a ten-year series. Using the current development of the lithium battery industry as a reference, especially the intertwined history of the LFP and ternary routes, which has written an epic chapter over time. In the long history of conventional liquid lithium batteries, semi-solid and solid-state batteries will take the stage, outlining a new generation of high-specific-energy battery world. artigo.texto: SMT Energy Secures $268 Million for Battery Storage Expansion ⚡ Quick Read - What happened: SMT Energy secured an equity investment of up to $268 million from Climate Adaptive Infrastructure (CAI) to scale its battery energy storage project portfolio. - Why it matters: This capital infusion highlights the growing institutional appetite for BESS assets, providing a roadmap for similar financing structures in the Indian market. - Watch: The deployment of these funds into utility-scale storage projects and the potential for similar cross-border infrastructure investments. Background and Context SMT Energy, a developer, owner, and operator of critical energy infrastructure, has successfully closed an equity partnership with Climate Adaptive Infrastructure (CAI) to secure up to $268 million in funding. This significant capital injection is earmarked for the development, construction, and operation of battery energy storage projects across the United States. The partnership builds upon a prior $32 million investment by CAI, signaling strong investor confidence in SMT Energy’s operational model and the broader energy storage sector. Key Details The funding is structured at the parent-company level, providing SMT Energy with the necessary liquidity to expand its development platform. According to the company, the capital will be used alongside tax equity and project-level debt to execute its pipeline of distributed generation and utility-scale storage assets. This follows a successful financing round in February 2025, where the company secured $135 million to develop a 160 MW/320 MWh battery energy storage project in Houston, Texas. Macquarie and KeyBanc served as joint lead arrangers for that specific project financing. What This Means for EPCs and Developers For EPC contractors and developers, this deal underscores the increasing importance of grid stabilization as renewable energy penetration grows. As wind and solar capacity continues to scale globally, battery storage is becoming the primary solution for managing intermittency. The ability to secure large-scale equity partnerships is a critical differentiator for developers. Furthermore, the involvement of specialized infrastructure firms like CAI demonstrates that institutional investors are moving beyond simple project-level debt, opting instead for platform-level investments to capture long-term value in the energy transition. What Happens Next The energy storage market continues to see robust capital flows, with Mercom reporting $8.9 billion in corporate funding across 73 deals in the first half of 2026. As the India renewable energy sector matures, the demand for sophisticated storage solutions is expected to mirror global trends. Developers in India should monitor such international financing models, as they provide a blueprint for securing the capital-intensive backing required for large-scale BESS and pumped hydro projects. The focus will now shift to how effectively SMT Energy deploys this capital to meet the rising demand for grid-scale storage capacity.

artigo.texto: Crusoe, a company building AI factories, has announced that it is the developer of Google’s new data center campus being built in Armstrong County outside of Amarillo, Texas. The campus is Crusoe’s latest in West Texas, joining two others under development in Abilene. Construction of the data center campus began in June 2025 and connects directly to Serena’s Goodnight 1 wind farm, which is operational and generates 265.5 MW. It is also adjacent to the Goodnight 2 wind farm ,which is under construction and will generate the same 265.5 MW. Surplus power from the wind farms will be fed back to the grid, in line with Crusoe’s efforts to support the buildout of clean, affordable energy in the region. “Building the future of AI requires a new kind of infrastructure, starting with energy. Crusoe’s strategy is to build AI factories directly at the source of abundant, low-cost energy – to both improve utilization of existing assets as well as catalyze new energy generation,” said Chase Lochmiller, Crusoe Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer. “The Armstrong County campus is a prime example of this energy-first strategy. We’re bringing new, affordable clean energy online. We broke ground in June 2025 and are building at the same swift pace we set in Abilene.” In addition to the power supplied by the wind farms, the campus is designed to be water efficient. It will utilize a closed-loop, non-evaporative liquid cooling system. According to the press release, this will limit the facility’s water consumption to domestic uses such as kitchens. Crusoe has not said how much IT capacity the campus will support, nor how much it intends to invest in the development. Power has become the great decider for projects in Texas. In August, governor Greg Abbott directed the Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUCT) and the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) to conduct a verification audit of all data center projects moving through ERCOT’s interconnection process. ERCOT was considering 474 GW in grid connection requests at the time, 90 percent of which were for data centers. Since then several projects have been granted conditional base load status including the 2 GW Sweetwater Hub in West Texas being constructed by IREN. CleanSpark, Hut 8, and Galaxy Digital were granted the same status in ERCOT’s Batch Zero process in September, as w.media reported.

artigo.texto: The global artificial intelligence industry needs to earn $6 trillion in annual revenue by 2031 to justify the capital being deployed to build data centers around the world, Bain & Co. said. Existing consumer and enterprise AI services may generate as much as $1.8 trillion of that sum, leaving $4.2 trillion in new revenue that needs to be created, the consulting firm said Tuesday in its annual global technology report. The shortfall likely will come from nascent segments ranging from autonomous machines to robotics, as well as emerging fields such as drug discovery, mental health and energy generation, it said. “What the industry needs is a wave of innovation that will dwarf what mobile and cloud unlocked,” said David Crawford, the report’s lead author and chair of Bain’s Global Technology, Media, and Telecommunications practice. “AI infrastructure is being built well ahead of the demand curve, and funding it sustainably will require adding approximately 1% to the annual global GDP growth rate,” he said. Bain’s report highlights the hurdles ahead to make the current pace of AI development sustainable. Companies led by Microsoft, Alphabet’s Google, Amazon.com, Meta Platforms and Oracle are investing trillions of dollars in data centers to quench AI’s demand for computational resources. Data center sizes and costs are doubling roughly every 12 to 16 months, in part due to surging prices of chips from the likes of Nvidia and SK Hynix, networking equipment and other components. The report comes as debate intensifies around the as-yet elusive returns for AI service providers. Critics worry about an increasingly interconnected web of dependencies between technology manufacturers and AI developers that help to propel lofty expectations that in turn require bigger sums of money. While discussions today are fixated on employee productivity, the economics of AI infrastructure will demand trillions in new revenue beyond productivity gains, Bain said. The consultancy projects $5 trillion to $6.5 trillion of data-center spending by 2030, adding at least 150 gigawatts of capacity that will further strain countries’ energy resources. Annual spending on AI infrastructure — spanning data centers, computing capacity and upgrades in accelerators and memory chips — may reach as much as $1.5 trillion by 2031, it said. Data center developers already face shortages in transformers and water and power supplies, as well as fierce local opposition that’s blocked or delayed $68 billion worth of projects in the June quarter in the United States.
