artigo.texto: As regras sobre o pagamento do Encargo de Potência para Reserva de Capacidade (Ercap) e o tratamento de uma eventual insuficiência de arrecadação estão entre os pontos questionados por agentes em relação aos editais dos dois leilões de reserva de capacidade de baterias previstos para dezembro. Enquanto associações de consumidores e distribuidoras defendem que os geradores continuem identificados expressamente como responsáveis pelo custeio do encargo, geradores e desenvolvedores pedem que os contratos possam se adaptar a uma eventual mudança na legislação. Os posicionamentos foram apresentados em contribuições nas consultas públicas realizadas pela Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel) para discutir os editais dos leilões. Levantamento da MegaWhat identificou contribuições de 101 agentes no certame com exigência de conteúdo nacional e 87 no segundo certame. A Lei 15.269/2025 determinou que os custos da contratação de sistemas de armazenamento por meio de leilões de reserva de capacidade (LRCap) devem ser rateados entre os agentes de geração. As minutas levam essa definição para os contratos e preveem que a Câmara de Comercialização de Energia Elétrica (CCEE) celebre o Contrato de Reserva de Capacidade para Potência (CRCap) como representante desses agentes. Há, no entanto, iniciativas no Congresso para alterar a legislação e incluir os consumidores entre os pagadores da remuneração das baterias. Base pagadora do encargo A Associação Brasileira de Distribuidores de Energia Elétrica (Abradee) pediu a manutenção dessa estrutura. Para a entidade, a legislação já delimitou os responsáveis pelo rateio e cabe à regulamentação da Aneel definir como a cobrança será operacionalizada. A Associação Brasileira de Grandes Consumidores Industriais de Energia e de Consumidores Livres (Abrace) também defendeu que os documentos mantenham expressamente a responsabilidade dos geradores. Segundo a entidade, eventuais dificuldades para arrecadar recursos suficientes devem ser resolvidas dentro do próprio segmento definido em lei. “Eventuais desafios relacionados à definição da base pagadora devem ser solucionados dentro do próprio segmento definido pela legislação como responsável pelo custeio”, afirmou. Outros participantes propuseram manter a aplicação da regra atual, mas sem vincular os contratos, que terão duração de 15 anos, permanentemente aos geradores. A Associação Brasileira dos Produtores Independentes de Energia Elétrica (Apine) sugeriu substituir as referências específicas aos agentes de geração por uma menção à legislação e à regulamentação vigentes. Segundo a associação, a mudança permitiria incorporar uma eventual alteração futura na base de custeio sem necessidade de modificar os contratos. “A presente contribuição não solicita o descumprimento da legislação vigente”, afirmou a Apine, ao defender que o contrato não “cristalize” a definição atual. A Associação Brasileira dos Investidores em Autoprodução de Energia (Abiape), a Associação Brasileira de Soluções de Armazenamento de Energia (Absae) e a Comerc Energia também propuseram vincular a definição dos pagadores à legislação e à regulamentação aplicáveis. Risco de arrecadação no leilão Outro ponto questionado é a cláusula do CRCap que inclui entre os riscos de responsabilidade do vendedor o recebimento do Ercap destinado ao custeio do contrato. Apine, Associação Brasileira das Empresas Geradoras de Energia Elétrica (Abrage), Absae e outros participantes pediram a exclusão dessa previsão. A Apine argumentou que o empreendimento poderia cumprir suas obrigações contratuais e ainda assim não receber integralmente sua remuneração por problemas na arrecadação do encargo. A Abrage também pediu a retirada da cláusula e afirmou que o Decreto 10.707/2021 já prevê mecanismos para tratar a inadimplência na contratação de reserva de capacidade. Para a associação, a regra proposta cria “risco desproporcional ao agente vendedor”. A Absae destacou que cobrança, arrecadação, liquidação e repasse dos recursos são operacionalizados pela CCEE e não estão sob controle do empreendimento. “Eventual inadimplência dos agentes responsáveis pelo pagamento, insuficiência de arrecadação ou alterações legais e regulatórias que afetem esse mecanismo não decorrem de ação ou omissão do vendedor”, afirmou. A 2C Energia fez distinção entre a definição de quem paga o encargo e a responsabilidade por uma eventual falta de recursos. A empresa afirmou que não questiona a base de custeio, mas pediu que inadimplência dos pagadores, insuficiência de arrecadação e mudanças no regime de custeio não sejam tratadas como riscos exclusivos do vendedor. A Kinea propôs uma solução diferente. Além de retirar a atribuição integral desse risco ao vendedor, sugeriu prever no contrato um mecanismo de recomposição dos valores não arrecadados, condicionado às medidas de cobrança previstas na regulamentação. Segundo a contribuição, “o vendedor não fatura o encargo, não conduz sua cobrança e não detém legitimidade para a recuperação dos créditos inadimplidos”. Contas separadas A administração dos recursos do Ercap também entrou nas contribuições. Apine e Eneva sugeriram separar financeiramente os contratos de armazenamento dos demais contratos de reserva de capacidade caso o custeio das baterias permaneça restrito aos geradores. A Apine propôs uma conta específica para armazenamento, separada da Conta de Potência para Reserva de Capacidade usada pelos demais produtos. A associação argumentou que bases pagadoras diferentes podem levar ao compartilhamento de riscos financeiros entre contratos com formas distintas de custeio. A Eneva também sugeriu uma subconta própria para os sistemas de armazenamento. Segundo a empresa, inadimplência ou insuficiência de arrecadação do Ercap das baterias não deveria afetar recursos destinados ao pagamento de contratos de outras tecnologias. artigo.texto: Mercedes-Benz deepens solid-state battery push with ProLogium The long-term partnership enters a new testing phase for ProLogium's Gen4 solid-state cells, as the battery maker accelerates construction of its 44 GWh European gigafactory Mercedes-Benz and Taiwanese battery developer ProLogium have signed a joint testing agreement giving the German carmaker priority access to evaluate ProLogium's latest Gen4 superfluidised inorganic next-generation lithium ceramic battery cells, deepening a technical relationship between the two companies that stretches back nearly a decade. The agreement builds directly on Mercedes-Benz's long-standing investment in ProLogium and a series of joint technical development agreements the two companies have pursued since 2016. Under the new arrangement, the Gen4 cells will undergo extensive electrical, thermal and safety testing at Mercedes-Benz's dedicated facilities, as well as at specialised external testing institutes, with the results used to assess the technology's suitability for potential use in future Mercedes-Benz vehicles. A "superfluidised" approach to solid-state chemistry ProLogium's Gen4 platform represents the company's latest attempt to resolve one of the central trade-offs in solid-state battery development: balancing safety, energy density and manufacturability. The Gen4 battery is built around what the company describes as five core advantages – intrinsic safety, high-performance, high-energy density, scalable manufacturing and a competitive cost structure. Its safety architecture combines a non-flammable inorganic electrolyte with ceramic separator technology and a proprietary active safety mechanism, while the cells are also designed to support fast charging, high power output and strong low-temperature performance. The "superfluidised" terminology reflects ProLogium's broader technology strategy: rather than pursuing a purely solid electrolyte, the company has positioned its next-generation lithium ceramic batteries as integrating the respective advantages of both solid-state and liquid battery technologies, with the stated aim of achieving scalable manufacturability alongside cost competitiveness. Over nearly a decade, our collaboration with Mercedes-Benz has evolved from early cell development and validation to testing our latest Gen4 technology for future vehicle applications Nearly a decade of joint development The relationship between Mercedes-Benz and ProLogium dates to 2016 and has progressed in stages – from early hybrid-solid-state Gen3 development and validation work through to joint technical development agreements and, eventually, Mercedes-Benz taking an equity stake in the battery maker. Over the course of the partnership, the two companies have validated multiple lithium ceramic battery formats together, including pouch cells and ProLogium's first next-generation prismatic cells, as well as the company's Bi-Polar cell technology. "Over nearly a decade, our collaboration with Mercedes-Benz has evolved from early cell development and validation to testing our latest Gen4 technology for future vehicle applications," said Vincent Yang, Founder and CEO of ProLogium. "For next-generation batteries, true value comes from turning years of innovation into scalable manufacturing and commercially viable products. With Mercedes-Benz's early investment and support for our European expansion, together with the strong support of the French government and the European Union, we are advancing toward large-scale production in Europe and building a manufacturing footprint to serve global markets." Jörg Burzer, Member of the Board of Management at Mercedes-Benz Group AG and Chief Technology Officer for Development & Procurement, framed the agreement as part of the carmaker's wider push into next-generation battery chemistries. "At Mercedes-Benz, we are committed to shaping the future of electric mobility through technological leadership and innovation," Burzer said. "Our long-standing partnership with ProLogium is a strong example of how we bring the best expertise together to advance next-generation battery technologies. By combining ProLogium's pioneering solid-state battery approach with Mercedes-Benz's deep battery development, testing and integration capabilities, we are taking the next step in exploring advanced battery technologies for future electric vehicles." Scaling from Taiwan to northern France ProLogium's ability to deliver on that scaling ambition rests heavily on its expanding manufacturing footprint. The company's first GWh-scale facility, the Taoke Gigafactory in Taoyuan, Taiwan, has already completed GWh-scale manufacturing validation and is supporting C-sample production and demonstration vehicle programmes, alongside future commercial production. ProLogium describes Taoke as the first commercial next-generation lithium ceramic battery gigafactory to have publicly demonstrated a mass-production line — evidence, the company argues, that next-generation lithium ceramic batteries are no longer confined to the laboratory. That manufacturing know-how is now being replicated in Europe. ProLogium's second gigafactory, located in Dunkirk, France, held its groundbreaking ceremony for phase one construction in February 2026 and has, according to a separate company announcement, now moved from preparatory work into coordinated on-site execution. Multiple infrastructure workstreams are underway, including electrical installation and grid connection activity, ahead of a planned power-up of the construction site in early October 2026. The Dunkirk facility will incorporate a bespoke cleanroom and dry room solution designed specifically for high-technology battery manufacturing, and ProLogium is targeting BREEAM sustainability certification for the site. artigo.texto: A company recently visited the site of Bucksport’s former paper mill with interest in developing a data center there. That information was shared publicly for the first time Thursday when the Town Council considered a temporary data center ban, which was introduced as a way to buy time to update regulations around such developments before any formal proposal came in. Bucksport’s lingering infrastructure from its mill – deep water access, a power plant, a fresh water supply – and the mostly vacant site itself make the town more realistically attractive to data center developers than many other Maine communities that have adopted such bans in recent months. But the proposed pause has met with a mixed reception rooted in the town’s long-running desire to attract new industry for its tax base post-mill. The confirmation that at least one developer has already visited adds new information to that conversation and adds to the number of Maine sites eyed by data center developers, who have sometimes caught officials off guard with proposals. “It’s current, it’s relevant, it should be discussed,” councilor Tracey Hair said during the council’s first reading of a potential ban Thursday. “…This [moratorium] is very timely because a data center has come to town with an interest.” She said after the meeting that she didn’t know a company had already visited when she brought up the idea earlier this month. No formal proposal has been submitted. The former mill site is privately owned, meaning the town’s say over what is built there is limited to local regulations. Almost all of it belongs to Whole Oceans, LLC, the company that proposed a major land-based fish farm eight years ago with big economic promises but never broke ground. A state economic development plan released last year also named a data center as one potentially valuable reuse of Bucksport’s mill site. Hair learned about the recent developer visit from resident Don White, who had confirmed it with town officials, she told the Bangor Daily News after Thursday’s meeting. White said the town’s economic and community development director, Rich Rotella, told him that a company called Kratos LLC visited part of the site earlier this summer with town officials and had last communicated with Bucksport in early August. Rotella did not respond to requests to verify that. He also did not respond to BDN inquiries earlier this month about whether any developers had shown interest in the site. Several entities named Kratos work in or around the data center industry – Kratos AI, Kratos Data Centers, Kratos Defense, Kratos Space, Kratos Industries – but it’s not publicly clear if, or how, most of them are connected to each other. Kratos Industries, which designs and manufactures electrical equipment for data centers and other large facilities, was acquired by data center supplier Legrand earlier this year. They have not visited Maine and are not connected to any potential plans here, a spokesperson said Friday. Kratos Industries are not affiliated with the other companies using Kratos in their name, the spokesperson said. Kratos AI, whose website advertises data centers, did not return an email seeking comment. The website for Kratos Data Centers includes only a contact form, which appeared to be broken Thursday night. The temporary ban was first fully discussed at a committee meeting two weeks ago. It would last for up to 180 days but could be rescinded if town rules were updated earlier; even supporters said the idea was not to keep away a data center, but to put guardrails in place. Supporters said it would be a way to protect townspeople, listing concerns about the potential impacts of new technology that didn’t exist when town code was written. Those included significant demands on energy and water that would bring higher electric costs, loud and constant noise, pollution, harm to human health and a lack of decommissioning plans. Hair also noted the town has learned the hard way that investors do not always keep their promises. “This is about Bucksport,” Councilor Paul Rabs said in support. “This is going to be about our water, this is going to be about our electricity.” A state task force formed after Gov. Janet Mills’ veto of a statewide ban, made to save a project at Jay’s former paper mill, is also studying large-scale centers and plans to release a report in January. Others said at Bucksport’s initial conversation, and in smaller numbers Thursday, that they felt a halt on data centers would send a hostile message to interested developers with deep pockets that could bring long-desired industry to the mill site. Existing ordinances are mostly prepared for such a proposal, Code Enforcement Officer Luke Chiavelli said earlier this month, but could be tweaked without a ban. The town has also begun a multi-year process of making structural cuts to reduce costs. Many residents want their tax burden relieved by industrial growth rather than cuts to services, according to councilor Ed Rankin. He was the only one to vote against advancing the ban Thursday, saying he could support a pause on larger projects over 20 megawatts but not smaller ones. Councilors also discussed a need for more information, calling the conversation speculative in some ways. A second reading and a public hearing will be held before a vote on the ban.

artigo.texto: NeoVolta reported $13.3 million in revenue for fiscal 2026, representing growth of 58% year over year, as the company expanded beyond its historical residential energy storage business toward commercial, industrial, and utility-scale battery systems. Despite the annual revenue increase, NeoVolta reported a substantial decline in fourth-quarter sales and a wider net loss as it invested in U.S. manufacturing capacity and its broader energy storage strategy. For the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026, revenue increased from $8.4 million in the prior year. The company reported a GAAP net loss of $21.5 million, compared with a $5 million loss in fiscal 2025. The annual loss was equivalent to $0.55 per share, compared with $0.15 per share a year earlier. Adjusted EBITDA was negative $12.8 million, compared with negative $2.6 million in fiscal 2025. NeoVolta’s fourth-quarter results reflected a particularly challenging period for its traditional residential energy storage operations. Quarterly revenue declined to approximately $13,500 from $4.8 million in the corresponding period of the previous fiscal year. Management attributed the decline primarily to reduced sales through residential and traditional installer channels following federal tax law changes earlier in 2026. The fourth-quarter GAAP net loss widened to $11.7 million from $1.6 million. The result included a $3.9 million provision for credit losses and bad debt expenses and a $1.1 million residential inventory obsolescence reserve. Adjusted EBITDA for the quarter was negative $8 million, compared with negative $700,000 a year earlier. NeoVolta ended June with $22.2 million in unrestricted cash and cash equivalents, alongside $3.2 million in restricted cash. Its combined cash position reached $25.4 million, following a public offering completed in May 2026. A central component of NeoVolta’s expansion strategy is NeoVolta Power, its 80%-owned battery energy storage manufacturing joint venture in Pendergrass, Georgia. The facility is being developed to manufacture battery energy storage systems for utility-scale and commercial applications. NeoVolta plans to complete site acceptance testing and commissioning, with the production ramp expected to begin during the second quarter of fiscal 2027. The company is also evaluating a second production line that could increase the facility’s capacity toward 8 gigawatt-hours of annual battery system production in calendar 2028. Following the fiscal year-end, NeoVolta Power announced a five-year strategic supply and manufacturing collaboration with SK On. The arrangement includes a signed agreement for SK On to supply 9 gigawatt-hours of U.S.-manufactured lithium iron phosphate battery cells between 2027 and 2031. A broader collaboration framework contemplates an additional 9 gigawatt-hours of cell supply and purchases of battery packs manufactured by NeoVolta Power. The signed agreement and broader framework together contemplate up to 18 gigawatt-hours of combined activity, although the additional commitments remain subject to future arrangements. NeoVolta is also developing commercial opportunities in the utility-scale and data center markets. The company previously signed a nonbinding letter of intent with Infinite Grid Capital involving approximately 1.1 gigawatt-hours of potential battery system deployments, representing an estimated $200 million in potential business. In September, the parties entered into a binding capacity reservation agreement supporting battery energy storage systems for North Ontario Edge AI data center projects in 2027. The full potential value of the original letter of intent should not be treated as contracted revenue. To support its manufacturing expansion, NeoVolta subsequently entered into a $20 million senior secured term loan facility, with an option to increase commitments by an additional $10 million through mutual agreement with participating lenders. The initial funding is subject to a $1 million original issue discount. Management intends to prioritize working capital for the Georgia manufacturing ramp and potential investment in a second production line during fiscal 2027. KEY QUOTES: “More importantly, fiscal 2026 was defined by the progress we made at Pendergrass. Our facility is advancing through commissioning and production-ramp activities, and our strategic collaboration with SK On supports our long-term capacity-expansion plans through a multi-year U.S.-manufactured LFP cell-supply agreement and broader pack-manufacturing collaboration. Combined with the growth of our utility-scale and C&I pipeline, we believe NeoVolta enters fiscal year 2027 with a stronger platform to execute our growth strategy.” Ardes Johnson, CEO Of NeoVolta “Beginning this quarter, we are introducing Adjusted EBITDA as a supplemental disclosure to provide investors with greater visibility into our underlying operating performance as our business grows. Our balance sheet was strengthened by the completion of our May offering, and subsequent to year-end, we entered into a senior secured term loan facility that provides additional capital for working capital and general corporate purposes. As we enter fiscal year 2027, our focus is on disciplined execution of the Pendergrass production ramp and converting commercial opportunities into durable growth.” Jing Nealis, CFO Of NeoVolta

artigo.texto: AGRONEGÓCIO Pesquisas preparam agro para mercado de carbono que já gera R$ 556 bilhões por ano Publicado em 28/09/2026 10:32:56 por infocoweb Pesquisas realizadas por universidades e pela Empresa Brasileira de Pesquisa Agropecuária (Embrapa) começam a dimensionar quanto o campo brasileiro pode reduzir de emissões e retirar de carbono da atmosfera por meio da recuperação de pastagens, do plantio direto, da rotação de culturas, dos sistemas integrados e do uso de microrganismos. Além do efeito ambiental, os resultados ajudam a construir as bases técnicas para a futura participação dos produtores no mercado de carbono. As pesquisas ganham cada vez mais importância, dado o tamanho crescente do mercado mundial de carbono. Segundo o Banco Mundial, os sistemas de precificação de carbono geraram mais de R$ 556 bilhões em receitas públicas no mundo em 2025, considerando a conversão pela Ptax mais recente. O resultado reúne a arrecadação com impostos sobre emissões e sistemas regulados de comércio de carbono. Atualmente, 87 instrumentos desse tipo estão em funcionamento e alcançam pouco mais de 29% das emissões globais de gases de efeito estufa. Uma dessas pesquisas reuniu cientistas da Escola Superior de Agricultura Luiz de Queiroz da Universidade de São Paulo (Esalq-USP), da Embrapa Agricultura Digital e da Universidade Estadual de Ponta Grossa (UEPG). O estudo conjunto, publicado em 2026 na revista científica Nature Communications, estimou que a conversão de áreas naturais para uso agropecuário retirou aproximadamente 1,4 bilhão de toneladas de carbono dos solos brasileiros. O volume equivale a cerca de 5,2 bilhões de toneladas de dióxido de carbono. A estimativa foi calculada com base em 4.290 registros reunidos por 372 estudos realizados ao longo de três décadas, com informações dos seis biomas brasileiros. Os pesquisadores chamam essa diferença de “dívida de carbono”: o espaço existente entre o estoque encontrado na vegetação nativa e o mantido atualmente nas áreas produtivas. Isso não significa que todo o volume possa ser recuperado, mas indica que o manejo pode devolver ao solo parte da matéria orgânica perdida. Os resultados variam conforme o bioma e o sistema produtivo. No Cerrado, a substituição da monocultura por sistemas integrados apresentou potencial teórico de elevar em 15,3% o estoque de carbono no solo. Na Amazônia, a adoção da rotação ou do consórcio de culturas pode proporcionar incremento de 14,1%. Parte desse potencial já foi observada em experimentos de campo. Em Sinop, no norte de Mato Grosso, a Embrapa Agrossilvipastoril e o Centro de Energia Nuclear na Agricultura da Universidade de São Paulo (Cena-USP) acompanharam durante quatro anos diferentes combinações de lavoura, pecuária e floresta. Ao final do período, todos os sistemas avaliados apresentaram remoção de carbono superior às emissões contabilizadas. O melhor resultado foi registrado na integração pecuária-floresta, com saldo de 51,3 toneladas de dióxido de carbono equivalente por hectare. Na integração lavoura-pecuária-floresta, a diferença chegou a 39,5 toneladas por hectare. Os valores correspondem ao resultado acumulado nos quatro anos, e não a uma taxa anual. As árvores armazenaram carbono nos troncos, galhos e raízes, enquanto as pastagens bem manejadas contribuíram para ampliar a matéria orgânica do solo. O aumento da produtividade também reduziu a emissão calculada por quilo de carne produzido. Outro acompanhamento da Embrapa foi realizado na Fazenda Santa Brígida, em Ipameri, Goiás. A propriedade começou a adotar sistemas integrados em áreas de pastagens degradadas em 2006, combinando plantio direto, rotação de culturas, braquiária, milho, soja, pecuária e árvores. Nos primeiros seis anos, o teor de matéria orgânica na camada de até 20 centímetros do solo passou de 1,8% para 2,8%. O aumento correspondeu à incorporação de mais de 11 toneladas de carbono orgânico por hectare. O resultado ambiental ocorreu junto com o aumento da produção. A produtividade do milho saiu de aproximadamente 80 para 180 sacas por hectare, enquanto a produção de carne passou de duas para até 16 arrobas por hectare. O caso mostra que a recuperação do solo e o aumento do estoque de carbono podem acompanhar a elevação da produtividade. Na pecuária, a Embrapa Gado de Corte desenvolveu os protocolos Carne Carbono Neutro e Carne Baixo Carbono. O primeiro utiliza árvores plantadas em sistemas integrados para compensar o metano liberado pelos bovinos durante a digestão. Experimentos indicaram que cerca de 200 árvores em crescimento por hectare podem armazenar carbono suficiente para neutralizar as emissões anuais de metano entérico de 11 bovinos adultos. Isso não significa, porém, que toda a propriedade seja automaticamente neutra. A conta completa precisa incluir fertilizantes, combustível, energia, manejo do solo e todas as demais fontes relevantes de gases de efeito estufa. Nas lavouras, outra frente de pesquisa utiliza microrganismos para reduzir a dependência de fertilizantes nitrogenados. A fixação biológica de nitrogênio, desenvolvida e aperfeiçoada no país por instituições como a Embrapa Agrobiologia e a Embrapa Soja, permite que bactérias associadas às raízes forneçam às plantas o nutriente retirado do ar. Na soja, essa tecnologia praticamente elimina a necessidade de aplicação de nitrogênio mineral. A Embrapa estima que a substituição do fertilizante pela ação das bactérias evite a emissão de aproximadamente 12 milhões de toneladas de dióxido de carbono equivalente por ano. A redução ocorre tanto na fabricação e no transporte do insumo quanto pela menor liberação de óxido nitroso no solo. Essas medições ganham importância com o avanço dos mercados de carbono. Nesse sistema, cada crédito representa, em regra, uma tonelada de dióxido de carbono equivalente que deixou de ser emitida ou foi removida da atmosfera. O ativo pode ser comprado por empresas que precisam cumprir obrigações legais ou que assumiram voluntariamente metas de red

artigo.texto: Advait Battery Ecosystem Private Limited, a subsidiary of BSE and NSE listed Advait Energy Transitions Limited, has entered into a Master Supply Agreement with HiTHIUM for the supply of lithium iron phosphate battery cells. The agreement will support Advait’s planned 2.5 GWh annual capacity cell to container Battery Energy Storage System assembly facility in Gujarat. HiTHIUM to supply 314 Ah LFP cells Under the agreement, HiTHIUM will supply its 314 Ah lithium iron phosphate prismatic cells to Advait. The arrangement is structured to support cell offtake of up to 1 GWh over the next year. It is expected to create a high volume supply framework as Advait scales domestic BESS assembly for utility scale, commercial and industrial and renewable energy applications in India. The cells will form part of Advait’s planned capabilities covering module and pack assembly, container integration and system commissioning. Advait building domestic BESS manufacturing capacity Advait’s 2.5 GWh BESS cell to container assembly facility is under development in Gangad, Gujarat. The facility is scheduled to begin commercial production soon. The company said the plant is being developed to serve grid scale energy storage, commercial and industrial applications and renewable energy integration projects. The Hithium agreement will provide a supply framework as the facility moves towards commercial production and volume manufacturing. Partnership strengthens integrated energy storage platform Advait said the agreement is part of its strategy to build an integrated battery energy storage manufacturing ecosystem in India. The company has also entered into a strategic collaboration with Adaptive Engineering for engineering design, Energy Management System architecture, PLC and SCADA systems and integration capabilities. With the latest agreement, Advait aims to combine cell sourcing, engineering, module and pack assembly, container integration and system commissioning under its domestic BESS platform. Advait Energy Transitions expands clean energy portfolio Advait Energy Transitions is a Gujarat based power and renewable energy company. Its portfolio includes battery energy storage manufacturing, green hydrogen project development, electrolyser manufacturing, fuel cell manufacturing and clean energy EPC services. The Hithium agreement supports the group’s wider expansion across energy transition technologies and related infrastructure.

artigo.texto: Em 2026, os parlamentares poderão deixar de cumprir certas regras fiscais ao proporem ou analisarem projetos que concedem benefícios tributários para Data Centers, programas de apoio a pessoas com câncer e com deficiência, áreas de livre comércio da Região Norte e resseguradoras brasileiras. É o que prevê a Lei Complementar 237, sancionada no dia (15.09.2026) pela Presidência da República, com um veto, e publicada no Diário Oficial da União. Criação de exceções às regras fiscais para setores determinados teve apoio do Executivo Entre as regras dispensadas para as propostas que reduzem tributos, estão: Criação de metas para o incentivo fiscal; Avaliação de seu custo-benefício; Limite em 2% do PIB. Várias dessas exigências haviam sido criadas em 2025 para frear o avanço de renúncias fiscais (cortes de impostos) e outras vantagens específicas para certos setores. A nova lei tem origem no Projeto de Lei Complementar (PLP) 74/2026, relatado no Senado pelo senador Camilo Santana (PT-CE). No relatório, Camilo diz que a medida é necessária para o “atendimento de demandas setoriais legítimas”. Ele lembra que tais incentivos fiscais devem estar previstos no Orçamento e que serão considerados para a meta do resultado primário — cálculo que monitora a saúde das contas públicas. Regras dispensadas Ao analisar os incentivos, os parlamentares poderão desconsiderar a vedação de ampliar isenções fiscais (prevista na Lei de Diretrizes Orçamentárias de 2026) e o limite de 2% do PIB para o total de benefícios tributários federais. Para 2026, o teto equivale a cerca de R$ 274,2 bi, segundo cálculo de 2025 do Planalto. Os senadores e deputados também ficam dispensados de: Estimar o impacto orçamentário-financeiro; Reavaliar a receita prevista na lei orçamentária; Prever a arrecadação do mesmo valor de outra forma, como compensação; Estimar a quantidade de beneficiários, entre outras normas. A maior parte das restrições flexibilizadas estavam previstas na Lei Complementar 224, de 2025, que determinou um corte linear de 10% em benefícios fiscais federais. Ela é fruto de discussões encabeçadas pelo Executivo para rever os valores que deixa de arrecadar. Em 2025, a Receita Federal projetou que os incentivos fiscais poderiam chegar a R$ 612,8 bilhões em 2026. Beneficiadas A norma viabiliza o Regime Especial de Tributação para Serviços de Datacenter (Redata), sancionado nesta quarta-feira (16.09.2026) para estimular a instalação desses estabelecimentos no país, principalmente os que tenham como foco a computação em nuvem e a inteligência artificial (IA). Os Data Centers (locais que guardam os sistemas de computação de uma empresa) são considerados estratégicos e cada vez mais demandados no mundo, segundo especialistas ouvidos no Senado. As novas regras também abarcam os seguintes incentivos fiscais: do Programa Nacional de Apoio à Atenção Oncológica (Pronon) e do Programa Nacional de Apoio à Atenção da Saúde da Pessoa com Deficiência (Pronas/PCD). Criados em 2012, os programas permitem deduzir doações do Imposto de Renda; às empresas habilitadas nas áreas de livre comércio, atualmente localizadas no Acre, Amapá, Amazonas, Rondônia e Roraima. Com menos impostos, o regime tributário busca impulsionar a economia de cidades fronteiriças; às resseguradoras locais (sediadas no Brasil), com relação à desoneração de Imposto sobre a Renda das Pessoas Jurídicas e da Contribuição Social sobre o Lucro Líquido. A resseguradora é uma empresa que funciona como “seguro das seguradoras”, assumindo parte dos riscos de seus negócios. Veto O governo federal vetou trecho que livrava municípios de até 65 mil habitantes de comprovar que não havia atraso nas suas dívidas com a União para receber transferências voluntárias de recursos federais. Atualmente 90,5% dos 5.570 municípios se enquadrariam na regra, segundo estimativa de julho do IBGE. Para o Planalto, a medida desincentivaria a boa gestão dos recursos públicos. artigo.texto: Rússia ataca maior operadora de telefonia móvel da Ucrânia e atinge data centers Cerca de 100 mil residências em Kiev tiveram os serviços interrompidos Internacional|Da Reuters LEIA AQUI O RESUMO DA NOTÍCIA Produzido pela Ri7a - a Inteligência Artificial do R7 A Rússia atacou neste domingo (27) a sede da Kyivstar, maior operadora de telefonia móvel da Ucrânia, informou a empresa à mídia local, enquanto Moscou seguia com bombardeios a data centers e infraestrutura de comunicações ucranianos. A Kyivstar informou à agência de notícias Interfax Ucrânia que sua sede em Kiev havia sido atingida, mas não houve vítimas. O Ministério da Defesa da Rússia também informou neste domingo que atingiu um data center pertencente à Vodafone Ucrânia, segunda maior operadora de telefonia celular do país. A Vodafone Ucrânia não respondeu a um pedido de comentário. O presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelensky, afirmou que a Rússia atacou um data center em Kiev duas vezes na manhã deste domingo, ferindo duas crianças e um adulto. Veja Também Moscou também atingiu data centers pertencentes a provedores de internet ucranianos na semana passada, causando interrupções no serviço para cerca de 100 mil residências em Kiev e na região circundante, de acordo com o Ministério Digital da Ucrânia. “A Rússia tem como alvo os principais data centers ucranianos, buscando interromper o fluxo de informações. Alertas rápidos sobre ameaças de mísseis e drones são essenciais -- eles salvam vidas”, escreveu o ministro das Relações Exteriores da Ucrânia, Andrii Sybiha, no X na quarta-feira. artigo.texto: Arcadis innovates with sustainable solutions for data centers: engineering that transforms digital infrastructure. The company is embracing advanced technologies and energy efficiency to build sustainable data centers, reducing environmental impact and driving global digital transformation. São Paulo – As demand for digital infrastructure grows, data center energy consumption and environmental performance are receiving greater attention. With the goal of creating innovative and efficient solutions, Arcadis, a global leader in sustainable design, engineering, and consulting, is adopting technologies that combine sustainability, energy efficiency, and high performance in its projects. With the acceleration of digitalization, data centers can consume up to 50 times more energy than commercial buildings of the same size, accounting for up to 3% of global electricity consumption, according to industry data. Arcadis sees the transition to more sustainable digital infrastructure as both an environmental imperative and a smart business strategy. The company believes it is possible to combine high performance with technological innovation while reducing carbon emissions. “The growing demand for cleaner and more resilient digital infrastructure has driven a true revolution in data center design. At Arcadis, we combine our expertise in engineering and sustainability to support clients in building more efficient, future-ready solutions with a lower environmental impact. Arcadis’ approach to data centers takes a systemic, one-stop-shop view, which also addresses the challenges of electrical connections, water supply, and fiber,” says Isabel Rando, head of industry solutions at Arcadis. Innovative solutions for energy efficiency Arcadis has implemented various technologies to increase data center efficiency and minimize environmental impact. Key solutions include: - Energy and water optimization: Both are fundamental resources for data center operations, particularly in the pursuit of sustainability and net-zero goals. As major priorities for clients in the technology sector, the efficient use of these resources is becoming increasingly essential in data center deployment projects. - Smart environmental monitoring: Technologies that expand the thermal operating range of equipment without compromising durability, in accordance with American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE) guidelines. This approach helps reduce energy consumption in cooling systems. - Use of battery energy storage systems (BESS): Replacing diesel generators with energy storage batteries contributes to data center decarbonization while providing greater efficiency and energy autonomy. Independent and strategic engineering for data centers In addition to technological solutions, Arcadis offers specialized independent engineering and owner’s engineering services, ensuring that projects meet clients’ technical, timeline, financial, and operational objectives. Through a strategic and impartial approach, the company helps protect the owner’s interests while treating sustainability, health, and safety as non-negotiable priorities. It also supports the minimization of technical and financial risks, strategic schedule management to meet project milestones, and alignment with industry best practices and client quality standards. A prime example of how Arcadis applies its innovative solutions is SINES DC in Portugal. With a capacity of 1.2 GW and 100% renewable energy, SINES DC is one of the largest data center campuses in Europe. The facility uses seawater cooling systems, taking advantage of its strategic location on the Portuguese coast to optimize energy efficiency and reduce its carbon footprint. “Arcadis is at the forefront of the transformation of data centers, delivering sustainable and innovative solutions to the challenges of digital transformation. With projects across various regions, such as Latin America and Europe, Arcadis leads the way in creating more efficient, resilient, and environmentally responsible digital infrastructure,” concludes Isabel. Accelerating a positive future for the planet.

According to the latest IndexBox report on the global Natural Graphite Anode Material market, the market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals, more disciplined procurement behavior, and a more regionally diversified supply architecture. The global natural graphite anode material (NGAM) market is positioned for transformative growth over the 2026-2035 forecast period, underpinned by the relentless expansion of lithium-ion battery megafactory capacity for electric vehicles and grid-scale energy storage. As the primary active anode ingredient in most commercial lithium-ion cells, NGAM sits at the core of the energy transition, and its demand trajectory is tightly linked to battery production volumes. China currently hosts over 70% of global NGAM processing capacity, spanning spheronization, purification, and carbon coating, creating a pronounced supply concentration that is reshaping trade policy and investment incentives worldwide. Prices for coated spherical graphite fell 30-40% during the 2023-2024 correction, resetting the pricing base for 2026 and compressing margins while opening volume demand from cost-sensitive battery segments. The market is bifurcating into standard-purity CSPG for LFP batteries and premium grades for high-energy NMC cells, with the former growing faster in tonnage. Environmental compliance costs and synthetic graphite substitution remain key challenges, but the overall outlook points to robust expansion through 2035. The baseline scenario for the natural graphite anode material market anticipates sustained double-digit growth through 2035, with a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of approximately 18% in volume terms. This outlook assumes continued global EV adoption, supportive government policies, and the gradual diversification of supply chains outside China. Demand will be primarily driven by lithium-ion battery production for electric vehicles, which account for the largest share of NGAM consumption, followed by stationary energy storage systems. The market is expected to see a shift toward higher-purity, coated spherical graphite as battery manufacturers demand improved performance and consistency. Supply-side constraints, including permitting delays and capital intensity for new purification plants outside China, may tighten availability in the short term, but ongoing investments in North America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific are expected to alleviate these bottlenecks by the late 2020s. Pricing is forecast to stabilize after the 2023-2024 correction, with gradual increases as demand outpaces supply. The market index, with 2025 as the base year (100), is projected to reach 450 by 2035, reflecting a 4.5-fold expansion. Key risks include accelerated synthetic graphite substitution, slower-than-expected EV adoption, and geopolitical trade disruptions. However, the fundamental demand drivers remain strong, and the market is poised for significant growth. Electric vehicle batteries represent the dominant end-use sector for natural graphite anode material, accounting for the majority of global demand. As automakers ramp up production of EVs to meet emissions targets and consumer demand, the need for anode materials surges. Natural graphite, particularly coated spherical graphite, is favored for its cost advantage and improving performance. Through 2035, this segment will expand as new gigafactories come online in North America, Europe, and Asia. Demand-side indicators include EV sales volumes, battery pack sizes, and the mix of battery chemistries (LFP vs. NMC). The shift toward higher nickel chemistries may slightly reduce graphite intensity per kWh, but overall volume growth remains robust. Major trends include vertical integration by OEMs, localization of supply chains, and the development of fast-charging batteries requiring advanced anode materials. Current trend: Growing rapidly. Major trends: Rapid EV sales growth in China, Europe, and North America, Increasing battery pack sizes for longer range, Shift toward LFP batteries in entry-level EVs, boosting natural graphite demand, Localization of battery supply chains driven by policy incentives, and Development of fast-charging batteries requiring high-performance anodes. Representative participants: Tesla, Volkswagen, General Motors, Ford, BYD, and Hyundai. Grid-scale energy storage systems are a fast-growing end-use sector for natural graphite anode material, driven by the global transition to renewable energy and the need for grid stability. Lithium-ion batteries dominate this segment, and natural graphite anodes offer a cost-effective solution for large-scale storage. Through 2035, demand will be propelled by utility procurement of storage capacity, government mandates for renewable integration, and falling battery costs. Key demand indicators include renewable energy capacity additions, storage duration requirements, and policy support. The segment favors LFP batteries, which use natural graphite anodes, due to their safety and cycle life. Major trends include the rise of long-duration storage, the use of second-life EV batteries, and the development of specialized anode materials for stationary applications. Current trend: Accelerating. Major trends: Rapid growth in renewable energy installations requiring storage, Government auctions and mandates for grid-scale storage, Declining battery costs making storage economically viable, Shift toward LFP chemistry for stationary storage, and Development of long-duration storage technologies. Representative participants: Tesla, Fluence, Sungrow, BYD, LG Energy Solution, and Samsung SDI. artigo.texto: Energy Vault adds gigawatt-scale BESS acquisition to portfolio | Projects Weekly AWM provides tailored cable management solutions for PV and BESS that are durable and reliable. This week on Projects Weekly, Energy Vault has acquired more than 2.3 GW of BESS projects from Goshe Energy Storage in a consequential deal for the U.S. energy sector. In Arizona, GridStor has closed a debt financing package for its White Tank project with a number of investment partners. NorthStar Clean Energy’s Hart Solar Project finished construction in Michigan last week, supplying more than 200 GWh of renewable energy across the Mitten State. Slightly southwest in central Illinois, PureSky Energy launched its first community solar farm in the Land of Lincoln. In Colorado, Cloudbreak Energy Partners and NORD/LB closed on financing for the Pueblo Battery Resource installation in the Black Hills, and Apex and Meta agreed to a seventh solar-related deal in Texas. Finally, Madison Energy Infrastructure announced a new community solar initiative with help from partners across the U.S. Keep reading for all the details and more! GridStor and investment partners close debt financing for Arizona battery project Utility-scale battery energy storage system (BESS) developer GridStor has secured a debt financing agreement worth $220 million for development of its White Tank project in Arizona. Signed in conjunction with KeyBanc Capital Markets, ING Capital, and Zions Capital Markets, the financing will go toward construction of 100 MW / 400 MWh of renewable energy for the Grand Canyon State. Aiming for a 2027 energization date, the project will operate within a 20-year tolling agreement with Arizona Public Service, the state’s largest electrical utility. “We are proud to work with three distinguished financial partners to complete the financing of the White Tank Reliability Project,” says Chris Taylor, CEO, GridStor. “Trusted partnerships like these are critical for advancing large-scale power supply and infrastructure to meet surging demand for new power capacity. We thank ING, KeyBanc Capital Markets, and Zions for placing their trust in us.” Bright spot: The financial close marks GridStor’s fourth major financing milestone over the past year. The company now boasts a project pipeline of more than 3 GW of battery storage projects either in late-stage development or under construction across much of the U.S. Filipe Barreto, director of ING, says the growth of renewable energy, especially batteries, provides a prime opportunity for investment banking firms like his. “The rapid growth of renewable generation is driving increasing demand for energy storage solutions, making BESS assets an integral part of energy infrastructure and one of the primary themes in energy financing,” he says. “This transaction reflects ING’s confidence in the sector and our commitment to financing energy infrastructure that enhances grid reliability and supports the transition to a lower-carbon energy future. We look forward to building on this success with GridStor.” Hart Solar Project comes online in Michigan NorthStar Clean Energy has announced the completion of the Hart Solar Project, a new 120 MW utility-scale solar installation in Oceana County, Michigan. Officials expect the new installation will generate more than 200 GWh of electricity every year, powering more than 21,000 homes throughout the Mitten State. The project will avoid about 96,000 metric tons of carbon emissions each year, officials add, operating through power purchase agreements with Executive Energy Services and the Michigan Public Power Agency (MPPA) to serve customers across the region. “Hart Solar is an important investment in Michigan’s energy future and demonstrates how strong partnerships can help deliver clean energy solutions to communities across our state,” says Brian Hartmann, president and CEO of NorthStar Clean Energy. “By working with organizations like Executive Energy Services and MPPA, we’re helping meet customer energy goals while strengthening Michigan’s energy infrastructure with additional renewable generation.” Bright spot: The new project also aims to strengthen the state’s communities through a number of economic investments and partnerships. NorthStar officials say the project created more than 300 construction jobs, making “significant contributions” to the state’s economy throughout its development. “Oakland County and small businesses across Michigan are expected to save on electric supply charges through the Hart Solar Project,” says Robert Bernardi of Executive Energy Services. “Through a partnership with NorthStar Clean Energy, Oakland Schools and 45 other public school districts statewide are projected to save approximately $25 million over a 10-year agreement. “These savings will allow schools to redirect funds toward students, staff, and core educational priorities while advancing their clean energy goals.” Cloudbreak Energy closes financing for Pueblo Battery Resource project Energy developer and IPP Cloudbreak Energy Partners and NORD/LB have closed on $60 million in construction financing for the Pueblo Battery Resource energy storage project in Colorado. The 50 MW / 200 MWh storage installation will be the first of its kind built in Black Hills mountain range territory, according to representatives. The project also marks Cloudbreak’s first foray into battery storage as a whole, which the company says paves the way for future storage development. “This financing demonstrates Cloudbreak’s ability to finance and deliver on grid-scale storage assets,” says Alec Shobe, COO of Cloudbreak Energy. “Nord was the right partner for us on this deal, bringing both thoughtful deal structuring and storage-financing expertise to get Pueblo Battery Resource to this milestone. artigo.texto: SpaceX (SPCX) está prestes a levar uma carga muito interessante para a órbita: chips de IA de um de seus maiores rivais. De acordo com uma postagem amplamente compartilhada no X, a Alphabet (GOOG) está lançando os TPUs do Google (os chips personalizados que ela constrói para executar IA) nesta semana em um Falcon 9 da SpaceX para testar data centers de IA em órbita. A resposta de Elon Musk? "A quantidade de computação no espaço obviamente será arredondada para 100% de toda a computação." (Sem hesitação!) Para os investidores da SpaceX, porém, o mais importante é quem está comprando a viagem. Escrevi no início desta semana sobre o cronograma agressivo de Musk para a Lua e Marte. Mas esta parece ser uma daquelas semanas em que décadas acontecem – porque a computação orbital oficialmente não é mais uma aposta exclusiva da SpaceX. A concorrência está pagando para entrar nela. A SpaceX é paga de qualquer maneira Pense na situação aqui. A SpaceX tem seu próprio negócio de IA (olá, Grok). O Google é um de seus rivais mais ferozes em IA. E quando o Google quis testar seus chips em órbita, foi à SpaceX para o lançamento. Se a Coca-Cola tivesse que enviar todas as latas nos caminhões da Pepsi, você gostaria de ser dono da empresa de transporte. A mesma ideia aqui. Quer o Grok ou o Gemini vença a IA no espaço, os chips têm que chegar lá de alguma forma. (Por que o espaço? A versão curta é energia. Na órbita certa, os painéis solares recebem luz solar quase constante, e você não precisa esperar na fila por um espaço em uma rede elétrica lotada.) E o Google já está aumentando os gastos... Como você pode ver, o CapEx está aumentando rapidamente. Mesmo uma pequena fração indo para a órbita seria importante para quem estiver fazendo o lançamento. Vamos testar esses 100 GW Fica maior. O CFO da SpaceX diz que a empresa está no caminho para implantar 100 GW de computação orbital a cada ano até o final da década. Enquanto isso, a FCC aceitou o pedido da SpaceX para implantar até 100.000 satélites Starlink Gen3 para arquivamento em 18 de setembro. E Musk adicionou um detalhe importante: "Cada satélite tem 250 kW e terá um computador Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 projetado pela SpaceX." Então, aqui está uma conta rápida de guardanapo: 100.000 satélites × 250 kW cada = 25 GW. Essa é toda a constelação Gen3 proposta... e é apenas um quarto do que o CFO diz que a SpaceX implantará a cada ano. Mesmo que as cargas úteis provavelmente fiquem maiores... ainda são muitos foguetes. E a SpaceX é dona dos foguetes. A NVIDIA também está pegando carona Observe o que Musk diz que vai dentro de cada um desses satélites: um computador construído com chips da NVIDIA (NVDA). A Nvidia já surfou o boom dos data centers no solo para um grande crescimento de receita... Se Musk estiver mesmo parcialmente certo, a órbita se torna outro mercado para esses chips. Eu chamaria isso de um bom bônus para os acionistas da Nvidia. Aqui está o problema Claro, um lançamento de teste do Falcon 9 é um contrato minúsculo. A computação orbital pode permanecer experimental por anos, e a receita da SpaceX pode não mostrar muito disso até bem depois do final da década. E a SpaceX vai precisar de toda a ajuda que puder obter para atender às expectativas de crescimento dos analistas e manter sua avaliação extraordinariamente rica. Quanto a mim, estou confortável em ficar de fora por enquanto. Há muito risco de execução em jogo aqui, mas a oportunidade, francamente, é enorme. E se você quiser modelar essa oportunidade com mais precisão, pode construir com a ferramenta de modelagem proprietária do TIKR.com, que requer apenas três entradas, para obter um modelo financeiro completo para o que a ação da SpaceX poderia valer em três anos. artigo.texto: WEG aumenta a aposta em SC e eleva investimento para R$ 330 milhões em megafábrica de baterias A empresa destacou que a ampliação do projeto da planta em Itajaí faz parte da estratégia da companhia de apoiar o crescimento do mercado de armazenamento de energia no Brasil WEG aumenta a aposta em SC e eleva investimento para R$ 330 milhões em megafábrica de bateriasFoto: WEG/Divulgação/ND Mais A WEG anunciou, nesta sexta-feira (25) a ampliação do projeto de sua nova fábrica de sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias, chamado BESS, em construção em Itajaí, no Litoral Norte de Santa SC. Anunciada em fevereiro deste ano, a nova fábrica terá um investimento total estimado de R$ 330 milhões e capacidade anual de 4 GWh, atendendo à demanda crescente por soluções associadas à transição energética, com início das operações previsto para o segundo semestre de 2027. A empresa destacou que o movimento faz parte da estratégia da companhia de apoiar o crescimento do mercado de armazenamento de energia no Brasil, na iminência do primeiro Leilão de Reserva de Capacidade Armazenamento Nacional, a ser realizado em dezembro de 2026, o projeto atualizado incorpora maior nível de automação e ganhos de eficiência industrial que permitirão ampliar a capacidade produtiva. WEG acredita na forte expansão do mercado de energia “O mercado de armazenamento de energia vive um momento de forte expansão, impulsionado pelo crescimento das fontes renováveis e pela necessidade crescente de maior flexibilidade e segurança para o sistema elétrico. A ampliação deste projeto demonstra a capacidade da WEG de adaptar rapidamente seus investimentos para atender às necessidades do mercado e apoiar o desenvolvimento sustentável do setor energético brasileiro”, Manfred Peter Johann, Vice-Presidente de Automação e Sistemas da WEG. A empresa destacou que a ampliação do projeto da planta em Itajaí faz parte da estratégia da companhia de apoiar o crescimento do mercado de armazenamento de energia no BrasilFoto: WEG/Divulgação/ND Mais O BESS desempenha papel fundamental nos sistemas elétricos modernos, principalmente na integração das fontes renováveis como solar e eólica, permitindo armazenar energia nos momentos de maior disponibilidade e disponibilizá-la quando necessário. Essa flexibilidade contribui para a estabilidade do sistema elétrico, maior eficiência operacional e aproveitamento dos recursos energéticos. Cláudio Costa é editor-chefe do ND Mais na redação de Itajaí, de onde coordena a equipe local e escreve sobre política, segurança pública, economia e temas relacionados à comunidade. Entre as cidades que cobre estão Balneário Camboriú, Itajaí, Navegantes, Penha e Bombinhas, assim como todo o Litoral Norte de Santa Catarina. Bacharel em Comunicação Social pela Faculdade Ielusc (Instituto Superior e Centro Educacional Luterano), atua no jornalismo desde 2007 e aprofunda suas matérias utilizando sua formação em investigação criminal e perícia criminal. Possui especializações em marketing digital e inteligência artificial, garantindo uma abordagem moderna e informada. Trabalhou nas eleições de 2012 e 2014 como editor no Jornal ND, em Joinville. artigo.texto: The nights are drawing in, there’s an autumnal chill in the air and shipping companies are preparing to surrender emissions allowances. The deadline to surrender allowances for the EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS) is fast approaching and it is important for parties to act now to avoid penalties for non-compliance. EU ETS surrender deadline is just days away Emissions trading schemes, most significantly the EU ETS, set a cap-and-trade system requiring companies from the maritime sector and other industries, to surrender European Union Allowances (EUAs) to offset their annual emissions. The EU ETS requires EUAs to be submitted by 30 September. An annual obligation for maritime companies since 2024, this year, shipping companies must surrender EUAs to cover 70% of reported emissions from 2025. Starting next year, EUAs will need to be surrendered to cover 100% of reported emissions. Don’t leave yourself open to liability: The 30 September deadline is only for the EU ETS. The equivalent UK legislation doesn’t require allowances to be surrendered until 30 April with special measures covering 2026 and 2027 emissions so no surrender is required until 2028. Looking at EU, responsible shipping companies The “shipping company” is responsible for surrendering the right numbers of EUAs. In cases where a ship manager has signed a mandate taking on the responsibility for the “shipping company,” they will have assumed responsibility for EU ETS obligations. Such managers must ensure that sufficient EUAs are transferred into their holding accounts in good time to surrender to the EU. The administrative process for receipt and then surrendering allowances is not always instantaneous, and any delay in procurement or transfer could leave managers exposed. Any managers carrying an EU ETS mandate should already know where their EUAs are coming from or, preferably, have any required EUAs in hand. Otherwise, urgent action will be needed to meet the 30 September deadline. Absent allowances The industry has become more accustomed to EU ETS, the rhythm of the reporting cycle and agreeing clauses in charters, MOAs and ship management agreements. This, however, has led some into complacency with delays in EUAs being transferred from charterers to managers/owners – often despite specific language in the relevant charterparty. While the deadline was a distant thought parties were willing to give one another leeway but, now that it approaches, attitudes are hardening. Although the registered shipping company will almost invariably have some contractual right of recovery against the charterer or the owner, in the case of ship managers, it also remains the entity liable under the EU ETS. The consequences of failing to surrender EUAs on time are severe. A penalty of €100 per allowance, adjusted for inflation, is levied and the shipping company must still surrender the EUAs next year. Persistent defaults can even result in an expulsion order effectively barring the vessel from entering European ports. Shipping companies must ensure that the requisite EUAs are surrendered by the deadline, even if that means purchasing allowances at their own cost and pursuing reimbursement separately.

artigo.texto: Chillicothe — Mayor Luke Feeney discusses the data center issue and the city’s powers concerning it, as well as other considerations about developments at the former paper mill, in an interview. With concerns about data centers in the news – and friction over allowing the “data hall” proposed by Alignment Engine Inc. on the “Chilpaco Innovation Campus,” I asked him for a sit-down interview. This was an offer to respond to Portia Boulger, founder of “Appalachians Against Data Centers,” who had confronted Feeney and other city officials over the February letter the city sent to the developer of the proposed “data hall.” Feeney declined that response, and instead he and I spoke about the data center and the city. Our interview is below, in three parts. He also soon produced a Facebook Reel video where he more thoroughly explained the city’s powers regarding zoning and other regulations: “This short video lays out the facts and timeline as clearly as possible. My goal being to provide the public with accurate information, explain the process, and make clear the difference between a discussion or inquiry, a zoning interpretation, a formal application, an approval, and actual construction. “Relevant documents can be found at this link.” Chillicothe Council will be meeting in the Main Annex of the Chillicothe and Ross County Public Library, behind 140 South Paint Street, at 7pm on Monday, September 28th. - He won’t comment on stories, but will comment on the process - Developing the “Universal Development Code (UDC, which replaced zoning and other powers) was a 19-month process - Regretfully, the process did not touch on data centers - 2025 was a “roller coaster of a year” - The “zoning certification letter” regarding the possibility of a data center - It was not zoning approval or permission to proceed - Such question and letter is almost always a first step - He wishes the data center issue was as big then as now, because they would have considered it in the UDC - The state was still giving out incentives for data centers, until May 2026 - The city did not get any other communications on the proposed data center between February 20th and the July 2 announcement - The city hired legal counsel to advise them, then created the moratorium - He wishes the moratorium had gone to committee for further review - There are still no formal communications about the proposed data center - There was only the email question from the developer - That means the city can’t say yes or no - City’s rules still cover industrial zones: setback, sound, etc. - The February letter is a typical hypothetical request, the start of a conversation - The Universal Development Code was meant to be updated, and has been once already - No matter what happens, data center regulation will go into the UDC - The February letter was very generic, and was sent in an email so it was dated by the email - Again, not want to address Portia Boulger’s statements - What is his perspective on the proposed paper mill development, including restarting The Chief? - The legal procedurals should be looked at completely separate from community impact by actual proposed development - The city has an absolute obligation to apply zoning rules - There are lots of proposals at the paper mill – he is excited about any opportunity to being back jobs - The proposals are speculative, and can’t be guaranteed - The city needs to be responsible about zoning, but also be supporting about jobs and business development - Zoning is city-wide – rules should be applied the same everywhere; can’t spot zone - Could there be a better solution than what has happened and is proposed? - Considering the speed of purchase, moving equipment in, the energy, conversations – better than expected - April 15th, 2025: his birthday, and paper mill closing announced - Across Ohio, paper mills have been closed for decades - His role is to be excited, supported, enthusiastic, and trust…but verify - He must budget for next year – but can’t budget city revenue on income tax from proposed jobs - 350 more people would mean more income tax – but can’t bet on - The city must be reserved, needs to see receipts - But what about claims of backstage deals and corrupt officials? ; ) - Data centers have been controversial – other than covid, he has not seen anything evolve so quickly - The state was incentivizing data centers through May - Similar to the seeming overpopulation of solar fields and windmills? - There is no solid data – only a presentation – is a proposal, a promise - We are all here to do the best for the city - This topic been so confusing, has created confusion, and challenges in communication has added to the confusion - The goal of the moratorium was to slow down the process and listen to the community - There is excitement around the paper mill redevelopment, but uncertainty around the data center - And then my camera battery died

artigo.texto: A Rússia bombardeou a sede da Kyivstar, maior operadora de telefonia da Ucrânia, e data centers da Vodafone e de provedores locais em Kiev. Os ataques causaram ferimentos em três pessoas e deixaram cerca de 100 mil residências sem acesso à internet. O presidente Volodymyr Zelensky confirmou os impactos na infraestrutura de comunicação, enquanto o governo russo alega que ataca infraestrutura militar e de dados para interromper o fluxo de informações ucraniano. A Rússia atacou neste domingo (27) a sede da Kyivstar, a maior operadora de telefonia móvel da Ucrânia, informou a empresa à mídia local. O ataque ocorreu enquanto Moscou seguia com bombardeios contra data centers e infraestrutura de comunicações ucranianos. A Kyivstar confirmou à agência de notícias Interfax Ucrânia que sua sede em Kiev havia sido atingida, mas não houve vítimas fatais. Ataques à infraestrutura de dados O Ministério da Defesa da Rússia também informou neste domingo que atingiu um data center pertencente à Vodafone Ucrânia, a segunda maior operadora de telefonia celular do país. A Vodafone Ucrânia não respondeu a um pedido de comentário sobre o ocorrido. Impacto nas telecomunicações e alerta internacional - Alvo estratégico: A sede da Kyivstar, líder do mercado de telefonia ucraniano, foi atingida em Kiev. - Vítimas: O presidente Zelensky afirmou que o ataque a um data center feriu duas crianças e um adulto. - Queda de serviço: Cerca de 100 mil residências em Kiev ficaram sem internet após os bombardeios da semana passada. - Segurança digital: O chanceler ucraniano alertou que interromper data centers busca silenciar alertas de mísseis que salvam vidas. - Contexto: Moscou alega atacar infraestrutura militar, mas críticos veem uma ofensiva contra a conectividade civil. O presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelensky, afirmou que a Rússia atacou um data center em Kiev duas vezes na manhã deste domingo, ferindo duas crianças e um adulto. Moscou também atingiu data centers pertencentes a provedores de internet ucranianos na semana passada, causando interrupções no serviço para cerca de 100 mil residências em Kiev e na região circundante, de acordo com o Ministério Digital da Ucrânia. A Rússia tem como alvo os principais data centers ucranianos, buscando interromper o fluxo de informações. Alertas rápidos sobre ameaças de mísseis e drones são essenciais -- eles salvam vidas, escreveu o ministro das Relações Exteriores da Ucrânia, Andrii Sybiha, no X na quarta-feira (23).

artigo.texto: Volkswagen Group, PowerCo and Gotion deepen strategic partnership. Valencia to be developed into European production hub for LFP batteries - The companies are expanding their long-standing strategic partnership to include the industrial production of LFP battery cells and cathode active materials. - Accelerated development of a regional battery supply chain for Europe through the establishment of joint ventures at the Valencia (Spain), Šurany (Slovak Republic) and Kenitra (Morocco) sites. - Valencia to be developed into European production hub for LFP batteries. - Thomas Schmall: “Gotion has been a close partner of the Volkswagen Group for many years. We are now expanding our partnership into joint industrial production of LFP batteries to strengthen Europe’s battery industry. This marks a major breakthrough for both companies.” Salzgitter/Hefei/Valencia. Volkswagen Group, PowerCo SE and Gotion High-tech have agreed to deepen their strategic partnership and jointly accelerate the development of a regional battery supply chain for Europe. Building on their cooperation since 2020, the partners agreed on establishing three joint ventures at the Valencia (Spain), Šurany (Slovak Republic) and Kenitra (Morocco) sites for the industrial production of LFP battery cells and cathode material. The agreement also covers joint procurement and sales activities in Europe. Separately, Volkswagen Group has announced that it has entered into definitive agreements to sell 5.3 % equity stake in Gotion to optimize equity structures and support long-term strategic synergies. Upon completion of the transaction, Volkswagen will continue to hold a significant stake in Gotion. LFP batteries offer competitive costs, a long service life and high levels of robustness, making them a key technology for affordable electric mobility in the volume segment. Demand in Europe is expected to grow strongly in the coming years: According to forecasts, LFP’s market share could rise from around 10 percent today to between 40 and 60 percent by 2030. At the same time, Europe currently has no relevant LFP battery production capacity. The partnership with Gotion strengthens Europe’s position in the global LFP battery market. Together, the partners will expand regional LFP battery production, diversify sources of supply for key cathode active materials, and thereby strengthen supply security and the competitiveness of the European battery industry. Thomas Schmall, Member of the Board of Management of Volkswagen Group for Technology and Chairman of the Supervisory Board of PowerCo SE: “I am delighted that we are expanding our long-standing partnership with Gotion into the joint industrial production of LFP batteries to strengthen Europe’s battery industry. This marks a major breakthrough for both companies and brings us one step closer to the forefront of electric mobility. Volkswagen is the first European automotive manufacturer to cover the entire battery value chain, from development and cathode materials through to production.” Li Zhen, Chairman of Gotion Hith-tech: “Six years of close collaboration between Volkswagen and Gotion have built deep mutual trust and a relationship that empowers both sides—one that has long since moved beyond ordinary business to become a partnership bound by a shared future. Today, together with Volkswagen Group and PowerCo, we are accelerating our global strategic cooperation. Through cross-shareholdings and three joint sites, we are anchoring our shared strategy to localise battery production in Europe, racing to seize the opportunities of global electric mobility, and jointly forging a new paradigm of world-class, win-win cooperation in the lithium battery industry.” Frank Blome, CEO of PowerCo SE: “Volkswagen and PowerCo are building Europe’s battery industry. The partnership with Gotion is the next milestone on this path: It strengthens the resilience of our value chain, accelerates industrialization and combines PowerCo’s capabilities with the strengths of a long-standing partner.” Diversifying the battery supply chain Volkswagen Group, PowerCo and Gotion have been working closely and successfully together since 2020. Gotion is both a cell supplier to the Volkswagen Group and a strategic partner of PowerCo. With the new joint ventures, the partners are strategically expanding this proven cooperation into the industrial production of LFP battery cells and cathode active material. Across the three sites, they will also share investments and industrial responsibilities. The agreement therefore supports Volkswagen Group’s long-term plans to establish a European battery supply chain and strengthens PowerCo’s growth plan. - Valencia / Spain: LFP battery cells The PowerCo gigafactory currently under construction in Valencia is envisaged to be transferred to a joint venture. The agreement provides for PowerCo to hold a 51 percent stake in the joint venture and to remain the majority shareholder. The joint venture is intended to be jointly managed by PowerCo and Gotion. One major goal is to develop the site into a European production hub for Unified Cells based on LFP technology. The planned investments and job creation measures remain as announced. - Šurany / Slovak Republic: LFP battery cells The Gotion cell factory in Šurany is intended to be transferred to a joint venture. The agreement provides for Gotion to hold a 51 percent stake in the joint venture and to remain the majority shareholder. The joint venture is intended to be jointly managed by PowerCo and Gotion, with a focus on LFP cells for both EV applications and energy storage systems (ESS). - Kenitra / Morocco: LFP cathode material The joint venture in Kenitra is planning to establish a new production facility to produce cathode material for LFP batteries. artigo.texto: A Associação Brasileira de Geradoras Termelétricas (Abraget) demonstrou preocupação com a possibilidade de o decreto que regulamentará o Regime Especial de Tributação para Serviços de Data Centers (Redata) ser publicado sem a inclusão do gás natural entre as fontes de energia elegíveis aos projetos. Isso porque, segundo a entidade, o gás natural oferece geração firme, em complementaridade às fontes renováveis, cuja produção varia conforme as condições climáticas. ‘ Em nota, a Abraget aponta que ‘a operação ininterrupta dos data centers, especialmente para serviços em nuvem e aplicações de inteligência artificial, exige elevada confiabilidade no fornecimento de energia. A inclusão do gás natural contribui, ainda, para a eficiência logística e econômica dos empreendimentos”, disse a associação. A exclusão da fonte iria na ‘contramão do que foi aprovado pelo Congresso Nacional’, segundo a Abraget, estimando um aumento no custo da conta de luz de aproximadamente R$ 7 bilhões. “Além de ter que recorrer ao gás e outras fontes nos momentos sem geração renovável, a regra prevê a criação de novas fontes intermitentes, que não vão entregar a energia fixa que as unidades de processamento de dados exigem”, disse em nota. Ouça também: As pontas soltas do Redata e a corrida por acesso à rede Além disso, como a geração renovável está concentrada no Nordeste, a associação aponta que será necessário realizar investimentos expressivos em transmissão para atender projetos nas regiões Sul e Sudeste, com possibilidade de repasse desses custos ao consumidor. Caso isso não ocorra, projetos de data centers nessas regiões podem se tornar inviáveis. “A Abraget defende uma matriz elétrica equilibrada, na qual os atributos de cada fonte são utilizados e, portanto, atendendo à complementaridade prevista no Redata. A associação reitera que o gás natural é essencial para a segurança e a viabilidade dos projetos de data centers”, ressalta a nota da associação.

artigo.texto: India and the European Union discussed strengthening cooperation in the power and energy sectors during a bilateral meeting held in New Delhi on September 24, 2026. Minister of State for Power and New and Renewable Energy Shri Shripad Naik met a delegation from the European Parliament’s Committee on Industry, Research and Energy (ITRE) to review ongoing cooperation and explore new areas of collaboration. The discussions covered energy security, power sector transformation, low-carbon development, nuclear energy, carbon markets and emerging technologies. Both sides also discussed the broader momentum in India-EU relations, including progress on the India-EU Free Trade Agreement. Shri Shripad Naik highlighted India’s ongoing transformation of its power sector and efforts to develop a resilient, reliable and future-ready energy system. He pointed to the country’s expansion of non-fossil fuel capacity and progress towards its climate commitments ahead of the targeted timeline. The Minister also highlighted developments in transmission and distribution infrastructure, energy storage, smart-grid technologies, nuclear energy, energy efficiency and green hydrogen. The meeting explored opportunities for greater cooperation in emerging technologies. These included long-duration energy storage, digital power-system technologies, green hydrogen, carbon capture, utilisation and storage (CCUS), and nuclear technologies such as Small Modular Reactors (SMRs). Carbon markets and the evolving global carbon-pricing framework were also discussed. The two sides exchanged views on the European Union’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) and its implications for international trade and energy-intensive industries. The discussions also focused on sharing expertise, technology and institutional knowledge between India and the European Union. Both sides recognised the importance of continued engagement to support the development of secure, resilient and sustainable energy systems. The meeting reaffirmed energy and power cooperation as an important component of the India-EU partnership, with both sides expressing their commitment to deeper technological and institutional collaboration across emerging and strategic areas of the energy sector.
