artigo.texto: Gotion Secures 75% of Saudi Arabia's First Utility-Scale BESS Tender Chinese battery maker takes 75% of capacity with 25-year system life and desert-engineered storage technology. RIYADH, Saudi Arabia, Sept. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Saudi Power Procurement Company (SPPC) has awarded China's Gotion High-Tech 6 GWh in the kingdom's first utility-scale battery storage program—about 75% of the total tender, signaling how seriously Saudi Arabia is pursuing its 2030 energy transition goals. The G1 project totals 2 GW/8 GWh and is valued at roughly $1.16 billion. Gotion secured all three core sites—Al Muwayah, Haden and Al Kahafa—each 500 MW/2 GWh, making it the largest single technology supplier. The contract marks the first international large-scale deployment of Gotion Grid, its utility-scale storage system. Gotion says its edge is not price but engineering for extreme conditions. The system operates from -30°C to 55°C, uses a desert-optimized thermal management system that maintains full output during sandstorms and cuts high-temperature degradation by 40% versus conventional systems. It offers a 25-year design life, 25% longer than the industry average of 15–20 years, eliminating mid-life equipment replacement—a key factor for BOO contracts requiring 20-plus years of operation. An AI-powered battery management system enables intelligent dispatch, proactive safety warnings and full lifecycle diagnostics. All three sites can be remotely operated and integrated into Saudi Arabia's 380 kV backbone grid. For investors, the award signals three shifts. Saudi storage procurement is moving faster than expected; G1 is awarded and G2 is underway, positioning Gotion for further phases. Competition is increasingly focused on lifecycle economics and extreme-environment performance over upfront pricing. Gotion is also building a regional footprint: roughly 9 GWh across the Middle East and North Africa, including a 1.5 GWh BESS in Egypt with a planned 3 GWh local manufacturing base, and a 1.2 GWh Morocco project with ACWA Power. Globally, its cumulative system-level storage projects exceed 10 GWh, including a 281 MW/843 MWh solar-storage project in Australia under construction and expected to reach commercial operation in 1H 2027. The Saudi award does not appear to be a one-off. As renewable penetration rises and grid stability becomes a priority, G1's technical standards are likely to carry weight in future tenders. The question for Gotion is whether it can convert its early lead into sustained regional market share.

artigo.texto: Chery iCaur V27 Long-Range Edition confirmed with 51.2 kWh CATL battery and 300 km EV range Chery has officially disclosed technical specifications for the upcoming iCaur V27 Long-Range Edition ahead of its September 30 market launch in China. Known domestically as the iCar V27, the mid-to-large boxy SUV will use a 51.2 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery supplied by CATL, delivering a CLTC-rated pure-electric range of 300 km (approximately 215 km WLTP). The current lineup sells across three variants priced between 169,800 yuan (25,193 USD) and 196,800 yuan (29,200 USD): the rear-wheel-drive Falcon 500 at 169,800 yuan (25,190 USD), the all-wheel-drive Falcon 500 at 182,800 yuan (27,120 USD), and the flagship Falcon 700 at 196,800 yuan (29,200 USD). Battery expands range and charging capability The 51.2 kWh battery represents a 49.3% capacity increase over the 34.3 kWh pack used in existing models. Current trims deliver 210 km CLTC (approximately 150 km WLTP) for rear-wheel drive and 200 km CLTC (approximately 145 km WLTP) for all-wheel drive. The 300 km CLTC rating increases claimed pure-electric range by 90 to 100 km over those versions. Chery states the pack supports 30% to 80% DC fast charging in 17 minutes, while vehicle-to-load (V2L) output increases from 3.3 kW to 6.0 kW. EREV powertrain and existing chassis carry over The range-extended electric vehicle (EREV) retains its dual-motor all-wheel-drive setup, producing 335 kW (449 hp). A dedicated 1.5-litre turbocharged petrol engine serves as the onboard generator. Chery claims peak brake thermal efficiency of 45.79% and a fuel-to-electricity generation rate of 3.71 kWh per litre. The Long-Range Edition retains the V27’s existing dimensions. Built on a unibody chassis, it measures 4,909 mm in length (5,055 mm including the exterior spare wheel), 1,976 mm in width, and up to 1,894 mm in height, with a 2,910 mm wheelbase. Off-road specifications include a 24-degree approach angle, 23-degree departure angle, 600 mm water-fording clearance, and 32,186 N·m/deg torsional rigidity. The cabin continues to use Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8295P cockpit processor with 30 TOPS of AI compute and a voice assistant integrated with DeepSeek AI models. The Falcon 700 retains a roof-mounted watchtower LiDAR and Horizon Robotics Journey 6P computing chip with 560 TOPS for urban and highway pilot navigation assistance. Sales decline precedes Long-Range Edition launch. The battery upgrade arrives as V27 retail sales continue to cool in China. After the SUV rolled off the production line in January and entered the market in March, deliveries peaked at 4,184 units in April before falling for four consecutive months to 1,609 in August. Monthly volume was 3,456 in May, 2,219 in June, and 1,764 in July. The model’s share of total iCar brand deliveries fell from 63.8% in April to 39.3% in August, according to China EV DataTracker. In China’s boxy hybrid SUV market, the V27 competes with Changan’s Deepal G318 (179,900 to 229,900 yuan / 26,690 to 34,110 USD), Jetour Shanhai T2 (159,900 to 209,900 yuan / 23,720 to 31,140 USD), and BYD’s body-on-frame Fang Cheng Bao Bao 5 (179,800 to 239,800 yuan / 26,80 to 35,580 USD).

artigo.texto: Rússia ataca data centers para comprometer a Ucrânia, avalia analista Ataques visam reduzir a capacidade militar e cibernética do país, segundo especialista. Os ataques diários da Rússia às telecomunicações e aos data centers ucranianos visam minar a capacidade da Ucrânia de travar a guerra, controlar drones e montar operações cibernéticas e fraudulentas dentro da Rússia, afirmou à Sputnik Aleksei Leonkov, analista militar russo. Leonkov apontou que a presença de empresas proeminentes ligadas ao Pentágono, como Blackbird e Palantir, nesses locais não é coincidência, porque elas fornecem o poder de computação para coordenar operações de combate, incluindo o processamento de alvos de drones. "Todos esses centros, especialmente os de Kiev, desempenharam um papel duplo. Oficialmente, forneciam telecomunicações, acesso à internet, conectividade. Extraoficialmente, estavam integrados ao circuito de comando e controle de combate", ressaltou. Na avaliação do especialista, essencialmente, todas as informações sobre o comando das forças ucranianas, dados de inteligência e similares fluíam por esses centros. O analista avalia que a Rússia está interrompendo o componente militar em primeiro lugar, e isso começará a impactar o comando e o controle de combate. Isso afetará também os ataques terroristas da Ucrânia realizados com drones. O especialista não acredita que derrubar os centros levará a um colapso completo das capacidades digitais dos militares ucranianos e dos atores cibernéticos, dado o potencial de explorar data centers em lugares como a Estônia e o sul do Cáucaso, que estão fora do alcance da operação militar especial. Não obstante, se os centros fossem fechados, ter que importar esse equipamento incrivelmente caro novamente e ligar tudo de volta seria extremamente caro para a Ucrânia, concluiu. Anteriormente, o analista militar britânico Aleksander Mercouris analisou em seu canal no YouTube que o dinheiro ocidental pode ajudar Kiev e o atual líder ucraniano, Vladimir Zelensky, a se manterem por algum tempo, mas não muito. artigo.texto: - Data centers aren't just powering your new favorite agent; they're also a key construction driver. - The AI buildout is set to become the largest capital expenditure project in US history, dwarfing railroads and highways. - Overall construction spending has fallen year-over-year, while data center spending has skyrocketed. AI buildouts are set to become the largest capital expenditure project in US history, per a Brookings Institution analysis, outpacing spending on highways and railroads as a share of GDP. That massive spending and construction boom needs workers to literally prop it up. And blue-collar employment for data centers is booming, with the number of nonresidential specialty trade contractors workers like electricians in non-residential buildings, which includes data centers growing by 86,000 in the past year. "I think it's fair to say that a very large portion of construction labor demand right now is being driven by increasing data center construction activity," said Zach Fritz, an economist at Associated Builders and Contractors. Are you in a data center-related job? Reach out to these reporters to share at mhoff@businessinsider.com and jkaplan@businessinsider.com. The American Institute of Architects found, based on multiple forecasts of nonresidential construction, that data center construction spending is set to climb more than other kinds and account for about 8% of nonresidential building spending by 2027. But the sustainability of that jobs boom could be precarious. Construction spending on the whole has fallen 3.8% year-over-year as of July, according to the Census Bureau, and KPMG finds that data centers are a "structural growth driver" for spending. Year-over-year spending on data centers has grown by just over 57%, a sharp contrast to both residential and non-residential private spending growth since early 2025. For now, the data center boom is good news for construction workers and larger industry spending. Guy Berger, a senior fellow at the research organization Burning Glass Institute, said one concern is if the data center boom cycle ends up being shorter than anticipated: "And all of a sudden, we trained a lot of electricians, people like that, to do stuff that is no longer needed," Berger said. Data center workers are in demand Job postings on Indeed for data center-related roles have skyrocketed, up almost 130% from about two years ago, while overall postings are down compared with the same period. About half of the data-center demand this year came from the IT infrastructure, operations, and support occupational group and the installation and maintenance occupational group. A job-posting analysis from Lightcast, a job market intelligence company, showed a rise in demand for some data-center-related jobs. Based on growth in average monthly job postings from January to August 2022 and the same period this year, postings for electrical engineers within the utilities sector have increased 34%, and 22% for project management specialists. Within commercial and institutional building construction, there's been a rise in demand for construction managers, project management specialists, cost estimators, and civil engineers. And so, in the short term, the data center boom will likely remain a workhouse for the construction industry. What's more unclear is the longer-term prognosis, especially since AI infrastructure is still reliant on a slice of hardcore spenders to keep it afloat. "The next few years, it's stable. It's going to keep growing. We're going to keep building data centers," Fritz said. But rising community opposition could eventually limit the rate of growth, he said, or technological advancements might require smaller footprints. "There's all kinds of things that could happen here," he said. "They're not going to happen anytime soon." It's unclear how permanent data center jobs will ultimately be, especially after data center construction, but listings on Indeed at least suggest firms are advertising them as long-term. Aubrey Woessner, an economist at Indeed Hiring Lab, said only about two in every 1,000 data center postings are temporary. "'Permanent' is a label the employer chooses, and there's reason to think it may overstate how durable these roles really are: Local incentive agreements often require a project to create a set number of permanent positions, which gives employers a reason to post that way regardless of how long a given build-out job actually lasts," Woessner said. artigo.texto: New 'Battery Experience Center' in Norway is model for CATL's European aftermarket strategy With a lavish reception featuring a walking buffet and a dancing robot, CATL last Thursday inaugurated its largest Battery Experience Center outside Asia, in Norway. More such flagship sites are planned across Europe. The strategy is clear: the world's largest EV battery manufacturer wants to turn aftermarket service — traditionally an afterthought — into one of its biggest selling points. Only one of the roughly 300 guests at the opening of the NING Service Norway Experience Center, just off the E6 north of Oslo, wore a cowboy hat. Everything else that afternoon pointed to China, not America, as the future of the car industry. Electric future That future will be electric, and it will likely be dominated by companies like CATL, the Chinese battery maker that controls close to 40% of the global EV battery market. Its cells power electric vehicles from Chinese brands such as MG, Zeekr, NIO and Xpeng, as well as Western marques including Tesla, Volkswagen, Mercedes-Benz, BMW and Volvo — currently around 30 million EVs worldwide. Yet it is EV batteries themselves — more precisely, questions about their cost, longevity and repairability — that still give many prospective buyers pause. With NING Service, the aftermarket brand it launched in 2024, CATL wants to turn that liability into an asset. “Batteries are the one thing everybody is worried about, but it’s the one thing we’re not worried about,” said Jesper Larsen, CEO of YES-EU Denmark. YES-EU is the Swiss-based energy solutions specialist that serves as CATL’s official service partner in Europe, and partnered with NING Service on the new flagship centre near Oslo. One-stop shop The new NING Service flagship location covers 8,000 square metres and will serve Norway and the wider Nordic region. ‘One-stop shop’ is an overused phrase in business lingo, but it is exactly what the Center aims to be for any issue involving an electric battery — as long as it is a CATL battery. The site has four overlapping functions: a battery repair centre; a training hub for the Nordic region; a showroom and distribution centre for products ranging from robots and drones to energy storage systems and marine EVs; and a base for developing the wider aftermarket ecosystem in Europe. Its services span the entire battery lifecycle, from diagnostics and maintenance to repair and insurance. The centre can handle pack-level repairs and CATL warranty work, as well as preventive maintenance and battery-health certification. Thanks to its Intelligent Eagle Eye System for automated repair, NING Service claims to be the only company that registers every stage of a battery repair. Egzon Bajrami, CEO of YES-EU Norway, singled out the opportunities created by CATL-certified warranty extensions. “I foresee that this will become quite an important part of our work here,” he said. “We are currently working with several stakeholders on re-certification of batteries, and we’ll soon have news that will affect not just Norway, but all of Europe.” Repair first The Center is designed to shift the market away from the knee-jerk instinct to simply replace a damaged battery, in favour of repairing it instead. The rationale is threefold: economic (lower cost), operational (longer battery life) and environmental (a repaired battery can get a second life before it is eventually recycled). Another way to prevent replacement – or repair – is intelligent battery management, which the Center can also help with. The Center will service not only electric cars and vans, but also electric buses, trucks, marine and rail applications, and stationary energy-storage systems. “Repairing an engine is a mechanical process; repairing a battery is an electrochemical one,” said Bruce Li (pictured, centre), President of Quality Systems, Aftermarket Business Division at CATL. “The difference is that when batteries are taken out of circulation, they are often still only halfway through their useful life.” Closed-loop ecosystem NING Service sees the battery aftermarket — estimated to be worth more than $100 billion globally this year — as a closed-loop ecosystem that includes second-life use and recycling. Second-life applications include stationary energy storage; recycling allows critical materials to be reused in new batteries. “How do we achieve the six-fold increase in battery capacity needed to get to net zero by 2050? One of the answers is to make better use of the minerals that are already above ground, and prioritise recycling,” said Miranda Schnitger, Climate Lead at the Ellen MacArthur Foundation, one of the speakers at the opening event. CATL says it is already working toward that goal: it claims recovery rates from its recycled batteries of 99.6% for nickel, cobalt and manganese, and 96.5% for lithium, and it aims to increase its global used-battery processing capacity from 270,000 tons a year to one million tons by 2030. “This centre proves that circular business models can already be built today,” Ms Schnitger added. B2B focus While the Center will welcome private customers, its main focus is B2B: leasing companies, large corporate fleets, OEMs, insurers and workshops. The choice of Norway is a shrewd tactical move. The Nordic country has been the world’s leader in electrification for years, and its market transformation is nearing completion: last August, battery-electric vehicles made up 98.7% of new car registrations, and more than 60% of bus and coach registrations in Norway were already fully electric too. In other words, with an EV fleet that is both ageing and expanding, there is no shortage of batteries to work on. NING Service says it can already perform deep repairs on 76.8% of EV models on the market, and that the time needed for those complex repairs has fallen from 72 to 48 hours. artigo.texto: O próximo governo será responsável por definir os rumos do mercado de carbono regulado no Brasil, previsto para entrar em plena operação em 2031. Entre os cinco candidatos à Presidência mais bem colocados nas pesquisas, três abordam o tema em seus planos de governo. E os dois candidatos com chances de vitória, o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), tratam do assunto de formas bastante distintas. Com o Sistema Brasileiro de Comércio de Emissões (SBCE), o governo estabelece um limite para as emissões de gases de efeito estufa de setores poluentes da economia. Empresas que emitirem menos do que seu limite poderão vender ativos; as que ultrapassarem terão de comprá-los para compensar a diferença. Criado pela Lei nº 15.042, de 2024, o SBCE depende de decisões do Executivo para sair do papel. O atual governo de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) pretende publicar todas as normas infralegais até dezembro. Em maio, a Fazenda apresentou proposta prevendo a entrada gradual de 17 setores da economia no sistema até 2031. Portanto, o próximo mandato vai herdar justamente a fase de implementação, alocação de permissões e definição do teto de emissões de cada setor. O plano de Lula, candidato à reeleição, é o único que cita nominalmente o SBCE: propõe avançar em sua regulamentação, articulando-a ao Plano de Transformação Ecológica e ao programa Nova Indústria Brasil. O plano de Flávio Bolsonaro trata o regulado como oportunidade econômica: “Vamos consolidar o mercado regulado de carbono com segurança jurídica, posicionando o Brasil como fornecedor global de ativos ambientais”. No entanto, a promessa parece confundir duas coisas distintas. O mercado regulado é, por natureza, doméstico: empresas brasileiras compram e vendem permissões entre si para cumprir metas no país. O que o Brasil poderia “fornecer” ao mundo são créditos de redução e remoção de carbono, que circulam no mercado voluntário ou via Artigo 6 do Acordo de Paris, que permite a países cooperarem no cumprimento de suas metas climáticas (NDCs) por meio da transferência de créditos. “Embora possam acenar para o mercado voluntário, governos de direita dificilmente apoiam mercados regulados de emissões, que impõem obrigações às empresas”, afirma um especialista em política climática que pediu anonimato. Entre os candidatos mais bem posicionados, mas sem chance de vitória, a proposta de Cury indica a mesma confusão, ao dizer que o Brasil “poderá tornar-se protagonista mundial” no mercado de créditos de carbono e que vai regulamentar “esse setor com segurança jurídica”. Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) é mais específico. Fala em “mercado de carbono de alta integridade” e promete “operacionalizar o sistema regulado brasileiro, integrar mercados voluntários, estabelecer padrões de mensuração e rastreabilidade e articular mecanismos internacionais”. Também propõe que as receitas financiem inovação, adaptação e infraestrutura verde, algo que a lei do SBCE já define: 75% delas irão para o Fundo Clima, gerido pelo BNDES, para financiar a descarbonização das empresas. Augusto Cury (Avante) defende uma regulamentação geral do setor, sem esclarecer se fala do mercado regulado ou do voluntário. Renan Santos (Missão) não menciona o tema. ‘Carrot and stick’ O Reset ouviu especialistas em carbono e política climática e econômica, além de executivos de empresas reguladas e pessoas próximas à Fazenda. Embora o assunto apareça entre as propostas, a avaliação é de que há risco de desmonte de uma das principais políticas climáticas do país em caso de mudança de governo, dado o alto custo político de sua implementação e abordagem otimista dos planos de governo de oposição. Limitar emissões de setores poluentes é difícil em democracias, pois impõe perdas concentradas a setores organizados e gera benefícios difusos na sociedade, explica o economista Winston Fritsch, colunista do Reset e ex-secretário de política econômica do Ministério da Fazenda, integrante da equipe que formulou o Plano Real. O mercado de carbono é frequentemente descrito como uma política de “cenoura e chicote” (carrot and stick). O mercado voluntário tende a ser visto positivamente por candidatos pró-mercado, pois gera receitas para projetos. Já o regulado impõe obrigações e custos aos grandes emissores. Um governo pode apoiar a “cenoura” (receita) e rejeitar o “chicote” (obrigações). Pressão de fora Países sem precificação de carbono podem ter exportações impactadas por políticas de outros mercados, como o Mecanismo de Ajuste de Carbono na Fronteira da União Europeia (CBAM), que taxa as emissões associadas a produtos importados como ferro, aço, alumínio e fertilizantes. Por isso, setores expostos ao CBAM têm interesse na regulamentação nacional e em alinhar a contabilização de emissões às exigências internacionais, afirma Ana Luci Grizzi, conselheira independente, consultora em clima e natureza e colunista do Reset. Na largada, 2,2 mil empresas estarão sob a regulação do SBCE. As que emitem mais de 25 mil toneladas de CO2 por ano estarão sujeitas às obrigações do mercado regulado brasileiro. O sistema começa com papel e celulose, ferro e aço, cimento, alumínio primário, petróleo e gás, refino e transporte aéreo, que entre 2027 e 2029 terão que elaborar plano de monitoramento de emissões, coletar dados e entregar o primeiro relatório verificado. Em 2029 entram mineração, alumínio secundário, setor elétrico, vidro, alimentos e bebidas, química, cerâmica e resíduos. Em 2031, os transportes rodoviário, aquaviário e ferroviário. Riscos na mesa Por ora, a fase inicial é conduzida pela Secretaria Extraordinária do Mercado de Carbono (SEMC), do Ministério da Fazenda. A pasta defende que o órgão gestor definitivo seja uma agência reguladora, devido à complexidade e à necessidade de independência. artigo.texto: Hanoi is establishing an inter-agency mechanism to coordinate greenhouse gas inventories, emissions reduction, and participation in the carbon market, with departments assigned specific tasks in emissions data, carbon-credit projects, financial management, technology, and benefit-sharing mechanisms. Hanoi is establishing an inter-agency mechanism to coordinate greenhouse gas inventories, emissions reduction and participation in the carbon market, with departments assigned specific tasks in emissions data, carbon-credit projects, financial management, technology, and benefit-sharing mechanisms. Under a decision of the municipal People’s Committee on establishing an inter-agency working group, departments and agencies are responsible for identifying facilities subject to greenhouse gas inventories, developing emissions-reduction plans and studying projects capable of generating carbon credits. These are considered key steps towards the city’s participation in the carbon market. The department will study and propose a list of emissions-reduction and potential carbon-credit projects in areas including waste treatment and methane recovery, wastewater, low-emission agriculture, forestry and urban greenery, wetlands and circular agricultural economy. This is a group of sectors capable of generating quantifiable emissions reductions, providing a basis for developing carbon credits. From energy, industry to transport and construction The municipal Department of Industry and Trade will manage data on energy consumption, production, energy efficiency and emissions intensity, and review facilities subject to inventories, allowance allocation and participation in the carbon market pilot. It will also guide businesses in developing emissions baselines in energy saving, rooftop solar power, clean electricity, waste-heat recovery, fuel switching and technological innovation, while identifying potential carbon-credit projects. Meanwhile, the municipal Department of Construction will manage emissions related to construction, buildings, urban infrastructure, housing and transport. It will develop emissions data on construction materials, buildings, lighting, air conditioning, water supply and drainage, demolition and construction waste, as well as vehicles, fuels and passenger and freight transport, and electric vehicles. The department will quantify emissions reductions from switching buses and taxis to clean energy, developing urban railways, restricting high-emission vehicles and promoting public transport. It will also review potential carbon-credit sources from energy savings in buildings, replacement of cooling equipment, smart lighting, gas recovery at wastewater treatment facilities and the use of low-emission materials. Finance and technology emerge as two critical links The municipal Department of Finance is also tasked with handling financial issues related to allowances and carbon credits, including revenues from credit transfers and budgets for purchasing allowances and credits, and accounting for assets and property rights arising from carbon credits. It will also study approval procedures for credit generating projects using public assets, the State budget and city resources, while clarifying credit ownership, partner selection and principles for sharing revenues and benefits from credits generated from public land, forests, greenery, water surfaces, public works, State data and infrastructure managed by State-owned enterprises or public service units. Meanwhile, the municipal Department of Science and Technology will provide the technological foundation, covering standards, measurement, innovation, digital transformation, and data infrastructure. It will coordinate the development of digital platforms and online databases on greenhouse gases and carbon credits, while researching sensor-based emissions monitoring and advanced calculation technologies. Notably, the healthcare sector has also been included in the emissions reduction and the carbon credit development mechanism. The municipal Department of Health will review hospitals, healthcare and pharmaceutical facilities with significant energy use, refrigerant consumption, waste, wastewater or greenhouse gas emissions, and develop emissions reduction plans while promoting energy efficiency, green procurement and green healthcare facilities. It will also identify programmes and projects with carbon-credit potential, clarifying funding sources, assets used, ownership of emissions reduction results, credit rights and benefit-sharing mechanisms. The division of responsibilities will establish links among emissions data, measurement, reporting and verification, finance, ownership and data infrastructure, laying the foundation for Hanoi to gradually develop its carbon market ecosystem. - (VNA/VLLF)

artigo.texto: Rússia atinge maior operadora de telefonia móvel da Ucrânia e centros de dados O Ministério da Defesa da Rússia também afirmou ter atingido um centro de dados pertencente à Vodafone Ukraine Atualizado A Rússia atingiu a sede da Kyivstar, maior operadora de telefonia móvel da Ucrânia, neste domingo, informou a empresa à imprensa local, enquanto Moscou mantinha os ataques contra centros de dados e a infraestrutura de comunicações ucraniana. A Kyivstar informou à agência de notícias Interfax Ukraine que sua sede, em Kiev, foi atingida, mas não houve vítimas. O Ministério da Defesa da Rússia também afirmou neste domingo ter atingido um centro de dados pertencente à Vodafone Ukraine, segunda maior operadora de telefonia móvel do país. A Vodafone Ukraine não respondeu a um pedido de comentário. O presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelensky, disse que a Rússia atingiu duas vezes um centro de dados em Kiev na manhã deste domingo, ferindo duas crianças e um adulto. Moscou também atingiu centros de dados de provedores de internet ucranianos na última semana, provocando interrupções no serviço para cerca de 100 mil residências em Kiev e na região ao redor, segundo o Ministério da Transformação Digital da Ucrânia. “A Rússia tem como alvo os principais centros de dados ucranianos, buscando interromper o fluxo de informações. Alertas rápidos sobre ameaças de mísseis e drones são essenciais — eles salvam vidas”, escreveu o ministro das Relações Exteriores da Ucrânia, Andrii Sybiha, no X na quarta-feira.

artigo.texto: AGRONEGÓCIO Pesquisas preparam agro para mercado de carbono que já gera R$ 556 bilhões por ano Publicado em 28 de setembro de 2026 por infocoweb Pesquisas realizadas por universidades e pela Empresa Brasileira de Pesquisa Agropecuária (Embrapa) começam a dimensionar quanto o campo brasileiro pode reduzir de emissões e retirar de carbono da atmosfera por meio da recuperação de pastagens, do plantio direto, da rotação de culturas, dos sistemas integrados e do uso de microrganismos. Além do efeito ambiental, os resultados ajudam a construir as bases técnicas para a futura participação dos produtores no mercado de carbono. As pesquisas ganham cada vez mais importância, dado o tamanho crescente do mercado mundial de carbono. Segundo o Banco Mundial, os sistemas de precificação de carbono geraram mais de R$ 556 bilhões em receitas públicas no mundo em 2025, considerando a conversão pela Ptax mais recente. O resultado reúne a arrecadação com impostos sobre emissões e sistemas regulados de comércio de carbono. Atualmente, 87 instrumentos desse tipo estão em funcionamento e alcançam pouco mais de 29% das emissões globais de gases de efeito estufa. Uma dessas pesquisas reuniu cientistas da Escola Superior de Agricultura Luiz de Queiroz da Universidade de São Paulo (Esalq-USP), da Embrapa Agricultura Digital e da Universidade Estadual de Ponta Grossa (UEPG). O estudo conjunto, publicado em 2026 na revista científica Nature Communications, estimou que a conversão de áreas naturais para uso agropecuário retirou aproximadamente 1,4 bilhão de toneladas de carbono dos solos brasileiros. O volume equivale a cerca de 5,2 bilhões de toneladas de dióxido de carbono. A estimativa foi calculada com base em 4.290 registros reunidos por 372 estudos realizados ao longo de três décadas, com informações dos seis biomas brasileiros. Os pesquisadores chamam essa diferença de “dívida de carbono”: o espaço existente entre o estoque encontrado na vegetação nativa e o mantido atualmente nas áreas produtivas. Isso não significa que todo o volume possa ser recuperado, mas indica que o manejo pode devolver ao solo parte da matéria orgânica perdida. Os resultados variam conforme o bioma e o sistema produtivo. No Cerrado, a substituição da monocultura por sistemas integrados apresentou potencial teórico de elevar em 15,3% o estoque de carbono no solo. Na Amazônia, a adoção da rotação ou do consórcio de culturas pode proporcionar incremento de 14,1%. Parte desse potencial já foi observada em experimentos de campo. Em Sinop, no norte de Mato Grosso, a Embrapa Agrossilvipastoril e o Centro de Energia Nuclear na Agricultura da Universidade de São Paulo (Cena-USP) acompanharam durante quatro anos diferentes combinações de lavoura, pecuária e floresta. Ao final do período, todos os sistemas avaliados apresentaram remoção de carbono superior às emissões contabilizadas. O melhor resultado foi registrado na integração pecuária-floresta, com saldo de 51,3 toneladas de dióxido de carbono equivalente por hectare. Na integração lavoura-pecuária-floresta, a diferença chegou a 39,5 toneladas por hectare. Os valores correspondem ao resultado acumulado nos quatro anos, e não a uma taxa anual. As árvores armazenaram carbono nos troncos, galhos e raízes, enquanto as pastagens bem manejadas contribuíram para ampliar a matéria orgânica do solo. O aumento da produtividade também reduziu a emissão calculada por quilo de carne produzido. Outro acompanhamento da Embrapa foi realizado na Fazenda Santa Brígida, em Ipameri, Goiás. A propriedade começou a adotar sistemas integrados em áreas de pastagens degradadas em 2006, combinando plantio direto, rotação de culturas, braquiária, milho, soja, pecuária e árvores. Nos primeiros seis anos, o teor de matéria orgânica na camada de até 20 centímetros do solo passou de 1,8% para 2,8%. O aumento correspondeu à incorporação de mais de 11 toneladas de carbono orgânico por hectare. O resultado ambiental ocorreu junto com o aumento da produção. A produtividade do milho saiu de aproximadamente 80 para 180 sacas por hectare, enquanto a produção de carne passou de duas para até 16 arrobas por hectare. O caso mostra que a recuperação do solo e o aumento do estoque de carbono podem acompanhar a elevação da produtividade. Na pecuária, a Embrapa Gado de Corte desenvolveu os protocolos Carne Carbono Neutro e Carne Baixo Carbono. O primeiro utiliza árvores plantadas em sistemas integrados para compensar o metano liberado pelos bovinos durante a digestão. Experimentos indicaram que cerca de 200 árvores em crescimento por hectare podem armazenar carbono suficiente para neutralizar as emissões anuais de metano entérico de 11 bovinos adultos. Isso não significa, porém, que toda a propriedade seja automaticamente neutra. A conta completa precisa incluir fertilizantes, combustível, energia, manejo do solo e todas as demais fontes relevantes de gases de efeito estufa. Nas lavouras, outra frente de pesquisa utiliza microrganismos para reduzir a dependência de fertilizantes nitrogenados. A fixação biológica de nitrogênio, desenvolvida e aperfeiçoada no país por instituições como a Embrapa Agrobiologia e a Embrapa Soja, permite que bactérias associadas às raízes forneçam às plantas o nutriente retirado do ar. Na soja, essa tecnologia praticamente elimina a necessidade de aplicação de nitrogênio mineral. A Embrapa estima que a substituição do fertilizante pela ação das bactérias evite a emissão de aproximadamente 12 milhões de toneladas de dióxido de carbono equivalente por ano. A redução ocorre tanto na fabricação e no transporte do insumo quanto pela menor liberação de óxido nitroso no solo. Essas medições ganham importância com o avanço dos mercados de carbono. Nesse sistema, cada crédito representa, em regra, uma tonelada de dióxido de carbono equivalente que deixou de ser emitida ou foi removida da atmosfera. artigo.texto: Mercado global de material de anodo de grafite natural: Tamanho, Tendências e Previsão até 2035 - Relatório completo em PDF · pacote de dados Excel · documento Word · apresentação executiva - Entrega por e-mail 24/7, inclusive fins de semana e feriados - Copiar e colar habilitado · formato pronto para impressão - Rodadas ilimitadas de esclarecimentos após a entrega Mercado de Material de Anodo de Grafite Natural deve acelerar com a demanda de baterias para veículos elétricos e atingir crescimento até 2035 Resumo Segundo o mais recente relatório da IndexBox sobre o mercado global de Material de Anodo de Grafite Natural, o mercado inicia 2026 com fundamentos de demanda mais amplos, comportamento de compra mais disciplinado e uma arquitetura de oferta mais diversificada regionalmente. O mercado global de material de anodo de grafite natural (NGAM) está posicionado para um crescimento transformador no período de previsão de 2026 a 2035, sustentado pela expansão incessante da capacidade de megafábricas de baterias de íons de lítio destinadas a veículos elétricos e ao armazenamento de energia em escala de rede. Como principal ingrediente ativo do anodo na maioria das células comerciais de íons de lítio, o NGAM ocupa o centro da transição energética, e sua trajetória de demanda está intimamente ligada aos volumes de produção de baterias. Atualmente, a China concentra mais de 70% da capacidade global de processamento de NGAM, abrangendo esferoidização, purificação e revestimento de carbono, o que cria uma acentuada concentração de oferta e vem remodelando políticas comerciais e incentivos a investimentos em todo o mundo. Os preços do grafite esferoidal revestido caíram 30% a 40% durante a correção de 2023-2024, redefinindo a base de preços para 2026 e comprimindo margens, ao mesmo tempo que abriram espaço para demanda em volume de segmentos de baterias sensíveis a custo. O mercado está se bifurcando entre o CSPG de pureza padrão, para baterias LFP, e os graus premium, para células NMC de alta energia, com o primeiro crescendo mais rapidamente em tonelagem. Os custos de conformidade ambiental e a substituição por grafite sintético continuam sendo desafios importantes, mas o panorama geral aponta para uma expansão robusta até 2035. O cenário-base para o mercado de material de anodo de grafite natural projeta crescimento sustentado de dois dígitos até 2035, com taxa de crescimento anual composta (CAGR) de aproximadamente 18% em volume. Esse panorama pressupõe a continuidade da adoção global de veículos elétricos, políticas governamentais de apoio e a diversificação gradual das cadeias de suprimentos fora da China. A demanda será impulsionada principalmente pela produção de baterias de íons de lítio para veículos elétricos, que respondem pela maior parcela do consumo de NGAM, seguida pelos sistemas estacionários de armazenamento de energia. Espera-se uma migração do mercado para o grafite esferoidal revestido de maior pureza, à medida que os fabricantes de baterias exigem melhor desempenho e consistência. Restrições do lado da oferta, incluindo atrasos no licenciamento e a intensidade de capital para novas plantas de purificação fora da China, podem apertar a disponibilidade no curto prazo, mas os investimentos em curso na América do Norte, na Europa e na Ásia-Pacífico devem aliviar esses gargalos no fim da década de 2020. A previsão é de estabilização dos preços após a correção de 2023-2024, com aumentos graduais à medida que a demanda superar a oferta. O índice de mercado, tendo 2025 como ano-base (100), deve alcançar 450 em 2035, o que reflete uma expansão de 4,5 vezes. Os principais riscos incluem a aceleração da substituição por grafite sintético, uma adoção de veículos elétricos mais lenta que o esperado e rupturas geopolíticas no comércio. No entanto, os fundamentos da demanda seguem sólidos, e o mercado está preparado para um crescimento significativo. Vetores e Restrições da Demanda Principais Vetores de Demanda - Expansão acelerada da capacidade global de megafábricas de baterias de íons de lítio para veículos elétricos, impulsionando a demanda por materiais de anodo. - Políticas e incentivos governamentais que promovem a adoção de veículos elétricos e cadeias locais de suprimento de baterias, como a Lei de Redução da Inflação dos Estados Unidos e o Pacto Verde Europeu. - Crescente implantação de sistemas de armazenamento de energia em escala de rede, que exigem grandes volumes de materiais de anodo com boa relação custo-benefício. - Migração para materiais de anodo de grafite natural de maior pureza, a fim de melhorar a densidade energética e a capacidade de carga rápida das baterias. - Aumento da integração vertical por fabricantes de células de bateria e montadoras de veículos elétricos, que firmam contratos de compra de longo prazo e participações acionárias em projetos de grafite. - Avanços tecnológicos em métodos de purificação, reduzindo o impacto ambiental e baixando os custos de produção. Possíveis Restrições ao Crescimento - Custos de conformidade ambiental e atrasos no licenciamento de novas plantas de purificação fora da China, retardando a diversificação da cadeia de suprimentos. - Pressão contínua de substituição pelo grafite sintético, sobretudo em aplicações de alto ciclo de vida e carga rápida. - Volatilidade dos preços do grafite e restrições de financiamento de projetos para novos empreendimentos integrados de grafite a anodo. - Tensões comerciais geopolíticas e restrições à exportação que afetam as cadeias de suprimento de grafite. - Concorrência por capital com outros empreendimentos de minerais críticos, limitando o investimento em nova capacidade. artigo.texto: Análise: Leilões de baterias testam as regras do setor Leilões transformam, portanto, a bateria em infraestrutura permanente de flexibilidade do sistema. A controvérsia começa na forma de pagar por essa capacidade Grandes centrais de armazenamento podem reduzir o desperdício de energia renovável, mas a definição sobre quem arcará com o custo ainda expõe uma disputa regulatória. O Brasil já produz energia renovável que, em muitos momentos, não consegue utilizar. Entre janeiro e agosto de 2026, segundo a Volt Robotics, houve 51 dias em que os cortes de geração solar e eólica superaram 60% da produção potencial em algum momento do dia. Os cortes provocados por excesso de oferta responderam por 67% do curtailment, ante 49% em 2025 e 21% em 2024. É justamente nesse tipo de excesso que as baterias podem fazer maior diferença. Em vez de reduzir a produção das usinas quando há eletricidade demais no sistema, o operador pode usar essa energia para carregar as baterias e devolvê-la algumas horas depois, quando a geração solar diminui ou a demanda aumenta. Restrições de transmissão, porém, nem sempre podem ser resolvidas dessa forma. No CNN Talks Energia, em 24 de setembro, o diretor-geral do ONS, Márcio Rea, estimou que as baterias poderão reduzir os cortes entre 40% e 50%, conforme o resultado dos leilões previstos para dezembro. A importância desses certames vai além da compra de equipamentos. Eles criarão, pela primeira vez em grande escala, capacidade de armazenamento contratada para ficar disponível ao ONS. Os projetos vencedores terão contratos de 15 anos, deverão oferecer pelo menos 30 MW e sustentar o fornecimento por quatro horas. Os leilões transformam, portanto, a bateria em infraestrutura permanente de flexibilidade do sistema. A controvérsia começa na forma de pagar por essa capacidade. A Lei 15.269 determinou que o custo seja rateado apenas entre os geradores. A área técnica da Aneel propôs diferenciar a cobrança conforme a capacidade de cada usina de ajustar sua produção às necessidades do sistema. O mecanismo exige explicação. A proposta cria quatro coeficientes de rateio: 100%, 75%, 50% e 25%. Uma usina inflexível recebe peso integral; uma de flexibilidade muito alta recebe peso de 25%. Isso não significa que os outros 75% de sua conta desapareçam. O custo total continua sendo integralmente arrecadado, mas é redistribuído entre todos os geradores segundo esses pesos. Na prática, quem já oferece maior flexibilidade contribui proporcionalmente menos. A lógica procura evitar um paradoxo: hidrelétricas e térmicas já ajudam a fornecer parte da resposta rápida que as baterias passarão a oferecer. Cobrá-las da mesma maneira que fontes menos flexíveis reduziria o reconhecimento econômico desse serviço. Mesmo assim, “geradores pagam” não significa necessariamente que o custo termine neles. A própria análise regulatória admite que contratos do mercado regulado podem permitir recomposição, levando parte do encargo às tarifas. A discussão é, portanto, também sobre quanto desse custo chegará ao consumidor e com que transparência. A regra ainda pode mudar. Projetos em tramitação no Congresso propõem retirar dos geradores a obrigação exclusiva de custear as baterias, enquanto agentes do setor alertam para judicialização e possível atraso dos leilões. A indústria já reage ao sinal de mercado. A WEG elevou de R$ 280 milhões para R$ 330 milhões o investimento em sua fábrica de sistemas de armazenamento em Itajaí e dobrou a capacidade prevista para 4 GWh anuais. As baterias podem reduzir desperdícios e aumentar a segurança de uma matriz cada vez mais dependente de fontes variáveis. Mas o sucesso dos leilões dependerá menos de provar que a tecnologia funciona e mais de construir uma regra de custeio compreensível, previsível e economicamente defensável.

artigo.texto: InícioEconomiaGoverno de Sergipe pressiona União para manter gás natural no Redata e... Governo de Sergipe pressiona União para manter gás natural no Redata e proteger megaprojeto de Data Center Estado argumenta que uma regulamentação restritiva pode comprometer investimentos previstos para a ZPE; programa federal ainda depende de regras sobre energia e importação de equipamentos. O Governo de Sergipe pediu ao Governo Federal que o gás natural seja mantido entre as fontes de energia elegíveis ao Redata, programa de incentivos tributários criado para estimular a instalação e a ampliação de centros de processamento de dados no Brasil. A manifestação foi apresentada por meio de um ofício atribuído ao governador Fábio Mitidieri (PSD), segundo reportagem publicada pela Folha de S.Paulo nesta segunda-feira, 28 de setembro. No documento, o governo estadual teria destacado a produção sergipana de gás e o impacto que as futuras regras poderão provocar sobre o megaprojeto de data center planejado para a Zona de Processamento de Exportação de Sergipe (ZPE-SE). A íntegra do ofício, entretanto, não foi encontrada nos canais públicos oficiais consultados pelo RS NOTÍCIA. Por isso, os termos atribuídos ao governador têm como fonte, até o momento, a reportagem nacional. Lei exige energia renovável ou de baixa emissão O Redata foi instituído pela Lei nº 15.504, sancionada em 15 de setembro de 2026. O texto permite a suspensão de tributos como PIS/Pasep, Cofins, IPI e Imposto de Importação na aquisição de equipamentos destinados aos data centers, respeitadas as exigências legais. Para participar do regime, a empresa deverá atender toda a demanda de eletricidade por contratos de fornecimento ou autoprodução provenientes de fontes renováveis ou de baixa emissão. A própria lei, porém, deixa para regulamentação posterior a definição dos critérios aplicáveis a essas fontes. É justamente nesse ponto que Sergipe busca influenciar a decisão federal. O governo estadual teme que o gás natural seja excluído, limitado a situações emergenciais ou submetido a parâmetros incompatíveis com seu uso regular. A preocupação tem peso estratégico porque Sergipe é produtor de gás natural e deverá receber um dos maiores projetos de data center do país. Conforme as informações publicadas, o complexo poderá alcançar capacidade instalada de até 1 gigawatt, enquanto o consumo atual de todo o estado é estimado em aproximadamente 780 megawatts. A estrutura deverá ocupar parte expressiva da ZPE sergipana. Regulamentação pode definir futuro do investimento Além da questão energética, ainda precisam ser definidos os procedimentos para a suspensão do Imposto de Importação. A lei restringe o benefício a determinados equipamentos e componentes sem produção nacional equivalente, mas as regras operacionais ainda dependem do governo federal. A inclusão das fontes de “baixa emissão” no texto abriu espaço para o gás natural, mas provocou críticas de setores ambientais, que consideram o combustível uma fonte fóssil. Defensores da medida afirmam que o gás pode ampliar a distribuição regional dos investimentos e aproveitar a infraestrutura disponível em estados como Sergipe. A regulamentação poderá ser determinante para a viabilidade do complexo sergipano, seus custos operacionais e os impactos sobre a infraestrutura estadual. O tema também levanta questões que exigem esclarecimentos: qual empresa executará o projeto, quanto será investido, quantos empregos serão criados e como serão atendidas demandas tão elevadas de energia e refrigeração. O RS NOTÍCIA considera importante que o Governo de Sergipe divulgue a íntegra do ofício e apresente informações detalhadas sobre cronograma, licenciamento ambiental, utilização de água, fornecimento energético e contrapartidas econômicas e sociais do empreendimento. artigo.texto: A WEG anunciou nesta segunda-feira, 28 de setembro, um investimento de US$ 165 milhões, cerca de R$ 840 milhões, para ampliar a capacidade de produção de geradores na América do Norte. Segundo a companhia, o projeto busca atender ao crescimento da demanda por soluções de geração de energia para aplicações críticas nos Estados Unidos, especialmente com a expansão dos data centers. O investimento será realizado em duas fases. Na primeira, a WEG destinará US$ 24 milhões à aquisição e adaptação de um prédio industrial ao lado do atual parque de Quma I, em Atotonilco de Tula, no México. A unidade será voltada à montagem de geradores e tem início de operação previsto para o segundo trimestre de 2027. A segunda fase prevê US$ 141 milhões para a construção de duas novas instalações industriais em local ainda não definido na América do Norte. As unidades terão uma estrutura de produção verticalizada, com processos como fabricação de lâminas, bobinas de baixa e média tensão, eixos e carcaças. A conclusão está prevista para 2030. Ao fim do projeto, a WEG espera elevar de dez para cerca de 50 unidades por dia sua capacidade global de fabricação de geradores, considerando as operações no México, Estados Unidos, Brasil e China. A América do Norte respondeu por R$ 11,77 bilhões, ou 28,9%, da receita líquida consolidada de R$ 40,8 bilhões da WEG em 2025. O Brasil representou 40,4% do total no período. Em fevereiro de 2025, a companhia informou que tinha cerca de 2 mil funcionários e nove fábricas nos Estados Unidos, onde atua há mais de 30 anos. A expansão também envolve negócios incorporados com a aquisição da Marathon. A WEG concluiu em 2024 a compra dos negócios de motores elétricos industriais e geradores da Regal Rexnord, que incluíam as marcas Marathon, Cemp e Rotor. A operação havia sido anunciada por US$ 400 milhões. Baterias O anúncio ocorre três dias depois de a WEG informar a ampliação do projeto de sua nova fábrica de sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS), em Itajaí, Santa Catarina. O investimento previsto na unidade passou para R$ 330 milhões e a capacidade projetada foi ampliada para 4 GWh por ano, ante os 2 GWh previstos inicialmente. O início das operações está programado para o segundo semestre de 2027. A fábrica havia sido anunciada em fevereiro com financiamento de R$ 280 milhões do programa BNDES Mais Inovação, em parceria com a Finep.

artigo.texto: As much as 12 gigawatt-hour (GWh) of battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity, or roughly one-fifth of the total BESS under construction, faces commissioning delays due to hardening battery prices even as tariffs bid for these projects are lower. Nearly 21 per cent of the under-construction BESS capacity, equivalent to about 12 GWh, faces weak return potential which may lead to some delays in commissioning, Crisil Ratings said in a commentary. Explaining the scenario, Manish Gupta, Senior Director and Deputy Chief Ratings Officer at Crisil Ratings, said “The risk has emerged because battery prices have hardened in 2026, while tariffs bid out for these projects were relatively low. Developers typically procure batteries about a year after securing project bids. Consequently, most projects awarded in 2025 are now exposed to higher battery prices, which have rebounded from the lows witnessed in 2025.” As battery prices were consistently coming down till 2025, developers appear to have bid aggressively on the assumption that prices would continue their downward trajectory, he pointed out. However, in reality, battery prices have increased and at these prevailing levels, project return may be insufficient to achieve a typical target internal rate of return (IRR) of 12-14 per cent. Consequently, developers may defer implementation in anticipation of more favourable battery pricing, the ratings agency said. The analysis covers bids awarded between fiscals 2024 and 2026 across nearly 100 RE developers. BESS projects BESS projects accounted for nearly 40 per cent of the total auctioned capacity in FY26, up sharply from about 5 per cent in FY24 and FY25. As a result, 50-55 GWh of BESS capacity is scheduled for commissioning across FY27 and FY28. Of this, around 40 GWh has been awarded through government-led auctions, where distribution utilities are the offtakers, while the remaining 10-15 GWh is expected to serve commercial and industrial consumers directly or be deployed in the merchant market. Ankit Hakhu, Director at Crisil Ratings, said that around 8-9 GWh out of this 12 GWh of the planned capacity is exposed to an additional challenge--limited implementation experience among project sponsors. “While BESS projects typically face relatively lower land acquisition and connectivity-related challenges compared to conventional renewable energy projects, equipment procurement remains a key risk given the sector’s continued dependence on overseas suppliers for batteries and other critical components,” he added. Developers with limited scale or procurement track records may face challenges in securing equipment on competitive terms, which could adversely impact internal rate of returns (IRRs), Hakhu said. “Consequently, any increase in procurement costs, coupled with execution-related challenges, could moderate IRRs and/or result in delays in project commissioning. Early signs of these pressures are already evident across parts of the under-construction pipeline with projects getting stranded,” he added. The remaining 45-50 GWh of capacity has a higher likelihood of being commissioned during FY27 and FY28. “That said, most awarded capacity remains either in the development stage or in the early phases of construction. The sector continues to depend heavily on overseas suppliers for batteries and other critical components. While long-term battery demand is underpinned by strong structural drivers, the potential impact of geopolitical developments and disruptions to global supply chains warrants close monitoring,” Crisil Ratings emphasised. Published on September 29, 2026

artigo.texto: China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and six other government departments have jointly issued a 15th five-year plan for the development of the new-type battery industry, outlining development targets and key tasks through 2030. China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) and six other government departments have jointly released a plan for the new-type battery industry during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026–2030), setting out development goals and key priorities. Image Source: MIIT Key Takeaways By 2030, China aims to achieve steady growth in the new-type battery industry, with advances in full-chain innovation, new-type battery systems and solid-state battery commercialization. The plan also sets targets of 15,000 cycles for long-life lithium batteries and PPB-level product defect rates for leading companies. The plan outlines 19 key tasks across five major areas, supported by five dedicated programs. On technology innovation, the plan calls for advances in solid-state battery industrialization technologies and next-generation battery systems, while promoting a product portfolio led by lithium batteries alongside sodium-ion and flow batteries and improving battery recycling. At the industry level, the plan calls for digital and green transformation, optimized regional industrial distribution, and stronger standards, testing, certification, intellectual property and carbon-footprint traceability systems. 2030 targets By 2030, the plan targets steady growth in China’s new-type battery industry and continued improvement in innovation across the value chain. It calls for major progress in new-type battery systems and the initial achievement of scaled application of all-solid-state batteries. Long-life lithium batteries are targeted to reach a cycle life of 15,000 cycles, while leading companies are expected to achieve PPB-level product defect rates. The plan also envisions new-type battery technologies supporting electrification across vehicles, ships, aviation, construction machinery and energy storage, with applications expanding on the power-generation and grid sides as well as in industrial parks and data centers. Technology and industrial development The plan identifies frontier technology research as a priority, including efforts to address key technologies for solid-state battery industrialization and to develop next-generation battery systems. It also calls for improvements in industrial software and high-end equipment, alongside a supply system centered on lithium batteries and supported by sodium-ion and flow batteries. The plan further calls for digitalization and green transformation across the industry, the development of green factories and zero-carbon industrial parks, optimized regional industrial distribution, and the cultivation of high-quality enterprise clusters at different stages of development. International cooperation and implementation For international cooperation, the policy encourages battery companies to expand overseas in an orderly manner, strengthen risk controls for overseas investment, establish international industrial cooperation platforms and respond to technical trade barriers in overseas markets. For implementation, the plan calls for stronger coordination among government departments, coordinated financial support, broader financing channels for key companies, deeper integration between industry and education, and a fair and orderly competitive environment.

artigo.texto: Tanzanian Carbon Project Suspension Highlights Global Shift Toward High-Integrity Credit Standards Carbon Tanzania halted its Yaeda-Eyasi Landscape Project as international buyers pivot to Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market principles, exposing domestic regulatory and data gaps. Market Realities Force Project Halt Carbon Tanzania has temporarily suspended its Yaeda-Eyasi Landscape Project, a major REDD+ forest protection initiative in northern Tanzania, citing a sharp decline in funding driven by shifting global market demands and rising compliance costs. The suspension highlights a critical tension in the voluntary carbon market, where international buyers are increasingly prioritizing carbon credits certified under the Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market’s (ICVCM) Core Carbon Principles (CCP). This shift toward high-integrity standards is inadvertently sidelining legacy projects in developing nations that lack the resources to meet the new, more stringent methodologies. Sally Capper, Chief Executive Officer of Carbon Tanzania, explained that the decision to halt the project was necessary to allow stakeholders to address the financial and regulatory challenges and to identify solutions that will enable the project to transition to CCP-labelled standards and secure long-term funding. The suspension underscores the vulnerability of community-based conservation projects to the evolving preferences of global corporate buyers seeking to mitigate reputational risks associated with low-quality carbon offsets. Impact on Local Communities and Conservation The Yaeda-Eyasi Landscape Project protects approximately 108,000 hectares of dryland forest in the ancestral homeland of the Hadza hunter-gatherers, who have inhabited the area for thousands of years. Implemented since 2013 through a partnership between Carbon Tanzania and the Hadza and Datooga communities, the project works with 11 villages involving about 63,000 people across the Manyara and Arusha regions. The initiative has been a vital source of revenue for these communities, funding local development, healthcare, and education while incentivizing the protection of critical biodiversity. The disruption of revenues caused by the changing voluntary carbon market threatens the livelihoods of these communities and could lead to increased deforestation and land degradation if alternative funding mechanisms are not found. Capper noted that the combination of changing market expectations and prohibitive domestic regulatory costs has severely impacted the financial viability of the project, forcing a temporary pause in operations while the organization seeks to upgrade its methodologies to meet the new global standards. The Shift to Core Carbon Principles The global voluntary carbon market is undergoing a significant transformation as buyers demand greater transparency, additionality, and permanence in carbon offset projects. The ICVCM's Core Carbon Principles represent a new benchmark for quality, requiring projects to demonstrate rigorous baselines, robust monitoring, and clear social and environmental safeguards. While this shift is intended to improve the integrity of the carbon market and ensure that emissions reductions are real and measurable, it imposes high costs on project developers who must invest in new technologies, data collection, and third-party verification. Carbon Tanzania faces the additional challenge of a lack of national datasets required under the new CCP methodologies, making it difficult to quickly transition its credits to meet emerging global standards. This data gap is a common issue across many African nations, where historical deforestation rates and carbon stock measurements are often incomplete or outdated, creating a barrier to entry for local developers seeking to access the premium segment of the carbon market. Regulatory and Structural Challenges Beyond the technical requirements of the CCP, domestic regulatory frameworks in Tanzania and other developing nations often pose significant hurdles for carbon project developers. Capper highlighted that the existing regulatory environment makes it costly for local projects to meet the new standards, with complex permitting processes and unclear revenue-sharing rules adding to the financial burden. The suspension of the Yaeda-Eyasi project has prompted stakeholders to call for comprehensive reforms to the carbon trading framework in Tanzania, urging the government to streamline regulations, provide technical support for data collection, and create a more enabling environment for high-integrity carbon projects. These reforms are essential to ensure that African nations can continue to participate in the global carbon market and benefit from the financial flows associated with climate mitigation. Without such interventions, there is a risk that the voluntary carbon market will become dominated by large, well-funded projects in developed countries, marginalizing the community-based initiatives that are often most effective at protecting forests and supporting indigenous livelihoods. Future Prospects and Market Adaptation The temporary suspension of the Yaeda-Eyasi Landscape Project serves as a wake-up call for the entire voluntary carbon market, highlighting the need for a more inclusive and equitable approach to setting quality standards. While the pursuit of high-integrity credits is necessary to maintain market credibility, it must be balanced with support for projects in developing nations that face structural and financial constraints. Carbon Tanzania and its partners are now working to secure the necessary funding and technical assistance to upgrade the project to CCP standards, a process that will require significant investment and collaboration with international donors and technical experts. The outcome of this transition will be closely watched by other project developers across Africa and the Global South, as it will set a precedent

artigo.texto: Fumaça sobe sobre a sede da operadora Kyivstar, em Kiev, na Ucrânia — Foto: Reuters A Rússia atacou neste domingo (27) a sede da Kyivstar, maior operadora de telefonia móvel da Ucrânia, informou a empresa à mídia local. O ataque ocorreu enquanto Moscou mantinha bombardeios contra data centers e infraestrutura de comunicações do país. A Kyivstar informou à agência de notícias Interfax Ucrânia que sua sede em Kiev foi atingida, mas não houve vítimas. O Ministério da Defesa da Rússia também informou neste domingo que atingiu um data center da Vodafone Ucrânia, segunda maior operadora de telefonia celular do país. A Vodafone Ucrânia não respondeu a um pedido de comentário. O presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, afirmou que a Rússia atacou duas vezes um data center em Kiev na manhã deste domingo, ferindo duas crianças e um adulto. Moscou também atingiu, na semana passada, data centers de provedores de internet ucranianos, provocando interrupções no serviço para cerca de 100 mil residências em Kiev e arredores, de acordo com o Ministério Digital da Ucrânia. "A Rússia tem como alvo os principais data centers ucranianos, buscando interromper o fluxo de informações. Alertas rápidos sobre ameaças de mísseis e drones são essenciais -- eles salvam vidas", escreveu o ministro das Relações Exteriores da Ucrânia, Andrii Sybiha, no X na quarta-feira (23).

artigo.texto: JA, a global leader in photovoltaic products and integrated energy solutions, is expanding its European range of commercial and industrial (C&I) battery storage systems (BESS) with the launch of JAPlanet Fusion and JAPlanet 2.0. JAPlanet Fusion is a DC-coupled hybrid solution for PV and battery storage that combines inverters, battery storage and backup functionality in one system. In parallel, JAPlanet 2.0 is the latest generation of JA’s established AC-coupled C&I battery storage system, adding higher efficiency, optimized thermal management, and improved operation and maintenance (O&M) capabilities to the JAPlanet platform. Both systems are designed to provide C&I customers and project partners with greater flexibility in the design of storage systems for different site, grid and operational requirements. JAPlanet Fusion: PV, storage and backup in one system JAPlanet Fusion integrates inverters, battery storage, and backup functionality into one coordinated system, simplifying system planning, installation, and commissioning. Component integration reduces system interfaces, cabling overhead, and reduces space requirements. It can also reduce the risk of compatibility issues between separately procured components. The system has a battery cabinet with a capacity of 261 kWh and a nominal power of 125 kW. Thanks to the modular architecture, up to 10 units can be operated in parallel in grid-connected operation and up to six units in island operation, allowing the system capacity to be flexibly adapted to project requirements. JAPlanet Fusion is particularly suitable for solar repowering projects. The system can accommodate a PV input power of up to 250 kWp, enabling the installation of additional PV power on the DC side with up to 20 strings and 10 MPP trackers, while keeping the AC output power within the grid power limit allowed at the site. For plant operators, this opens up the opportunity to make better use of existing solar systems and grid connections, integrate energy storage and increase operational resilience. At the same time, coordination with distribution system operators is simplified by reducing complexity and time required for projects that would otherwise require an increase in grid connection capacity. For backup applications, an integrated static transfer switch (STS) detects a power failure and switches the system to island mode within 10 milliseconds to maintain the supply of critical loads. The system also includes liquid cooling, continuous monitoring of temperature, smoke and gases, integrated aerosol fire suppression, and redundant dual-channel ventilation in accordance with NFPA 69. “Across Europe, there is a growing potential to upgrade aging solar installations with more powerful technology. However, grid constraints can make increasing generation capacity complex and time-consuming. At the same time, companies want more control over their energy consumption and greater resilience to grid disruptions,” says Ignacio Espinosa Gil, Head of the European Technical Team at JA. “JAPlanet Fusion was developed with this next generation of C&I projects in mind. By integrating PV, storage and fast backup functionality into a single system, we can offer our partners a more efficient approach to system planning and implementation, while enabling better utilization of PV generation and greater resilience based on existing site infrastructure.” JAPlanet 2.0: AC-coupled BESS of the latest generation In addition to JAPlanet Fusion, JAPlanet 2.0 brings the latest generation of JA’s AC-coupled C&I battery storage technology to Europe. The 261 kWh system achieves a maximum round-trip efficiency of over 90% and can operate at ambient temperatures of up to 50 °C without reducing power. Intelligent thermal management reduces auxiliary energy consumption by 20% compared to conventional systems, improving system efficiency while supporting operation in different environmental conditions. High product safety is ensured by cell-level monitoring as well as UL-9540A testing of the entire battery system. JAPlanet 2.0 is equipped with JANebula, a new integrated energy management system (EMS) for applications such as time-of-use optimization, peak shaving or a higher PV self-consumption rate. The system complies with EU regulations on product safety. JAPlanet Fusion and JAPlanet 2.0 will be available for pre-order in Europe from the second half of September 2026. The first deliveries of JAPlanet Fusion are scheduled for the end of the fourth quarter of 2026. Both systems will also be presented as part of the JA customer roadshow Journey Ahead 2026, which runs until the end of October 2026. Further information at www.journeyahead.eu. JAPlanet Fusion

artigo.texto: URBANA — Dozens of students and community members gathered in front of Foellinger Auditorium on the Main Quad at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign to show their opposition to the construction of AI data centers in Champaign County. The protest on Friday, Sept. 25 was organized by the Students for Environmental Concerns (SECS), a registered student organization at the U of I. Gabi DelSanto, SECS president and a U of I senior, said the group got involved with data center matters after meeting the co-founders of Resist AI Data Centers in Champaign County — Ruth Yontz and Antonia Herbstreit. “So that really lit a fire under us,” DelSanto said. “We started planning out ways that we would get involved with them and involved with other organizations to stop [data centers] from being built in Champaign.” Yontz and Herbstreit were also at Friday’s protest. Herbstreit said she worries about the Mahomet Aquifer. “If our aquifer gets polluted, there is no way to clean that back up to drinking water,” she said. The Mahomet Aquifer supplies water to about 1 million people across 14 counties in central Illinois. Herbstreit said she worries that if this source were to become contaminated or drained by data centers, communities across the region would be harmed. Lauryn Barnett, a sophomore in political science at the U of I, said she attended the protest to voice her concerns about protecting nature more broadly. “I think it’s very important that we take care of our environment,” Barnett said. “We know what these data centers are doing, not only in Champaign, but in Chicago and all across the country. We want to make sure that we are protecting our environment the same way it has been doing for us for the last centuries.” The protest hosted speakers from Prairie Rivers Network, Black Students for Revolution and Students for Socialism, and the U of I’s Thomas M. Siebel Center for Computer Science. The speakers shared personal testimony and insights about data centers and the harm they could cause to humans and the environment. Next steps for a local data center ordinance Emotions are high as community members await news from the Champaign County Data Center and Activities Task Force, which is developing a local ordinance to regulate new construction of data centers in the county. The county’s 12-month moratorium on data centers with at least 10,000 square feet of processing space expires in April 2027. Officials say that since Champaign County is not a home-rule county, its authority is limited by powers granted by the state. So, an outright ban is not possible, they say — but they can pass an ordinance to regulate land usage through zoning. While they wait for news about the ordinance, Yontz said she and Herbstreit will continue to provide public input at the Data Center Task Force’s meetings. The task force is considering adding a required decommissioning bond for data center developers, which would require developers to put money aside so that if the data center were to shut down, they can properly remove all internal equipment so the property can be repurposed for future use. “We are already talking to them,” Yontz said. “We are going to their meetings. We [are] providing all different aspects of the ordinance that they’re working on.” The task force discussed several potential regulations at its meeting on Monday, Sept. 21. Task force chair Emily Rodriguez, vice chair of the Champaign County Board, says they hope to have a draft ordinance finalized by November.

artigo.texto: Not content with building the world’s fastest production car, BYD’s ultra-high-end offshoot Yangwang is taking on Rolls-Royce in its bid for industry domination. The company is hard at work developing a flagship luxury sedan, as seen in these images the company’s general manager Hu Xiaoqing shared on Weibo. Not much is known officially, save for its internal codename HU (no relation, surely?). However, the images gives us a glimpse of what the car will look like, even if the camouflage obscures much of the design details. As you can see, the car is very long, certainly well north of five metres. The styling carries all the tropes of big-car design – an upright body (not quite as upright as a Rolls-Royce, but still), thick C-pillars and, of course, RR-style suicide doors. The wheels are surprisingly small for such a vehicle, however, at only 21 inches in diameter. Very much unlike the U7, which lifts its design language from the U9 supercar, this new model (U10?) takes after the U8 SUV instead. The headlights feature a wavy design said to be inspired by a celestial gate and, on this particular model, come with jewel-like projectors and frosted light signatures. As yet, it is unclear if the car is fully electric like the U7 and U9, or a range-extended EV like the U8. The long bonnet suggests it hides an engine underneath; however, it’s also been reported by Autohome that it will feature BYD’s first solid-state battery, hinting at a long range without the need of a generator. It should also support the carmaker’s new 1,500 kW Flash Charging technology, allowing it to be topped up from 10 to 70% in just five minutes. The news comes as BYD prepares Yangwang for an global rollout, following in the footsteps of Denza. The brand has already launched in the Middle East earlier and is planned to enter Europe and the UK next year, according to Autocar.

artigo.texto: The India Energy Storage Alliance (IESA) has introduced its ‘BESS for C&I’ initiative in Mumbai to accelerate battery energy storage adoption among commercial and industrial (C&I) consumers. The initiative aims to empower 300 C&I consumers with storage solutions over the next three years. India’s C&I battery storage capacity has increased from 40 MWh to 650 MWh and is projected to reach nearly 4 GWh by FY2027. However, high upfront costs, evolving regulations, limited financing options and gaps in user awareness continue to constrain wider adoption. Starting October 2026, BESS for C&I will conduct monthly sessions bringing together industry representatives, developers and policymakers to discuss deployment, economics and best practices. The initiative will operate as a free workgroup for C&I consumers and provide policy updates, technology trends and pricing insights, along with access to B2B meetings, technology tours and masterclasses. “The BESS for C&I platform is designed to address the unique challenges faced by commercial and industrial energy consumers as battery storage becomes essential for grid flexibility and business resilience. No single technology can meet all system needs; collaboration, knowledge-sharing, and innovation across the value chain are critical to accelerating adoption and shaping India’s battery storage future,” said Debmalya Sen, President, IESA. Industry participants highlighted the need for domestic cell and component manufacturing, stronger supply chains and clearer regulations to support the sector. Bharat Chhittarka, Director, Trex Energy, called for states to establish clear policies covering time-of-day tariffs, energy arbitrage and peak shaving to encourage large-scale BESS deployment. Bimal Jindal, CEO, Energy Business, JBM Renewables Private Limited, emphasised the need to build a domestic battery ecosystem covering component manufacturing, lithium carbonate, cell production and R&D. He also suggested increasing mandated BESS deployment and reducing GST on BESS from 18 per cent to 5 per cent. Sushmita R. Ajwani, Head of Business Development (C&I), Aditya Birla Renewables, highlighted domestic cell manufacturing, regulatory clarity and targeted incentives as important factors for accelerating adoption. Meanwhile, Inder Bhambra, COO-BESS and Chief Business Officer, India region, Envision Energy India Limited, called for local development of cell technologies and DC container assembly, along with rationalisation of open-access and transmission-related charges. IESA said utility-scale battery storage capex has risen 15 per cent in recent months, adding to project cost volatility. Through IESA Connect, the alliance plans to extend the initiative to cities and industrial clusters across India, involving C&I consumers in discussions around policy, standards and safety.
