The report, titled ‘From 1 GWh, RE battery storage systems charging to ~45-50 GWh’,covers bids awarded between fiscals 2024 and 2026 across nearly 100 renewable energy developers. However, around 8-9 GWh of awarded capacity faces a higher risk of delays, which could moderate the pace of deployment. It said that the growing need for storage is a direct consequence of the rising share of renewable energy to 39 per cent of India's installed power generation capacity and 15 per cent of energy generated last fiscal. He said that developers typically procure batteries about a year after securing project bids. “Most projects awarded in 2025 are now exposed to higher battery prices, which have rebounded from the lows witnessed in 2025. As the battery prices were consistently coming down till 2025, developers appeared to have bid aggressively on the assumption that prices would continue their downward trajectory,” he said. The report also noted that as by nature, the RE generation is intermittent which has increased the need for firm and peak-hour power supply. This has elevated the importance of energy storage solutions, particularly BESS. However, in reality, battery prices have increased and at these prevailing levels, project returns may be insufficient to achieve a typical target internal rate of return of 12-14 per cent. Consequently, developers may defer implementation in anticipation of more favourable battery pricing.

artigo.texto: The Walker County Data Center Development Standards Study Committee reconvened recently for its third meeting, undertaking a section-by-section review of the county’s initial draft data center ordinance. Key discussions focused on parcel size thresholds, conditional use options, water capacity limits, and a tense exchange regarding committee transparency and industry conflicts. Draft Ordinance Review: Parcel Minimums and Micro-Facility Rules Planning & Zoning Director Jon Pursley and Economic Development Director Stephanie Watkins opened the session by outlining updates to the draft ordinance. Following recommendations from prior meetings, staff added Section 15, which mandates upfront performance and decommissioning bonds to protect the county from abandoned infrastructure. Under Section 3 (Land Use), the draft restricts data centers to industrially zoned districts and establishes a 10-acre minimum parcel size. Committee members debated whether a 10-acre requirement is suitable for smaller “micro-facilities” or fiber “booster stations” which can occupy as little as 5,000 square feet and consume minimal power and water. District 1 Appointee Barney Danks said restricting data centers strictly to the industrial zone could make land disappear quickly. He questioned why would the county force an industry to locate on 10-acres, if it only needs two. “I think commercial sites, whether existing in the county today or in the future, may want to have a ‘data center’ that is small.” He encouraged the committee to focus industrial zone requirements on hyper-scale operations. “Not every data center is the same as another data center.” The other District 1 appointee, Jason Rader, suggested restrictions for data centers with a footprint greater than 50,000 square feet. “I think smaller ones should be allowed in commercial. It’s no different than other buildings. It could be a dollar store or anything else.” Pursley explained that developers seeking smaller footprints or commercial locations (such as C1 or C2 zones) can apply for a conditional use permit or variance, allowing the Board of Commissioners case-by-case oversight. County records show Walker County contains 63 industrial-zoned parcels with a majority of the acreage located within the Walker County Business Park (400 acres) and the Northwest Georgia Business Park in Rock Spring (50 acres). Appointees agreed to consult legal counsel to confirm whether restricting facilities strictly to established industrial parks is legally defensible. Closed Loop Cooling Systems and Committee Member Experience District 3 Appointee Laura Owsley questioned District 1 Appointee Barney Danks regarding his industry holdings. Danks mentioned he operates an 8-megawatt Bitcoin mining facility on 2.5 acres along Glentana Road using open-air cooling fans. Owsley raised concerns over a lack of prior disclosure and questioned whether Danks resides in Walker County. Danks clarified that while he owns commercial property and businesses in Rossville and Walker County, he resides elsewhere. He acknowledged that his 6-year-old facility relies on older open-air technology, which generates noise and would not comply with proposed modern standards, and expressed support for requiring closed-loop cooling systems for future developments. Committee members appear favorable toward recommending closed-loop system requirements in their report. Water Capacity Limits, Utility Easements, and Power Restrictions Resource protection remained a core focus. While Walker County Water and Sewer maintains an excess capacity of 4.5 to 5 million gallons per day, officials noted that upcoming commercial developments (such as the Pilgrim’s prepared foods facility) and residential housing growth will absorb much of that margin. To prevent unexpected grid strain, the committee agreed to require developers to submit utility capacity confirmation letters covering all project phases prior to permit approval. On power infrastructure, Danks noted the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) now requires major power users to pay $1.5 million per megawatt upfront for infrastructure expansion. The committee discussed prohibiting on-site fossil fuel power plants and requiring data center developers, and not utility companies or the county, to secure their own utility easements to prevent the use of eminent domain through residential neighborhoods. Setbacks, Green Space, and Environmental Protections The committee reviewed physical development standards under Section 4: - Setbacks & Buffers: The draft establishes a 100-foot setback between adjacent industrial properties and a 400-foot setback from residential properties, matching the county’s restrictive poultry house standards. - Green Space & Height: Parcels must maintain a 15% minimum green space buffer, and buildings are capped at a maximum height of 50 feet. HVAC units and generators must be placed on roofs or oriented away from residential borders. - Environmental & Historic Protections: Owsley advocated adding an anti-clustering clause to prevent cumulative air quality impacts and urged prohibiting data centers in historic districts such as McLemore Cove. Next Steps and Data Center Tour Committee members will take a tour early next month of regional data centers and booster stations to see operations firsthand. At their next meeting, they plan to discuss sound/noise and lighting restrictions. The committee is working toward a December 4 deadline to finalize its draft recommendations. Once complete, the proposed ordinance will move to the Planning & Zoning Board for public hearings before reaching the Board of Commissioners for a final vote in early 2027. artigo.texto: WEG (WEGE3) anuncia plano de investimento de R$ 840 milhões de olho na expansão de data centers; veja A WEG (WEGE3) anunciou nesta segunda-feira (28) um plano de investimento de US$ 165 milhões, aproximadamente R$ 840 milhões, para expandir sua capacidade de produção de geradores na América do Norte. De acordo com o comunicado ao mercado, o projeto se dará em duas fases, visando atender à crescente demanda por soluções de geração de energia para aplicações críticas nos Estados Unidos, especialmente impulsionada pela expansão dos data centers. “A iniciativa representa mais um passo na estratégia de crescimento dos negócios incorporados à companhia por meio da aquisição da Marathon”, diz a WEG. Vale recordar que, em setembro de 2023, a WEG anunciou a aquisição dos negócios de motores elétricos industriais e geradores da norte-americana Regal Rexnord no valor de US$ 400 milhões. A transação, conforme anunciado à época, teve como foco os negócios de motores elétricos industriais e geradores, vendidos sob as marcas Marathon, Cemp e Rotor. Receba gratuitamente as newsletters do Money Times As fases do investimento A primeira fase do projeto da WEG contempla investimentos de US$ 24 milhões para aquisição e adequação de um prédio industrial localizado ao lado do atual Parque Industrial de Quma I, em Atotonilco de Tula, no México. A unidade será destinada à montagem de geradores e contribuirá para a expansão da capacidade produtiva da companhia, com início das operações previsto para o segundo trimestre de 2027. Na segunda fase, em local ainda a ser definido na América do Norte, a WEG investirá US$ 141 milhões na construção de duas novas instalações industriais. O projeto prevê a implantação de uma estrutura produtiva verticalizada que abrangerá processos estratégicos como fabricação de lâminas, bobinas de baixa e média tensão, eixos e carcaças, aumentando a eficiência operacional e a competitividade da operação. Ao fim da segunda fase, prevista para ser concluída em 2030, a companhia terá capacidade global de fabricar cerca de 50 geradores por dia em suas fábricas no México, EUA, Brasil e China, ante a atual capacidade de 10 geradores por dia.

artigo.texto: Why Calumet County hasn't passed a data center moratorium CHILTON (WLUK) -- While other cities and counties are passing data center moratoriums, Calumet County has not. It's because their zoning ordinance already doesn't allow data centers in the county. "We didn't need to [pass a moratorium]," said Calumet County Administrator Todd Romenesko. "Our current ordinance does not allow it as permissible use." A legal adviser said because it isn't allowed as permissible use, a moratorium would be redundant. "From my standpoint, you don't need a moratorium in Calumet County," said Rebecca Roeker, attorney at Attolles Law, who advised the county on Monday night. "Again, because of your existing ordinances and because of the modifications that the elected officials are going to consider in the near future." - RELATED: Manitowoc County Board votes unanimously to impose 18-month moratorium on data centers - RELATED: Winnebago County will pursue 12-month data center moratorium Any modifications would likely just be to close any potential legal loopholes. These zoning ordinances apply to townships in the county, but not necessarily villages or cities. For example, it'll apply in the town of Woodville, but may not in the city of Chilton, as villages and cities may have their own separate zoning ordinances. Romenesko said there are no current data center proposals in the county. The discussion comes as the Chicago-based Invenergy has proposed a natural gas energy project and wind energy project in the county, which has raised concerns from residents about the possibility of a new data center in the county. County Administrator Todd Romenesko says there's no link. "This just happened to be something we were trying to be proactive on regarding trying to regulate anything regarding data centers," said Romenesko. The county does already have several small data centers, according to Romenesko. Because Calumet County has lots of open land, it could be the target of a major data center development.

artigo.texto: Battery energy storage system is beginning to look like solar did a decade ago — a technology whose importance is moving rapidly from the drawing board to the electricity market. And, increasingly, the market itself is sending the signal. Government agencies are beginning to adapt the rules to make storage easier to deploy. The latest example is the Central Transmission Utility of India (CTUIL), which last week issued a procedure for BESS projects that have grid connectivity to seek an increase in their energy-storage capacity (MWh) without increasing their approved charging/discharging capacity (MW). The distinction is significant. A 100 MW/200 MWh battery can, for instance, become a 100 MW/400 MWh battery by adding storage capacity while retaining the same grid connection and power conversion capacity. CTUIL’s move gives developers a regulatory route to do this rather than having to treat the increase in MWh as an increase in grid connectivity. CTUIL is also seeking clarity from the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission over whether the ₹2 lakh per MW ‘Connectivity Bank Guarantee-3’ would apply when the increase is only in MWh. Pending clarification, it is not seeking BG-3 for such applications. But the strongest case for BESS may be coming from the electricity market. Former Grid-India CMD SR Narasimhan recently did a study by modelling the arbitrage potential of a 1 MW BESS using four years of day-ahead market data — 96 time blocks a day, 365 days a year, six storage durations and two operating models. The exercise shows that arbitrage opportunities have generally strengthened, with FY2025-26 emerging as the strongest year for most configurations. The other finding is equally interesting: longer-duration batteries earn more, but with diminishing returns. Moving from one hour to six hours of storage gives six times the energy capacity, but arbitrage revenue rises only 3.5–4.4 times. The battery captures the most attractive price spreads first. And the market is changing with solar. Cheap charging opportunities are increasingly moving from winter nights to solar-heavy afternoons, while discharge opportunities are emerging around demand peaks, including mornings. Then there is the ₹20-a-unit signal. Between September 6 and 17, the high price day-ahead market on IEX repeatedly touched its ₹20 per kWh ceiling, with much of the trading occurring in non-solar hours. At the same time, India’s peak demand touched a September record of 269 GW on September 10. Gas-based generation jumped 80.32 per cent year-on-year during September 1–9 as the system leaned on flexible generation to meet the evening shortfall. Meanwhile, solar capacity reached 168 GW as of August 31, according to data from the ministry of new and renewable energy. The message is becoming difficult to miss. Increasingly, India needs not just more electricity but also electricity at the right time. Solar solved the generation problem. BESS may solve the timing problem. And if ₹20 electricity is the price of getting power at the wrong hour, then the battery suddenly starts looking less like an accessory to renewable energy and more like the thing that makes renewable energy truly useful. Published on September 28, 2026

Gotion described the signings as consistent with its overseas expansion strategy, aimed at consolidating its position in the global electric vehicle battery market while further deepening its long-term strategic partnership with Volkswagen. Ônibus elétrico avança nas cidades brasileiras: ao menos 12 fabricantes estão de olho nesse mercado
BYD, Eletra e mais dez fabricantes disputam o mercado de ônibus elétricos no Brasil, que já conta com 1.883 unidades em circulação, superando a Colômbia. Emplacamentos tiveram salto
Atualizado
O Brasil bateu uma marca importante no segmento de ônibus elétricos: chegou a 1.883 unidades circulando pelo país, no primeiro semestre, superando a Colômbia (que tem 1.737 unidades) e ficando apenas atrás do Chile (onde rodam 4.808 veículos), países precursores na eletrificação da frota pública na América Latina. Especialistas afirmam que este é um ponto de virada para esse mercado no país, que vem ganhando tração e atraindo cada vez mais a atenção dos fabricantes: pelo menos 12 empresas estão de olho no potencial brasileiro, sendo que oito já fabricam ônibus elétricos por aqui.
— O crescimento da produção e das vendas, nos últimos dois anos, vem sendo forte. Nos últimos meses, mais ainda. Já temos oito empresas fabricando no Brasil e mais chinesas têm intenção de produzir aqui, aproveitando as regras do Mercosul para exportar para a região — diz Carlos Eduardo de Souza, diretor-conselheiro da Associação Brasileira do Veículo Elétrico (ABVE) e CEO da Tevx, companhia focada em eletromobilidade e infraestrutura de transporte sustentável no Brasil.
Transição em curso
Os números mais recentes refletem o aumento da procura: foram emplacadas 932 unidades entre janeiro e agosto de 2026, um crescimento de 82,03% em relação ao mesmo período de 2025 (quando foram emplacados 512 veículos). Apenas em agosto, o volume de emplacamentos de ônibus elétricos saltou de 89 (julho) para 254 unidades.
- Novas fontes de receita: rede de atacarejo Assaí expande negócios e anuncia compra de postos de combustíveis em São Paulo
São Paulo vem puxando a transição da frota a diesel para os veículos elétricos, com cerca de 80% do total em circulação, porque conta com um modelo de financiamento junto a instituições como o BNDES, que inclui as operadoras, além de ter implementado metas rígidas de descarbonização, que preveem zerar as emissões de gases do transporte público até 2038.
A Secretaria Municipal de Mobilidade Urbana e Transporte (SMT) determinou, em 2022, que seria aceita apenas a inclusão de ônibus movidos a energia limpa na frota, medida fundamental para a renovação dos veículos com modelos elétricos. O programa de metas 2025-2028 determina a substituição de 2.200 ônibus por veículos de matriz energética mais limpa. As concessionárias do transporte paulistano são responsáveis pela contratação da empresa que fará a instalação dos carregadores e pela garantia de abastecimento dos modelos. Atualmente, a infraestrutura de carregamento conta com 455 pontos instalados, diz a SMT.
Na sexta-feira, o BNDES aprovou financiamento de R$ 329 milhões para a cidade do Rio eletrificar a frota por meio de parceria público-privada. O projeto prevê a aquisição de 175 ônibus elétricos.

Prisão da ex-vereadora Verônica Costa é mantida após audiência de custódia no Rio
Conhecida como Mãe Loira do Funk, empresária foi presa em Petrópolis na quinta-feira; processo tramita sob segredo de justiça
Atualizado
A ex-vereadora e empresária Verônica Costa, conhecida como Mãe Loira do Funk, teve a prisão mantida pela Justiça após passar por audiência de custódia realizada neste sábado, em Benfica, na Zona Norte do Rio. Verônica foi presa na quinta-feira, em Petrópolis, na Região Serrana. A decisão de manter a custódia foi ratificada durante a audiência, mas os fundamentos não foram divulgados porque o processo tramita sob segredo de justiça. Por esse motivo, a ata da sessão não está disponível para consulta pública.
A ex-parlamentar foi encaminhada ao sistema prisional após a prisão e permanece à disposição da Justiça.
Segundo uma investigação feita pela Polícia Civil, em fevereiro de 2011, quatro pessoas ligadas à funkeira teriam ido até a residência do casal e, por ordem dela, amarrado Márcio no banheiro. Além dela, também foram presos Bruno Chaves Ribeiro, Tatiane Chaves Ribeiro Marques e Bruno Marcelo Bahia Marques. Uma quinta pessoa condenada pelo crime segue foragida.
Verônica trocou de defesa após a decisão judicial. A advogada criminalista Maíra Fernandes, que assumiu sua representação, protocolou na última sexta-feira (25) um pedido de revisão criminal no Tribunal de Justiça do Rio (TJRJ), sustentando que a condenação desconsiderou o histórico de violência doméstica relatado pela ex-parlamentar.
O que a defesa de Verônica alega
O principal argumento da revisão é um boletim de ocorrência registrado por Verônica em 2010. No documento, ela relata ter sido vítima de agressões físicas e psicológicas constantes praticadas pelo então marido, além de ameaças com arma de fogo. Segundo o registro, em um dos episódios ele teria feito uma roleta-russa apontando a arma para a cabeça da vereadora.
O boletim também afirma que o homem retirou dinheiro destinado à campanha eleitoral de Verônica, caracterizando, segundo a defesa, um episódio de violência patrimonial. Segundo a advogada, familiares encontraram a ex-vereadora machucada e em estado de desespero e reagiram ao presenciar a situação. A defesa ressalta que não considera a reação física dos parentes uma forma legítima de solucionar o conflito, mas argumenta que o episódio deve ser analisado dentro do contexto de violência e da ausência de proteção estatal existente à época.
— É muito diferente olhar para uma mulher que procurou a polícia em 2010 com os instrumentos de proteção que temos em 2026. Hoje, uma mulher que relata agressões, violência patrimonial e ameaças com arma encontra uma legislação mais detalhada e mecanismos de proteção que foram fortalecidos ao longo de 16 anos. Não podemos analisar o que aconteceu em 2010 como se toda a estrutura existente hoje estivesse disponível naquela época — afirmou Maíra Fernandes.

O delegado Felipe Santoro recorreu às redes sociais, no fim de semana, para traçar um paralelo entre um inquérito recém-concluído e “Quem Ama Cuida”, da TV Globo. “Engraçado como a novela, muitas vezes, imita a vida real, de forma simultânea”, escreveu o policial. Santoro se referia ao indiciamento de um homem por estelionato sentimental — crime em que uma relação afetiva é usada como instrumento para obter vantagem financeira. Na ficção, Carmita, personagem de Deborah Evelyn, também cai em um golpe amoroso aplicado pelo namorado, Edson (Vandré Silveira).
- Falsa intenção: veja como funciona o golpe em aplicativos de namoro e como se proteger

— Hoje estou bem abalada. Reviver tudo e ler críticas de pessoas dizendo “como você cai em um golpe em 2026” está sendo duro. Mas existem outras mulheres que são vítimas e se calam por vergonha; por isso ele continua agindo. Eu estou com vergonha, mas não vou me calar.
Ligação do chefe
Ela conta que conheceu Dirlei Aguiar da Silva no aplicativo de namoro Tinder e que os dois começaram a conversar pelo Instagram. O passo seguinte foi trocar números de celular, e as mensagens migraram para o WhatsApp, até que marcaram um encontro. No dia, de acordo com a vítima, ele foi buscá-la em casa.
— Nesse trajeto, eu recebi uma ligação do meu chefe e fiquei chateada por estar tratando de assuntos profissionais depois do horário. Ele escutou tudo e comentou que conhecia uma pessoa que estava precisando de uma secretária. Eu falei: “me indica”. Eu estava insatisfeita naquele momento.
Segundo ela, o homem teria dito que haveria uma prova para a admissão no emprego:
— Ele disse que não tinha risco, que eu ia receber as respostas e que eu ia precisar somente comprar a prova por R$ 1,3 mil. Eu vi que tinha alguma coisa errada, só que eu não consegui enxergar.

artigo.texto: RWE secures 119 MW of onshore wind capacity in latest German auction 18.09.2026 The Moerdijk power station site will be home to a flagship large-scale battery system in the Netherlands. RWE has taken the final investment decision to build a 400 megawatts (MW) and 1100 megawatt-hours (MWh) battery storage system at the site. It will consist of 208 containers with lithium-ion batteries and can deliver its full output for almost three hours. Construction is scheduled to start in due course, commissioning is planned for second quarter of 2028. Nikolaus Valerius, CEO of RWE Generation SE: “This battery marks a major milestone for reliable power supply and grid relief in Noord-Brabant. As one of the largest and most powerful battery systems in the Netherlands, it will be capable of covering the evening peak demand of around 500,000 households for almost three hours. At the same time, it can absorb surplus electricity from the grid within seconds. Battery storage plays a crucial role in building a resilient energy system that can accommodate a growing share of renewables.” Mark Lentjes, Regional Director of TenneT Southern Netherlands: “We are pleased that RWE intends to contribute to a more efficient use of the electricity grid in West Brabant with a large-scale battery that acts as a congestion reliever. RWE’s large-scale battery is located close to the 150,000-volt high-voltage substation at Moerdijk-Noord, where it will help to alleviate the regional bottleneck, which in turn has an impact on congestion across the whole of Noord-Brabant.“ Moerdijk battery to relieve grid congestion The new battery system will make best use of the existing infrastructure: It will be connected to the national grid via the existing substation at the RWE power plant in Moerdijk. Through capacity steering agreements with Transmission System Operator TenneT, the battery will be dispatched to relieve congestion in the Noord-Brabant region. Thanks to this development, space is being created on the grid for parties on the waiting list who wish to purchase electricity. TenneT, together with the regional grid operator Enexis, will be investigating what this means in the coming period. The grid operator will take this development, along with other developments in the region, into account when reviewing the congestion management study in December of 2026. The new battery system will also be equipped to provide advanced grid services such as instantaneous reserve (inertia). The Moerdijk site already hosts the first synthetic inertia battery connected to the continental European grid, with a capacity of 7.5 MW/11 MWh. Matching offshore wind with onshore flexibility RWE and TotalEnergies’ 795 MW offshore wind project off the Dutch coast, is designed to combine offshore wind generation with onshore flexibility solutions that help align renewable power production with electricity demand. At Moerdijk, the battery projects play an important role here by storing electricity when wind output is high and feeding it back into the system when needed, helping to balance fluctuations and optimise the use of renewable power. Together with technologies such as electrolysis, e-boilers and smart charging, it supports OranjeWind’s ambition to integrate offshore wind more effectively into the Dutch energy system. Battery storage at RWE As a driver of the energy transition, RWE develops, builds and operates battery storage systems in the US, Europe and Australia. In the Netherlands, RWE currently operates two battery storage systems. In addition to the existing battery at Moerdijk, RWE operates a 35 MW/41 MWh battery at Eemshaven power plant. Globally, RWE currently operates battery storage systems with a total capacity of around 1.7 gigawatts (GW) and 3 GW are under construction. As an integral part of its growth strategy, RWE plans to significantly expand its battery storage capacities worldwide. Pictures for media use are available at the RWE media centre (credit: RWE): More information on battery storage systems at RWE can be found here.

artigo.texto: News Should Tesla move away from its battery technology? Should Tesla replace its current battery system when it works so well? The 18650 battery cells Tesla Motors has been using in its Model S, have proven to perform very well compared to other types of battery chemistries on the market. The cylindrical battery which measures 18 mm wide and 65 mm in height, hence its name 18/650, has been the main component of Tesla’s battery pack, but could there be a possibility that it would soon move away from this proven technology? Tesla isn’t married to 18650 Tesla Chief Technology Officer JB Straubel has recently said the company isn’t married to cylindrical cells and the company would move to flat cell manufacturing if and when there are greater advantages to replacing the 18650. This has started speculations in the world of investors, yet again. Elon Musk Elon Musk’s AI Grok Bot can now handle banking while your Tesla FSD handles the road Elon Musk says Grok Bot can manage your finances through linked bank and investment accounts. Grok Bot now wants access to your wallet, with SpaceXAI rolling out a new Finance integration for its agent platform that lets users link bank, credit card and investment accounts thereby letting their Bots help manage spending, investments and more. Elon Musk amplified the announcement on X with a short endorsement, “Grok Bot can manage your finances.” The feature builds on two earlier steps. In early September, Grok gained the ability to answer questions about spending, savings, investments and cash flow using accounts connected through Plaid, starting with users in the U.S. Before that, on August 28, SpaceXAI let Grok Bot buy things online through Link, with users approving every spend request and the Bot receiving a single use card for each payment. Musk has already shown how far he wants users to push it. In late August, when Tesla investor account Teslaconomics said he was weighing whether to give Grok Bot access to his bank accounts, Musk replied, “Try it out. If Grok Bot messes up, we will make you whole.” That promise goes beyond SpaceXAI’s consumer terms, which make users responsible for what their agents do and generally cap the company’s liability at the greater of fees paid or $100. SpaceXAI’s own documentation recommends requiring approval for purchases and financial transfers. For Tesla owners, the update lands five days after Tesla brought Grok Bot into its vehicles, letting drivers hand off errands by voice while FSD (Supervised) handles the road. Bot access inside the car is currently limited to SuperGrok Heavy subscribers, though Connectors are open to anyone signed into Grok. With Finance linked, a driver could ask for a spending summary or a check on upcoming bills during the commute. Grok’s role in the car has grown quickly since Tesla’s Summer Update let it control cabin features by voice. We have been using Grok Bot in our own Tesla for several weeks, and here’s how our latest test went. Elon Musk SpaceX just got the green light Starship has waited years for The FAA has cleared Starship Flight 14, setting up SpaceX’s first orbital attempt on Monday. SpaceX has cleared the last regulatory hurdle standing between Starship and its first trip to orbit. The Federal Aviation Administration issued the launch license for Starship Flight 14 late Saturday, keeping the mission on track for liftoff Monday, September 28, from Pad 2 at Starbase, Texas. The 75 minute launch window opens at 7:15 a.m. Central, and Boca Chica Beach closures are also scheduled for September 29 and 30 as backup dates. This will be Starship’s first revenue generating mission. The license was the missing piece after SpaceX completed a full wet dress rehearsal with Booster 21 and Ship 41 on September 24. At the time, the company said the flight remained on track pending regulatory approval. Because Flight 14 flies an orbital profile, the FAA had to sign off on a modified license that met its safety, payload and financial responsibility requirements. Observers combing through the new FAA paperwork also noticed that lightning no longer appears among Starship’s listed launch hazards. If that holds, it matters more for where Starship is headed than for Monday’s attempt. Florida and Louisiana, home to LC-39A and the planned Starbase Louisiana site, see some of the most frequent lightning in the United States. SpaceX tells the FCC that Starship Flight 14 is going to orbit Flight 14 is the mission SpaceX has been building toward for months. Ship 41 will carry 26 Starlink V3 satellites, the first operational V3 units to be deployed, and attempt roughly six orbits at about 275 kilometers over a flight lasting just under 10 hours. SpaceX says the ship will only perform its orbital insertion burn after flight controllers confirm enough hardware redundancy remains for the deorbit burn at the end of the mission. Ship 41 is targeting a splashdown in the Pacific west of Chile, while Super Heavy will return to the Gulf of Mexico. The date carries some symbolism as well. A Monday launch would come 10 years and one day after Elon Musk first presented the Interplanetary Transport System, the design that became Starship, at the International Astronautical Congress in Guadalajara, Mexico. SpaceX has not announced what comes next, but air traffic planning slides reported this week, list Flight 15 no earlier than October 19 and a first Starship launch from LC-39A in Florida no earlier than October 30. Both dates depend on how Monday goes. SpaceX launched another classified mission for the U.S. Space Force from California early Saturday morning, and the Falcon 9 booster that carried it landed on a drone ship in the Pacific for the tenth time. The USSF-385 mission lifted off from Space Launch Complex 4E at Vande
